articleTitle: Power control and experiment of 2MW/10kV cascaded H-bridge power conversion system for battery energy storage system
abstract: Renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic and wind turbine power generators may make the power grid unstable because of their output fluctuations. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are being considered as a countermeasure for this issue. Cascaded H-bridge (CHB) is expected as a promising topology for large capacity BESSs because the state of charge (SOC) of battery clusters can be controlled independently by H-bridge power units, and the harmonic current of the system is low enough to remove the ac filter. This paper describes the development of the Y-connection CHB-BESS and a power control strategy for the BESS. A real-scale 2MW/10kV CHB-BESS was constructed in Shenzhen, China and its successful operation verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method. Based on the system, the power control strategy was verified by three parts of the experiment, which are decoupling power control test, emergency shutdown test and step response test. The results indicate that the system can realize decoupling control of active and reactive power effectively, achieve step response at the millisecond level and make full-load shutdown in an emergency state at the microsecond level.

articleTitle: A statistical learning framework for the intelligent imputation of offshore wind farm missing SCADA data
abstract: The Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system collects operational data of wind turbines in a wind farm and monitors operational conditions of them. Yet, the SCADA system is often affected by various factors, such as the sensor failure and network congestion, resulting in the data loss. In this paper, a statistical learning framework is developed to intelligently impute the SCADA missing data of an offshore wind farm, which is of a high dimension and a long time span. The framework mainly consists of three parts: (1) the data pre-processing based on correlation analysis; (2) the model training and verification based on a novel integration of the feature selection, candidate models, and virtual sensor principles; as well as (3) the missing data estimation and data post-processing. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and generality as well as the industrial application value of the developed statistical learning framework.

articleTitle: Finite control set model predictive control strategy of grid simulator for the test of renewable energy system and motor driver
abstract: In recent years, grid simulator based on two-level inverter is widely used in the grid integration testing for renewable energy system and motor driver. However, the traditional control strategy is difficult to achieve higher output voltage quality. This paper proposes a finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) based strategy for grid simulator. Compared with the traditional control strategy which is based on the linear control algorithm, the proposed algorithm eliminates the process of rotation coordinate transformation and avoids the coupling conditions in the current control loop. With the analysis of LC filter, the current prediction equations are obtained, and the cost function is also designed. Simulation test on a two-level grid simulator is carried out with the output voltage reference containing power quality disturbances like harmonics, voltage sag and voltage swell. Simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm can improve the voltage response speed and simplify the process of parameter adjustment, and it has good application foreground in the grid simulator for the test of renewable energy system and motor driver.

articleTitle: Understanding the nonlinear behaviour and synchronizing stability of a grid-tied VSC under grid voltage sags
abstract: Transients of a typical grid synchronizing VSC are closely associated with the over-current and over-voltage in circuits. Previous analysis in evaluating such transient phenomenon usually ignore the nonlinear control effects of the VSCs (e.g. phase-locked-loop, PLL). Although this assumption allows a simpler analysis of the transient process, it may overlook potential stability issues on which the nonlinear controls may a great impact and the consequence of which is easily confused with the passive circuit transients. Therefore, this work aims to achieve a good understanding of the nonlinear control dynamics of the VSC and their impacts on the stability provoked by the grid voltage sags. To better reveal the mechanisms, the power control loop (PCL) and the PLL-dominant dynamics are analysed separately with corresponding reduced-order nonlinear models. From which the grid synchronizing stability of the VSC is revealed, and a quantitative study of stability margin is presented through the calculation and evaluation of the critical clearing time (CCT). Based on this, CCT under various PLL bandwidths are evaluated, the results of which could facilitate the parameter design of PLL from a stability viewpoint. All the analyses are verified by time-domain simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Analysis of impact of grounding-pole current-limiting reactor on fault detection of MMC based DC grids
abstract: The Zhangbei ±500kV DC pilot project is the world's first modular multilevel converter based DC grid project, which integrates large scale wind power over long distance using the overhead lines. Once DC fault occurs on the overhead line, fault currents rise rapidly with a large amplitude, which requires fast trip of DCCBs to isolate faulted lines. To suppress the fault current rise rate and leave more time for fault detection, the current-limiting reactors (CLR) are implemented on both polar and grounding poles in the Zhangbei project. This paper analyses the impacts of grounding pole (G-CLR) on the DC line protection and the fault characteristics of the voltage across G-CLRs under bus faults. In addition, a DC bus protection scheme using G-CLRs is proposed. In order to verify the correctness of analysis and effectiveness of the proposed scheme, extensive simulations have been conducted under PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Emergency control strategy of PV for suppressing transient overvoltage peak in LCC-HVDC infeed power system
abstract: The transient overvoltage appears commonly in LCC-HVDC infeed power system and could lead to tripping of adjacent PV and cascading failures, especially in the peak stage. The current solutions mainly focus on improving short circuit capacity and the response of reactive power compensation devices. However, these solutions need extra devices or could not response rapidly to the voltage peak. Thus, this paper proposes an additional emergency control strategy of PV to suppress overvoltage peak, which utilizes PV's rapid adjustment capacity. The topology of a practical system and controls of key devices are introduced first. Then, the process of transient recovery overvoltage peak is analysed. Further, an emergency control strategy is proposed. An additional signal, which is formed by the error between terminal voltage measurement and its reference, is attached to the output voltage reference of PV to provide emergency reactive power support. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy are validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparison of power quality and inter-phase circulation for one-stage and two-stage modular battery energy storage system
abstract: There are one-stage and two-stage topologies for battery energy storage systems, one-stage system offers higher efficiency, and two-stage system can make better use of battery capacity. For CHB-BESS (Cascaded H-Bridge Battery Energy Storage System) and MMC-BESS (Modular Multilevel Converter Battery Energy Storage System), the two-stage topology also decreases the second-harmonic current through the battery, which is inherent in the topology and is thought to have a potential impact on the battery. Then two-stage MMC-BESS with bidirectional dc-dc converters is proposed. However, the second-harmonic current is absorbed by the dc capacitor of the dc-dc converter, which brings negative effects to output current. The phenomenon is more obvious when the number of submodules is small. Moreover, the second-harmonic fluctuation of dc capacitor voltage is coupled to the circulation, making it difficult to control. One-stage CHB-BESS and MMC-BESS avoid these problems. This paper analyses and compares the power quality of one-stage and two-stage MMC-BESS system. Mathematical models for both topologies are built, the theoretical results show that one-stage topology performs better with respect to ac output voltage, ac output current and inter-phase circulation. Finally, a simulation model on Simulink platform is established, the simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Research on system conditions of a 500kV novel fault current limiter based on high coupled split reactor
abstract: To solve the problem of excessive short-circuit current with the development of 500kV power grid, also the voltage drop and power loss caused by typical current limiting reactor, a novel fault current limiter, which combines highly coupled split reactor (HCSR) and paralleled circuit breakers, has drawn intense attention due to its superior properties of trigger-free, high current limiting ability and low normal operation loss. This paper mainly focuses on system working conditions of the novel fault current limiter in Guangdong Power Grid from the perspective of system analysis. For this, an electromagnetic transient model of 500kV fault current limiter with HCSR is built in EMTP, the key technical requirements such as electrical parameters, operating voltage, overvoltage level are clarified, the transient recovery voltage (TRV) of breakers are analysed. The results show that the TRV peak and the rate of rise of TRV are much higher than the allowable values of the circuit breaker test in the current standard. Suppression measures, such as installation of opening resistors or capacitances in parallel with circuit breakers, are proposed at last. Conclusions obtained in this paper can be used to guide the production and manufacture of 500kV fault current limiter.

articleTitle: The impedance modelling of MMC for oscillation analysis considering control dynamics and delays
abstract: The oscillation phenomena in the Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) based HVDC system has caused severe damage to the related devices and grids. The fundamental causes of the oscillations can be very sophisticated depending on the configuration and control operation of the system. Therefore, an impedance model of the MMC was proposed while considering the dynamic characteristic of each control loop and the overall signal delays in the control scheme. The results have shown that, the current inner loop, active power control loop and the overall signal delays have great impacts on the impedance characteristics of the converter. The impacts of the control loops and the delay times have been demonstrated by deriving the impedance model of the MMC and compared to the measured impedance curve, which was obtained by frequency scanning method. The consistence between these two curves have proven the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed impedance model.

articleTitle: Economic technical analysis of low frequency transmission system under scene of renewable energy integration into grid
abstract: High-voltage AC system, high-voltage DC system and low frequency transmission system are the three methods widely used for renewable energy integration. This paper introduces the topology structure of low frequency transmission in renewable energy integration. The technical and economic advantages and disadvantages of three integration methods are discussed with Dachen Island Star Wind Farm as the background. The results show that the low frequency transmission system meets the integration requirements of the example and has the best economy. It further shows the application potential of low frequency transmission in the renewable energy integration scenario.

articleTitle: Optimal power flow for AC and DC grids based on power electronic transformer
abstract: The development of power electronics technology and the application of DC source and DC load promote the transformation of AC grid to AC and DC grids. The optimal power flow (OPF) of the traditional AC grid can determine the safe and economic operation state of the grid. The existence of the nonlinear power flow equation makes OPF a nonlinear and non-convex optimization problem. In the AC and DC grids with power electronic transformer (PET), the operational constraints of PET further increase the non-convexity. This paper will focus on addressing the non-convexity of OPF in AC and DC grids. The objective function of OPF in AC and DC grids is to minimize the generation cost or the system losses. The constraints include node power balance constraints, voltage amplitude constraints, line capacity constraints, and operational constraints of PET. The convex relaxation technique is used to transform OPF into a semi-definite programming(SDP) problem, and the sufficient conditions for the zero relaxation gap are derived to obtain the global optimal solution. The simulation on the extended IEEE33 test system with PET proves that the global optimal solution can be obtained.

articleTitle: Phase angle compensation of virtual impedance for resonance mitigation in DFIG system under weak grid
abstract: Subsynchronous resonance (SSR) and high-frequency resonance (HFR) occurs due to the impedance interaction between the DFIG system and series compensated and parallel compensated weak grid, respectively. Virtual impedance is the traditional technique of resonance mitigation in grid-connected applications. To cope with the problem that the control delay would lead to the failure of virtual impedance, this paper inaugurates the impedance model of the DFIG system in weak grid considering the control delay. Then the resonance phenomenon is revealed for the DFIG system. It is shown that traditional virtual impedance fails to mitigate resonance due to negative damping at high frequencies. The phase shift initiated by control delay is scrutinized quantitatively, and to restore positive damping characteristics, the virtual impedance is reshaped with the phase angle compensation. Thus, more efficient resonance mitigation can be achieved by the impedance reshaping. Then the stability of the proposed method is analyzed, and the range of virtual impedance is determined. Finally, simulations in MATLAB based on a 2 MW DFIG system verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The preemptive virtual impedance based fault current limiting control for MMC-HVDC
abstract: The dc- and ac-side short-circuit faults of the HVDC system bring large over currents in the phase arms of the Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC), and may interrupt the continuous operation of the HVDC system due to valve blocking. This paper proposes a preemptive control approach, which employs the virtual impedance technique to suppress the fault currents in the arms. This is realized by mapping the characteristics of the ac and dc output impedance of MMC to the classical double-loop d- and q-axis controllers. Two indices in both time-averaged and transient manners are proposed to evaluate the control effect of the proposed schemes. Time-domain simulations on PSCAD/EMTDC have shown that the additional control blocks can reduce the overcurrent levels and ensure a faster system recovery from temporary short-circuit faults.

articleTitle: Double-sided ring topology for offshore wind fram collector system layout: A multi-cable application
abstract: Owing to the benefit of high reliability, the double-sided ring topology has been widely applied in the collector system layout for large-scale offshore wind farms (OWF). However, such design also shows the drawback in economic efficiency as the ring topology requires longer cable distances compared with other designs, such as the radial topology. This paper introduces the multi-cable application for the double-sided ring topology, which achieves improved economic efficiency with the consideration of both cable and power loss costs. It begins with the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to locate the substation with smallest distances to wind turbines. This is followed by the modified Two-Phase Clark and Wright's saving algorithm to divide and connect turbine clusters using cables with various current ratings, and the optimal solution is selected among different cluster sizes. The proposed multi-cable design is tested and compared with traditional double-sided ring topology and the results verify that using cables with various ratings enhances the economic efficiency of collector system planning.

Author Keywords: two-phase Clark and Wright saving algorithm

articleTitle: A predictive control method for suppressing the continuous commutation failure of LCC-based HVDC systems
abstract: Unreasonable selection of control parameters of voltage dependent current order limiter (VDCOL) in the DC system may lead to further deterioration in recovery characteristics, causing continuous commutation failure. Firstly, by analyzing the relationship between VDCOL recovery slope, the AC bus voltage and the extinction angle, a method for changing the slope of VDCOL characteristic curve according to the AC bus voltage during faults is proposed. When the commutation failure occurs at DC grid, the VDCOL immediately sets the characteristic curve slope during system recovery according to the real-time measured commutation voltage and critical extinction angle value. This method can reduce the reactive power consumed by the converter which benefits to suppress the continuous commutation failure of the DC system to a certain extent. Finally, the CIGRE HVDC standard test model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC, and the effectiveness of the proposed recovery strategy in suppressing subsequent commutation failure and improving system recovery characteristics is verified. This method makes full use of HVDC system controller and does a great significance to improve the recovery performance of HVDC.

articleTitle: Study on equivalence of MMC modeling under multi-dq frames and harmonic state space
abstract: The model of modular multilevel converter (MMC) has attracted extensive research efforts in the last few years to analyze stability or to design controllers. Multi-dq frames and harmonic state space (HSS) are two major modeling methods to address the time-variance of MMC caused by the complex internal frequency coupling. However, no details are presented on essential relation of these two methods. In this paper, the mathematical essence and equivalence of the MMC model in multi-dq frames and in HSS are revealed by using Fourier series. On this basis, the transformation matrix connecting two types of models is developed, which increases flexibility in MMC modeling process. Finally, correctness of the theory and transformation matrix are verified by experimental and simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimal scheduling method for regional photovoltaic-storage-charging integrated system participating in demand response
abstract: With the development of photovoltaic power generation and the popularity of electric vehicles, the integrated system of regional photovoltaic-storage-charging emerges as the times require. In this paper, the optimal scheduling problem in the operation of photovoltaic-storage-charging integrated system under the condition of grid connection is studied. This paper introduces the structure, basic composition unit and operation strategy of optical storage and charge integrated system under time-sharing electricity price. Considering the demand response of the charging load of the electric vehicle and the basic electric load of the village area, the transferable load of the peak and trough of the electricity price is determined. A two-objective optimization model is established to reduce the load peak and valley difference and improve the economy of the integrated optical storage and charging system, and the NSGA-II algorithm is used to solve it. Finally, an example is given to prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Frequency enhancement of grid-forming inverters under low-SCR weak grid
abstract: Investigating frequency issues of voltage source inverters (VSIs) integrating into weak grid, a quasi-virtual synchronous generator (VSG) droop controller is proposed in this paper. The review of traditional active power droop control and VSG given in the paper reveals drawbacks of these methodologies, especially with respect to microgrid application. Motivated by the limitations, the proposed controller is designed to be capable of providing virtual inertia in support of frequency response, buffering frequency violations upon disturbances and synchronising to the grid without engagement of phase locked loop. Furthermore, considering about system strength, as this has been a critical barrier preventing renewable energy from further penetration, characteristics of weak grid are analysed as preliminary in this paper. And then criterion of the controller connecting to weak grid will be introduced based multi-input multiple-output (MIMO) Nyquist theorem. Complex transfer functions for the proposed controller are developed to understand frequency-coupling issues in inverter-weak grid integrated system, which will reinforce feasibility of the controller in frequency domain. A single machine infinite bus (SMIB) model built in PSCAD/EMTDC software is adopted as a specific case to validate the control strategy in time domain.

articleTitle: An overview on wind farm modelling for power system stability studies
abstract: With the continuous increase of wind power penetration level in power systems, impacts of wind farm consisting of plentiful wind turbines on the stability of the power system become significant. To investigate the impacts by means of analytical analysis or numerical simulation, appropriate wind farm models should be provided in advance. In the past two decades, great efforts have been made on wind farm modelling and validations, and also significant development have been achieved. However, it still lacks a clear understanding on the thought pattern and technical way of wind farm modelling specifically for various types of stability studies. Besides, technical bottlenecks and potential development trends in wind farm dynamic equivalent modelling are also unclear. To further clarify the current status of wind farm modelling research and promote the progress of generic modelling, this paper makes a comprehensive overview on wind farm modelling used in power system stability studies, in terms of the following four aspects 1) modelling purposes, 2) model classification, 3) modelling techniques, and 4) model validations. Finally, unsolved issues and future trends of wind farm modelling are summarized.

articleTitle: The real-time optimization of active distribution system based on deep deterministic policy gradient
abstract: A real-time optimal control strategy of active distribution network (ADN) based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) is proposed in this paper. The proposed control strategy can continuously update the network's parameters based on the gradient descent method, according to the operation information of ADN and then directly get the optimal strategy with high return value. The goal of return function is to minimize the total node-voltage deviation, line loss of distribution network, the regulation of microgrid (MG) and the power fluctuation of tie-line. The optimization model can improve the operation performance of the ADN and reduce the impact on MGs. Finally, the effectiveness of the real-time optimization of ADN based on DDPG is proved by an improved IEEE 13-node case-study.

articleTitle: Multi-terminal hybrid UHVDC line protection scheme
abstract: The hybrid ultra-high voltage direct current (UHVDC) system is composed by line commutated converter (LCC) and voltage source converter (VSC). And the multi-terminal hybrid UHVDC system which can provide a larger capacity, more economical and more flexible transmission mode, is a development trend of HVDC technology. The system proposed in this paper adopts VSC converters with the characteristics of DC fault self-clearing and high speed switch (HSS). The DC line protection scheme of multi-terminal hybrid UHVDC system is investigated. First, the configuration scheme of DC line protection and and coordination strategy are proposed. Then, aiming at the key problem of line fault isolation in this multi-terminal system, the fault line selection method is proposed. Finally, based on PSCAD/EMTDC simulation, the feasibility of the proposed fault line selection method is verified.

articleTitle: The operating environment substitution-based field test technology of UHVDC protection system: Part 2 software environment substitution and field application
abstract: In order to implement the field test of functions and performance of the UHVDC protection system, the software environment substitution of the tested UHVDC protection is also much necessary, besides that the hardware environment substitution of the UHVDC protection system is realized by the various hardware interfaces of the field test device. Based on that, the key technologies, such as replaying of fault record data, manual test function, and synchronization of distributed multi field test devices are developed in this paper, which make the outputs of the field test device of the UHVDC protection system can simulate the real operating condition of the UHVDC transmission project and consequently test the logic of the UHVDC protection functions credibly. Moreover, in order to validate the effectiveness of the proposed operating environment substitution-based field test scheme of UHVDC protection system, the field application is carried out.

articleTitle: Impact mechanism of turbine control of DFIG-based wind turbines on damping of power system oscillations
abstract: The penetration of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind turbines (WTs) is suspected to have some impacts on power system oscillations. In order to find out the relationships, several models have been established in previous studies. However, those models mostly overlooked the influences of the turbine control of WTs, including maximum power point tracking (MPPT), pitch control, and speed control. This paper proposes a new DFIG-based WT model, which enables further research on the impact rules and mechanisms of turbine control on the damping of power system oscillations. In detail, a linearized WT model, which can explicitly describe the external characteristics of WTs, is first derived. With the aid of this model, the differences introduced by the MPPT and the pitch compensation under different operation areas are compared. Finally, the impact rules and mechanisms of DFIG-based WT on power system oscillations are clearly explained through the interaction analysis based on the proposed model and the model of synchronous generators (SGs).

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of soft open points in distribution networks based on candidate location opitimization
abstract: More and more distributed renewable energy generation (REG) integrations have brought challenges to the secure operation of tradition distribution networks. As a new power electronic-based device, soft open point (SOP) can play an important role in flexible power and voltage regulation for distribution systems. As a fully controlled power electronic device, the investment and operation maintenance costs of SOP are still high, and the optimal allocation of SOPs can increase grid revenue. This paper presents an optimization method for SOP allocation to promote the integration of renewable energy generation. In order to find proper SOP candidate locations, a selection strategy is proposed based on two technical indexes, including power flow betweeness index (PFBI) and voltage violation risk index (VVRI). Considering multiple operation scenarios, a mathematic programming model of SOP allocation is formulated to minimize the total cost of SOP investment and network operation cost. Mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) method is adopted to solve the problem. Simulation results on the IEEE 33 bus system show that the candidate location selection strategy can effectively find the SOP planning scheme with lower cost.

articleTitle: Sequence impedance modeling of droop-controlled inverter
abstract: The grid-connected three-phase inverter is an indispensable part of the microgrid. The droop control is widely used in parallel inverters for high reliability and flexibility. The output impedance of droop controlled inverters plays an vital role in its stability. However, the sequence impedance model of grid-connected inverter is currently based on the grid side converter with a single current loop control exdluding the low-frequency dynamics similar in doubly fed induction generators. Both the droop control and voltage loop control greatly affect the stability of inverter, specifically in the low frequency response. This paper proposes a sequence impedance model of inverter, which considers the droop control and voltage and current dual closed-loop control using the harmonic linearization method in the frequency domain. The accuracy of the model is verified through comparing the measurement impedance value in simulation with the impedance value calculated in the sequence impedance model. The influence of control method on system impedance is verified by showing the difference between the single loop controlled inverter and droop control inverter.

articleTitle: Interoperability assessment of MMC and DRU connected offshore windfarms in meshed multi-terminal DC grids
abstract: In the last decade, a number of academic and industry studies have identified diode rectifier unit (DRU) as a potential replacement for offshore modular multilevel converter (MMC) of DC connected offshore windfarms. However, side-by-side operation of DRU and MMC connected windfarms in multi-terminal DC grid will present new operational challenges. Therefore, this paper will study the interoperability of a minimum meshed DC grid, which includes MMC and DRU connected offshore windfarms. To identify any potential issues that may arise from introduction of DRU, the system performance during onshore AC faults are simulated using PSCAD models. Simulation results show that the DRU connected windfarm exhibits different behaviours with the MMC based equivalent, but does not adversely impact the DC grid performance. Instead, the use of DRU improves DC grid performance with its inherent sensitivity of active power transmission to DC voltage variation.

articleTitle: High resistance grounding fault feeder detection in a resonant grounding system based on transient current correlation coefficient comparison
abstract: Because the fault characteristics is not obvious, the high resistance grounding fault feeder selection in a resonant grounding system has always been a hot and difficult problem in the field of power system protection. To solve this problem, the expressions of the transient zero sequence current of each feeder under over-damping and under-damping conditions are obtained based on the transient equivalent circuit of high resistance grounding fault in a resonant grounding system. The correlation degree of the transient zero sequence current between any two feeders is analysed by using the correlation coefficient method, so as to realize the fault feeder selection for high resistance grounding fault. Simulation results of PSCAD software show that this method is not affected by transition resistance, initial phase angle of fault, and has high accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Research on startup circuit parameter selection and startup control strategy for multi-terminal VSC HVDC system
abstract: The startup of multi-terminal VSC HVDC system is not only one of the key conditions to be considered in the system design, but also the basis for the system to operate normally. In this paper, the detailed theoretical analysis and simulation calculations are carried out for each stage of the charging process of VSC. Furthermore, the parameter selection principle and technical requirements of start-up resistor and netural grounding resistor of each station are proposed. Smooth start-up control strategy is designed to reduce equipment cost and communication dependence between stations. The proposed parameter selection principles and control strategy of start-up circuit have been verified by Nan'ao VSC-MTDC project.

articleTitle: Operation area calculation and parameter analysis of virtual synchronous machine
abstract: A complete scheme is proposed for the design of the parameters of the virtual synchronous generator. The mathematical model of the virtual synchronous generator is established. The selection range of the parameters is restrained for the active power loop from the stability, the stability margin and the overshoot. For the reactive power loop, the range of parameter selection is restrained from the stability, the cut-off frequency of low-pass filter. Considering with the corresponding standards about power grid, the selection range of parameters can be further narrowed. Finally, the range of parameters selection can be obtained which takes steady-state and dynamics performances into consideration. The influence of parameters changing on steady-state and dynamics performances has been analyzed by using of Bode diagram and zero-pole map, et al. The simulation carried out in PSCAD/EMTDC proves the feasibility of the method proposed in this paper. The method proposed in this paper can be used to design the controller parameters using the virtual synchronous generator algorithm. The conclusions obtained can be used in practical engineering and experiment to adjust parameters according to the performance.

articleTitle: An extended Kalman filtering based time-varying fundamental and subsynchronous frequency tracker
abstract: The oscillation caused by subsynchronous control interaction pose serious threat to the large-scale grid interfaced wind farms. The magnitude and frequency of the oscillation vary with the variation of system operating conditions, such as the total number of online wind turbine generators, wind speed, wind turbine converter control structures and their parameters, degree of series compensation and strength of the AC grid. Such time-varying subsynchronous oscillation must be monitored to maintain the system's stability. However, the simultaneous tracking of time-varying fundamental and subsynchronous phasors is a challenging task. This paper explores the capability of extended Kalman filter for joint tracking of the time varying fundamental and subsynchronous frequency phasors. The proposed tracking algorithm is first verified on computer generated test signals, and then on a reduced simulation model reflecting an actual event system facing subsynchronous oscillation. The results show that extended Kalman filtering, with adaptive noise covariance matrix, can accurately and efficiently estimate the time-varying subsynchronous phasors.

articleTitle: Short-term photovoltaic power forecasting method based on K-means algorithm and spiking neural networks
abstract: In view of the adverse impacts on the power grid dispatching, energy management and other aspects caused by the volatility, intermittence and uncertainty of photovoltaic (PV) power generation, this paper proposes a novel short-term PV power forecasting method based on K-means algorithm and spiking neural networks (SNN). Considering meteorological factors and seasonal characteristics, this approach utilizes the K-means algorithm to cluster different short-term PV power generation characteristics and implements SNN training with different kinds of PV power generation data obtained from clustering results. In addition, an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to globally optimize the synaptic weights of SNN, which enhances the pattern recognition ability and numerical stability of the forecasting model. We assess the performance of the proposed method by using actual PV power generation data in a certain area for simulation analysis. The simulation results illustrate that the proposed method can achieve a better prediction accuracy than the conventional BP neural network and support vector machine (SVM), and performs excellent engineering application potential.

articleTitle: Power system dynamic economic dispatch with multi-type renewable energy
abstract: This paper reports a dynamic economic dispatch approach for the power system with multi-type renewable energies. The renewable energy sources considered in the paper are wind, PV and hydro power, which are configured as a virtual power plant (VPP) according to their complementarities. To evaluate the ability of VPP power output tracking the load demand curve, three indices, that is, the fluctuation rate, the standard deviation, and the changing rate of the fluctuation of the VPP power output are proposed. Accordingly, a comprehensive performance index is defined to combine three individual indices with different weighting factors. A dynamic economic dispatch model for power system with multi type renewable energies is set up, which considers the complementarities of multi-type energy, as well as the optimization of VPP power output. The firefly algorithm and an improved particle swarm optimization are applied to solve the proposed model. A practical power system with multi type renewable energy sources, which is a real provincial integrated energy system in Southeast China, is used for simulation. The results and analysis are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Research on optimization configuration of M-SMES in micro-grid with renewable energy
abstract: Superconducting magnetic energy storage system (SMES) has a broad application prospect in micro-grid due to its fast response ability and high energy storage density. Because of the limitation of superconducting material development level, the capacity of a single SMES can hardly meet the energy storage demand at present, so the energy storage of the power system needs a distributed layout. Modular superconducting magnetic energy storage system (M-SMES) can effectively improve the utilization and economy of SMES by rationally configuring its capacity and planning its layout. For the typical micro-grid with renewable power generation, an optimization method for configuring capacity and planning location of M-SMES is proposed and verified by a case. Firstly, a multi-objective mathematical optimization model is established. Then the capacity and steady-state layout of M-SMES are optimized by Genetic Algorithm (GA), and the function of SMES is verified in transient analysis. Finally, a micro-grid with renewable power generation — three-generator and nine-bus system is taken as a case to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed M-SMES capacity and layout optimization scheme.

articleTitle: Evaluation of trans-regional UHVDC tieline power optimization in promoting renewable energy accommodation
abstract: With the trans-regional UHVDC transmission lines built and put into operation, the delivery capacity of the "Three North" regions has been increasing in China. However, the problem of wind power and photovoltaic power curtailment has not been fundamentally solved. Based on the actual situation of power grid operation, this paper studies the coordinated optimization of multiple trans-regional UHVDC transmission lines deliver power to promote renewable energy accommodation between multiple regions. Firstly, the distribution characteristics of renewable energy curtailment power in typical areas are analysed, and the complementarity of renewable energy generation power among different regions is studied. Secondly, an analytical model of renewable energy accommodation capacity considering trans­regional UHVDC transmission lines deliver power optimization is established. Then, the effects of trans-regional UHVDC transmission lines deliver power complementation to promote accommodation of renewable energy are measured for multiple regions. The case analysis results show that the proposed UHVDC transmission lines operation method can effectively improve the renewable energy accommodation capacity of the entire power system.

articleTitle: MTDC topological analysis and evaluation for high penetration of renewable energy
abstract: Multi-terminal direct current (MTDC) system is a promising approach to solve the problem brought by the high-penetration renewable energy in the grid. There exist three typical topologies of MTDC grids, namely serial, radical and ring type. This paper proposes a topological analysis and evaluation method for the MTDC system, considering its reliability, economy, and renewable energy consumption. In order to achieve the topological analysis and evaluation, the output of each node and the power flow are calculated based on the modified second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxation. This paper summarizes the characteristics and the scope of application of each topology from the topological analysis and evaluation in terms of reliability, economy, and renewable energy consumption. The case study based on a four-terminal MMC-HVDC system is carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed topological analysis and evaluation method.

articleTitle: Study on coordinated control strategy of offshore wind farm integration system via MMC-HVDC based on transient response characteristic analysis
abstract: With the offshore wind turbines getting larger and the offshore distance of the wind farm increasing, the offshore wind farm integration via MMC-HVDC technology has become one of the current mainstream solutions. This paper discusses the transient characteristics of offshore wind farm integration system via MMC-HVDC and a coordinated control strategy between the offshore wind farm and the converter station in response to grid fault is proposed to enhance the support of the system to the receiving end grid. In the strategy, the improved droop characteristics of frequency-DC voltage are introduced in the grid side VSC (GSVCS), meanwhile the droop characteristics of active power-DC voltage are introduced in the wind farm side VSC (WFVCS), so the offshore wind farm can participate in the frequency adjustment of AC system. Finally, the model of offshore wind farm integration system in PSCAD/EMTDC platform is realized, and the common conditions such as wind speed variations, sudden load change and AC line fault are analysed. The results verify the correctness and effectiveness of grid-connected system and coordinated control strategy.

articleTitle: A system state modelling and ABC algorithm optimization for CCHP and smart building
abstract: Combined cooling, power and heat (CCHP) technics are widely used in district energy utilization. The domestic application of high energy efficiency buildings, regarded as smart buildings, rely on CCHP technics to improve overall performance. Dynamic process optimization is used to improve systems with its consumer comfort, carbon footprint, cost effectiveness and resilience. In this paper, a passive building module is proposed as a load for inserting CCHP generation, and an artificial bee colony is selected to analyze the performance of the proposed module. The module is divided into centralized generation and decentralized generation topologies, and a contrast analysis is also proposed. Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is used to solve problems with both state variables and decision variables existing simultaneously. The study shows that the proposed method can well reproduce the strategy and reveal the performance of the standard of smart buildings. Each characteristic of the smart building strategy is given in this passage.

articleTitle: Anomaly detection for power system forecasting under data corruption based on variational auto-encoder
abstract: With the expansion of information technology in the era of smart grid, cybersecurity vulnerability issues are becoming a major threat for the modern power system. Among various results of cyberattacks, data corruption may lead to poor forecasting performance in the power system issues. To tackle this problem, this paper introduces an anomaly detection method for power system forecasting based on variational auto-encoder. This reconstruction-based anomaly detection method adaptively discovers the potential common patterns of data series and find the anomalies different from common patterns. Taking load forecasting as example, the numerical results of case studies on the dataset of Global Energy Forecasting Competition 2014 demonstrate the outstanding effectiveness of proposed method over other competing methods.

articleTitle: The influence of phase-locked loop on the impedance of single phase voltage source converter
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing capacity of renewable energy, the sub-super synchronous oscillation caused by the interaction between power electronic devices such as Voltage Source Converter (VSC) and weak grid reduces the stability of the system. This paper proposes VSC impedance model with two kinds of Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) and compares the influence of PLL on VSC impedance using stability criterion. First, the dynamics of T/4 delay PLL and Second Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI) PLL are analysed and the VSC impedance models based on harmonic linearization considering the two PLLs are established respectively. It shows that with the same control parameters VSC impedance between the two PLLs is different in sub-super synchronous frequency. Stability of VSC considering the two PLLs in weak grid is analysed by applying the impedance-based stability criterion. The results indicate that in the same bandwidth VSC with SOGI-PLL leads system to become stable. The correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of oscillation suppression are verified by models built in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Charging schedule optimization of electric bus charging station considering departure timetable
abstract: This paper investigates a charging schedule optimization problem of electric bus charging station. From the prospect of optimal schedule of electric buses, the demand response potential of electric buses is analysed and a simulation method of electric buses is proposed. According to the generated rechargeable time intervals, a demand response model of electric bus charging station is established. After that, a charging schedule optimization model of electric bus charging station which embedded in proposed demand response model of electric bus station is built to minimize the charging cost. Finally, proposed method is verified through case study. The results show that the proposed method is valid and is able to provide strong support for operation and demand response potential ability analysis of one electric bus route.

articleTitle: Study on the impact of renewable portfolio standard on Ningxia renewable energy consumption based on system dynamics
abstract: In order to further improve the consumption of renewable energy sources (RES) and promote the participation of RES in market trading, the implementation of the renewable portfolio standard (RPS) is an inevitable choice in the future. Based on Ningxia, China, this paper analyses the reasons for the lack of motivation of RES participation in the market according to the current situation of market trading. Combined with the development of RPS and tradable green certificates (TGC), the system dynamics (SD) is used to analyse the impact of the implementation of RPS and TGC on Ningxia RES consumption. The results show that the RPS and the TGC can promote the consumption of RES, which provides a scientific and powerful proof for the advantages of implementation of RPS and TGC policy in Ningxia.

articleTitle: Research on island operation of small scale hydro powered network with back-to-back MMC-HVDC
abstract: With the rapid development of China's power grid, a great progress has been made in MMC-HVDC application. The MMC-HVDC has the advantages of decoupled control of active and reactive power, which provides significant potential in asynchronous network connection, small network island operation, etc. Based on potential scope of MMC-HVDC project, island operation is an inevitable situation. The ability of HVDC to operate and maintain island system stable can help improving the power supply quality and reduce the loss of load probability. But the voltage stability, and most of all, the frequency stability plays important roles during island operation. This article is inspired by Chongqing-Hubei back to back MMC-HVDC project. Firstly an objective function of minimum generators combination requirement was proposed. Secondly an equivalent network with large number of runoff hydro generators was modelled. Finally the correlation of the power flow through the tie-line and the commission level of generators in island network was analysed, and the system safety and stability control measurement suggestions were provided.

articleTitle: Analysis on capacitance rise of 500kV XLPE submarine cable in AC voltage withstand test
abstract: In Zhoushan transmission project, 500k V XLPE submarine cable lines are used for the first time in the world. In order to proofread the capacitance rise in AC voltage withstand tests of 500 kV XLPE submarine cable system, we established the models of simulation calculation with the PSCAD/EMTDC software based on this project, and calculated the voltage responses at certain position under different frequencies and sheath grounding modes for 17km submarine cables. The results show that when the test voltage of 493kV (1.7U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) is applied on the submarine cable, the terminal voltage of the 17km submarine cable core monotonously increases with the frequency(20Hz∼300Hz), and the different grounding methods of the sheath have no effect on the terminal voltage of the submarine cable core. The maximum capacitance is about 6% at 300Hz. The maximum value of the sheath distribution voltage increases with the increase of frequency, and the different grounding methods of the sheath have a large impact on the terminal voltage of the submarine cable sheath. The maximum sheath voltage is 5.38kV (300Hz) of grounding at head end, and the maximum sheath voltage is 1.19kV (300Hz) of grounding at both ends, and the maximum sheath voltage is 0.51kV (300Hz) of multiterminal grounding. The research can provide a necessary reference for ensuring the AC withstand voltage test to be implemented successfully and avoiding insulation damage of XLPE submarine cable.

articleTitle: Research and application of large-scale renewable energy control & monitoring system key technologies
abstract: In view of the development and management needs of renewable energy generation companies in China, this paper proposes a remote integrated monitoring construction scheme for renewable energy power plants. By building a renewable energy production information management platform with three levels integration, together with using the object-oriented modeling technology, distributed processing technology and renewable energy operation cockpit technology, this scheme can realize remote centralized monitoring of renewable energy power plants, as well as sharing of various production data. Through the intelligent analysis of the equipment, this scheme can greatly reduce the overall operation cost of the renewable energy power plants. The project practice proves that the scheme can take into account the management requirements of renewable power generation companies and Power Grid Corp, and realize unified access and integrated monitoring of all kinds of power generation equipment in renewable power plants, which greatly improves the economy and intelligence level.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a universal grid computing platform applicable to optimal operation of power grid
abstract: With the rapid development of the electric power industry, the demand for high performance computing is getting higher and higher. The advent and development of grid computing technology provides a strong guarantee in achieving highly efficient power grid simulations [1]. However, how to further improve the universality and usability of grid computing platform is always a difficult issue. This paper tries to design and construct a universal grid computing platform applicable to optimal operation of power grid with multi-task problem­solving features. The designed platform can flexibly organize and schedule various heterogeneous computing resources by constructing a management node. In particular, the platform can identify newly added computing nodes automatically by receiving http requests and seamlessly integrate them into schedulable computing resources. An intelligent decision­making strategy, named "make the best use of everything", is proposed to realize the automatic division of tasks and dynamic balance of load, and the automatic conversion of different data formats can be efficiently implemented through the function of type recognition. Finally, the designed grid computing platform programming in Python is applied to implement the distributed parallel computation of optimal power flow solved by different computational intelligence algorithms based on specific test systems.

articleTitle: Complementary and coordinated optimal dispatch solution for hybrid thermal-wind-PV power grid with energy storage
abstract: It is known that renewable energy sources like wind power and photovoltaic (PV) solar energy bear obvious inherent uncertainties. With the increasing penetration level of wind/PV generation, how to effectively stabilize the volatility of wind generation, reduce wind/PV curtailment, and improve the capability of wind/PV accommodation while satisfying load demand still requires in-depth research. In this paper, a solution of complementary and coordinated optimal dispatch for hybrid thermal-wind-PV power grid with energy storage is proposed, aiming at minimizing the total fuel cost of thermal power generation while meeting corresponding system operating constraints. The scenario-based analysis technique is employed to model the uncertainties of wind power and PV generation. Regarding the factors of improving wind/PV accommodation and avoiding dispatch thermal power units frequently, some complementary and coordinated dispatch strategies are elaborately designed and further introduced into the optimization model as constraint conditions. Owing to the highly nonlinear characteristic of the proposed model, the grey wolf optimization algorithm is applied to solve the problem. Finally, the validity and effectiveness of the proposed model and strategies are verified on the IEEE standard test systems.

articleTitle: Research on HVDC frequency limit control to improve frequency restoration in muti-HVDC asynchronous system
abstract: Yunnan power system is the first asynchronous operation system sending by multi-HVDC, which adopts multi-Frequency Limit Controllers (FLC) to control frequency of sending part. At the HVDC single-polar block experiment of Yunnan asynchronous system, the Frequency dynamic process of muti-HVDC asynchronous system was exposed: First, FLC absorbed most of the unbalanced power; and the Primary Frequency Control (PFC) of unit act to release the FLC adjustment; lastly, the system frequency reached at a steady-state value (depends on Speed-droop characteristic). In order to avoid long-term overload of frequency and HVDC, the impacts of FLC reserve arrangement, dead-band and parameters on Frequency dynamic process of muti-HVDC asynchronous system are studied, which conclude an optimized setting for FLC reserve arrangement, dead-band and parameters. The results of simulation and system operation show that the Frequency dynamic process of muti-HVDC asynchronous system were obviously improved after setting optimized.

articleTitle: Fault warning of pitch system of wind turbine based on kernel density estimation
abstract: The pitch system is one of the core components of the wind farm and plays an important role in the safe and stable operation of the wind turbine. This paper presents a study on the fault warning method for pitch system based on kernel density estimation(KDE). After the description of the structure, control principle and monitoring parameters of the wind turbine pitch system, the paper analyzes the correlation of the parameters of the pitch system using the SCADA(Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) data of a wind farm, and establishes a training model under normal working conditions of the pitch angle with the wind speed input, then obtains a confidence interval for the working under the normal operating condition of the pitch angle. Finally, the hypothesis test of Bernoulli binomial distribution is used to judge whether the current working state is abnormal and provide early warning. Through the case verification, the fault warning method of the pitch system based on the kernel density estimation can effectively and accurately predict the fault, which provides a new idea for the subsequent performance analysis of the wind turbine.

articleTitle: A new model of CCHP system with various new energy integration
abstract: The CHP(Combined Heating Power) system driven by fossil fuel is a factor that causes a large amount of new energy being abandoned, As a result, we need to model a new CCHP(Combined Cooling Heating Power) system with the integration of new energy. This paper presents a method to enhance the ability of load regulation by adding thermal storage and electric heater to the traditional CHP system. Firstly, the basic principle of this model is introduced. Then the output of photovoltaic cell and wind turbine before and after the configuration of the thermal storage and electric heater is analyzed. Based on the above analysis, a mathematical model is established to calculate the ability of load regulation before and after the configuration of the thermal storage and electric heater Simulation results show the ability of load regulation is enhanced after thermal storage and electric heater added in CCHP system.

articleTitle: Research on transient overvoltage of transmission lines combined with 500 kV XLPE submarine cable and overhead line
abstract: The first transmission lines combined with 500 kV XLPE submarine cable and overhead line in the world have been adopted in Zhoushan 500 kV power network project. Switching operation and short circuit faults of 500 kV XLPE submarine cable system will cause transient overvoltage. Based on the transmission lines combined with 500 kV XLPE submarine cable and overhead line, the simulation calculation model was established with the PSCAD/EMTDC software to simulate transient overvoltage under different closing and opening phases of the circuit breaker and various short circuit faults. And we studied the effect of circuit breaker closing resistance, parallel reactor, and arrester configuration on reducing the transient overvoltage of the line. The simulation result was compared with the measured oscillography data, which verified the effectiveness of transient overvoltage suppression measures for the transmission lines. It offers reference for the study on suppressing transient overvoltage of transmission lines and reducing failure rate of XLPE submarine cable.

articleTitle: Design of general framework for multi-fault diagnosis based on photovoltaic grid-connected inverter system
abstract: Since normal single fault diagnosis method cannot deal with multiple fault problems in the photovoltaic (PV) grid-connected inverter system, which will cause a serious accident. This paper proposes a general framework design for multi-fault diagnosis for the PV grid-connected inverter system. The framework mainly analyses the process of fault diagnosis of sudden faults in the inverter system based on the requirements of data volume and time which is fault detection, fault classification, fault location, and fault isolation. The scheme integrates the advantages of three kinds of fault diagnosis methods based on mathematical theory analysis, signal analysis and artificial intelligence, and introduces the technical direction and technical difficulties of each diagnostic process. Mathematical model analysis, wavelet packet decomposition, data mining, fuzzy logic, and artificial neural network are applied to each process of fault diagnosis, respectively. Thus, the scheme has the ability of logical thinking and empirical thinking. The simulation results prove that the scheme can diagnose multi-fault inverter systems in real time.

articleTitle: Study on the impact of communication network on reactive power control in wind farm
abstract: The performance of reactive power control system seriously affect the normal operation of wind farm. However, typical system architecture of reactive power control system usually contains several hierarchies and the communication network of the whole system is very complicated. So, the assessment of reactive power control system should take the communication network between these hierarchies in consideration inevitably. In this paper, instead of using a time delay to simulate the data transportation delay, a new method to model the network topology and data link layer is proposed. With this method, the communication network model, the reactive power control strategy as well as the wind farm model are all established in the same MATLAB/Simulink environment. Then the communication network performance such as end to end delay, node workload, communication protocol etc. can be evaluated and the influence of communication network to the reactive power control system can be analysed in one environment. In final, the effectiveness of this modelling method is validated by model simulation of the reactive power control system integrated with communication network.

articleTitle: Pilot protection scheme for pole-to-ground fault in DC distribution network
abstract: With the development of hybrid AC-DC system, DC distribution network attracts wide attention. Different grounding modes of converters in DC network have an important impact on fault characteristics of pole-to-ground fault. In this paper, fault characteristics of pole-to-ground fault with different grounding modes were discussed in detail and protection scheme was proposed correspondingly. When pole-to-ground fault occurs in DC network, unbalanced voltages and currents in two poles can be detected by protection devices. Hence, a directional element, defined as unbalanced power, was proposed to selectively recognize the fault direction. Furthermore, a pilot protection scheme based on unbalanced power was proposed, which collects information at two ends of the fault line and accurately distinguishes pole-to-ground fault from other conditions. Numerous simulation studies were carried out in PSCAD/EMTDC. The results validated the speedability, selectivity and reliability of proposed protection scheme, which also works effectively in high-resistance faults and is promising to be applied in DC distribution network.

articleTitle: Comparison of modulation and power control between modular multilevel converter based large scale battery energy storage system and MMC-HVDC
abstract: In recent years, Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) has been a significant candidate for medium and high-power conversion systems. Substantial research has been done on the operation and control of MMC based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) transmission systems. Lately, MMC based battery energy storage system (MMC-BESS) has been introduced with batteries integrated into the submodules. This paper provides a comparison between the MMC-HVDC and MMC-BESS structures with half-bridge submodule topology. It focuses on the dynamic performance of MMC-BESS and the special features of its modulation method, main circuit voltage level, connection inductor, and submodule voltage control. MMC-HVDC requires circulating current control, inrush current control and submodule voltage equalization while the MMC-BESS only requires state of charge (SOC) control for battery units integrated into a submodule. The discussion is followed by the simulations of MMC-HVDC and MMC-BESS on MATLAB/SIMULINK. The simulation results compare the control requirements of both systems and also approves MMC-BESS as a viable solution for the future energy storage systems because of its high efficiency.

articleTitle: Electrical vehicle ordered charging control based on electrical price guiding strategy
abstract: The use of electric energy in electric vehicles can effectively save energy and reduce emissions, However, the disorderly charging of large-scale electric vehicles will have far-reaching impacts and challenges on the economical and reliable and power quality of the distribution network. A charging load model of the electric vehicle is established by the Montacaro method to obtain the parameters such as user charging time, daily driving mileage and charging duration. An effective control strategy for the disordered charging of electric vehicles is proposed which based on the electricity price. Three single-objective optimization strategies with the smallest maximum value of the charging load curve, the smallest peak-to-valley difference and the lowest charging cost are selected. Multi-objective model aiming at reducing the peak-to-valley difference of daily load and reducing the charging cost of electric vehicle users is proposed. Pareto optimal solution set based on fuzzy clustering is introduced to simulate and analyze the comparison of the order and disordered charging of electric vehicles. The results show that the proposed control strategy can smooth the fluctuation of the daily load and improve the steady and reliability of the distribution network with many vehicles.

articleTitle: An optimal volt/var control strategy for an islanded microgrid considering the volt/var control capability
abstract: As an effective way to solve the problem of renewable energy utilization and power supply in remote areas, islanded microgrid has attracted extensive attention in recent years. However, due to the lack of stable reactive sources to provide voltage support and large random fluctuation of renewable energy and load, the reactive power balance and voltage stability of islanded microgrid in remote areas have encountered great challenges. In order to solve the problem of short-term optimal volt/var control of islanded microgrid better, firstly, a new index--volt/var control capability, has been proposed to determine the dynamic reactive power reserve and the allowable upper and lower limits of bus voltage in the microgrid for time to come in this paper. Then, based on this index, an optimal volt/var control strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) has been proposed to make full use of the reactive power output capacity of renewable energy. This optimal volt/var control problem was solved on GAMS platform. Finally, an islanded multibus microgrid with renewable energy such as photovoltaic and micro gas turbine was used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed index and strategy

articleTitle: Research on BMS of large scale battery energy storage power station
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy such as wind energy and solar energy, more and more intermittent and fluctuating energy sources bring a series of unprecedented challenges to the safe and stable operation of power grid. Energy storage technology provides an effective way to solve the problems of frequency modulation and peak shaving of large power grid, friendly access of renewable energy on generation side, peak shaving and valley filling on user side, and stable operation of isolated network. It is considered as one of the most critical technologies to realize renewable energy-dominated power system. Now, several energy storage methods can be divided into physical energy storage, electromagnetic energy storage, electrochemical energy storage and phase change energy storage according to the type of energy storage carrier. Among all kinds of energy storage, the battery energy storage system is used in wind/solar renewable energy fluctuation power smoothing and grid friendly access, frequency and peak regulation of urban power network, and emergency protection of important loads due to its characteristics of no moving parts, no special requirements for site, good dynamic characteristics and high energy density<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]–[5]</sup>.

articleTitle: The evaluation of wind power time series multi-scale modeling methods
abstract: Accurate forecasts of renewable energy generation are critical to the grid operations in the future. Wavelet Transform (WT), Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Mathematical Morphology (MM) are three representative time series decomposition method used to analyze wind power fluctuation patterns. It is proved that the hybrid forecast model has higher accuracy than the traditional model without multi-scale analysis. However, less articles provide an appropriate method to assess multi-scale decomposition analysis. Thus, this article designs an evaluation index system based on the amplitude-frequency characteristic analysis of the decomposition result. The evaluations of decomposing methods mentioned above are compared by their performances on four hybrid forecast model. According to the testing result, our evaluation method is effective and feasible. MM is suitable to extract long-term tendency of wind power, but its middle frequency components have complex fluctuation patterns which may increase modeling complexity. While, WT show better performances on detecting high frequency fluctuations. The evaluation index system proposed in this paper may provide guideline on selecting time series decomposition method to better analyze fluctuation patterns.

articleTitle: Impacts of sequence model for type-3 and type-4 wind turbines on voltage unbalance in large-scale wind farms
abstract: In this paper, the impacts of converter-interfaced wind turbine generators(WTGs) on the voltage unbalance factor(VUF) of wind farms are illustrated. Firstly, the steady-state negative-sequence models of doubly fed induction generator(DFIG) and permanent magnetic synchronous generator(PMSG) are proposed. And the dynamic performance of negative-sequence impedance of DFIG and PMSG with wind speed increasing is analysed. Then, an equivalent negative-sequence model of grid-connected wind farms is proposed. And finally, the verification is performed based on the matlab/simulink platform.

articleTitle: Expanding flexibility with P2H for integrated energy systems
abstract: Combined heat and power (CHP) unit serves as a significant kind of heating source in energy systems, but its heat production must be accompanied by electric production. It could worsen the wind power curtailment in the context of large-scale installed wind farms, which is unfriendly to the integrated energy system operation. Power to hydrogen (P2H), a promising energy conversion technology, is a possible solution to mitigate this issue by consuming excessive electric power, and stored hydrogen can be used in many fields, such as fuel cell and chemical synthesis. Hence, this paper designs an integrated energy system optimisation model with P2H to discuss the feasibility of combining electric power, heat and hydrogen together. Water electrolysis is modelled with an electricity-hydrogen conversion efficiency factor, which is easy to be integrated into a mixed integer optimization problem that mimics the system operation in a 24-hour period. Three cases are designed to demonstrate that the application of P2H improves operating flexibility, and more specifically, the flexibility is visualized by showing equivalent operating region of CHP units.

articleTitle: Power procurement strategies of retailer considering demand response program
abstract: For electricity retailers, the decision-making of energy procurement and sale has become the core issue of operation. In this paper, an energy management model of the electricity retailer in smart grids has been proposed. Multiple energy procurement sources contain pool market (PM), bilateral contracts (BCs), renewable energy sources (photovoltaic (PV) system and wind turbine (WT)). In addition, electric vehicles (EVs), energy storage system (ESS) and demand response program (DRP), are considered for the retailer to reduce the energy procurement cost and to improve the operational risk resistance ability. In the proposed model, objective functions are established from the perspective of the retailer and end-consumers respectively. To validate the proposed model, a case study is conducted and the results are analysed to draw the conclusions.

articleTitle: Faulty line selection based on active-intervention-type arc suppression device via additional neutral resistance
abstract: The excessive arc current will damage electric equipment and threaten personal security when the single-phase-to-ground fault occurs in the distribution network. The active-intervention-type arc suppression device can effectively suppress the arc current by actively switching on the grounding switch of the faulty phase at the bus. However, in case of mis-selection, a more severe two-phase fault will be triggered. This paper studies the procedures of the active-intervention-type arc suppression device and proposes a faulty line and faulty phase selection method based on the neutral point additional resistance. The real-time line-to-ground parameters are calculated using the neutral point voltage changes before and after the additional resistance switching, and then the change of the line-to-grounding parameter is analysed to determine the faulty phase. The zero-sequence components of each line are analysed, and a mathematical formula is presented to determine the faulty line as the switching of the additional resistor will change the zero-sequence circuit of the faulty line. Simulation results show that the proposed method has high accuracy and reliability even for high-resistance-to-ground fault.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity assessment and model reduction based on gap metric for wind turbine predictive control
abstract: Wind energy conversion system (WECS) is a typical nonlinear system that is challenging to control. The nonlinear system is commonly divided into numerous operating subregions employing advanced control method to enrich performance. In each subregion, local model is deduced from the nonlinear system based on selected steady-state operating points (OPs). Large quantity of sub-models brings about frequent model switching with uncertain dynamics and great amount of calculation. This paper presents a nonlinearity assessment approach for wind turbine system espousing gap metric algorithm. The assessment result reveals WECS possesses strong-nonlinearity in the operating region below rated wind speed, and has weak-nonlinearity above rated wind speed. Based on the nonlinearity assessment, the number of local models stored in model bank is reduced significantly. Then model predictive control (MPC) with simplified model bank is proposed covering the whole wind speed range. Simulation results verify the feasibility of model reduction approach depending on presented nonlinearity assessment, and prove the good coordinative control performance of proposed MPC.

articleTitle: Modular modelling method for DC transformer with multiple inputs and multiple outputs
abstract: Today's power grid is characterized by the high penetration of the power electronic devices. With the emergence of large numbers of DC loads and DC renewable energy sources, medium-voltage (MV) DC distribution network is the potential to develop the modern power system in the future. As one of the key techniques of the MVDC distribution network, a modular modelling method of the DC transformer is presented in detail in this paper. Firstly, based on the power balance, a big-signal average model of DC transformer is proposed by analysing the switch working mode. The equipment of the DC transformer used in this paper is the dual active bridge (DAB). The model provides a unified and flexible modelling method without changing the control strategy. Furthermore, for the multiple inputs and outputs of the MVDC distribution network, the model is applied in the Input-Series Output-Parallel (ISOP) and Input-Parallel Output-Series (IPOS) system based on the modular method. Finally, the average model proposed is built in the MATLAB/SIMULINK software. For the potential project of the MVDC distribution network, the systematic simulation model of DABs with multiple inputs and multiple outputs is built and the effectiveness of the modular modelling method proposed is verified.

articleTitle: Two-terminal fault location scheme based on distributed parameters of cable-overhead hybrid transmission line
abstract: A complex cable-overhead hybrid transmission line was used in the Zhenhai-Zhoushan 500k V line project in East China, which cannot be located accurately in the event of a fault and cannot automatic reclosing the failure of the overhead line. This paper proposes a fault location scheme which is suitable for cable-overhead hybrid transmission lines. The scheme uses positive-sequence fault components and uses the accurate parameters of each section for the hybrid line to achieve two-terminal location based on distributed parameters and locate fault zone accurately. The simulation results show that the accuracy parameters of each section of the Zhenhai-Zhoushan 500kV overhead-submarine hybrid line are used. The fault location accuracy of each fault location and fault type is no more than 2.5% or ±1km. The distance measurement result is not affected by the transition resistance, which could identify overhead line faults automatically and put into reclosing.

articleTitle: Business model and economic analysis of user-side BESS in industrial parks in China
abstract: A business model of user-side battery energy storage system (BESS) in industrial parks is established based on the policies of energy storage in China. The business model mainly consists of three parts: an operation strategy design for user-side BESS, a method for measuring electricity, and a way of profit distribution between investors and operators. And then an economic analysis model of user-side BESS is developed considering different charging/discharging operation strategies. Particularly, for lead carbon battery, lithium ion battery and all-vanadium redox flow battery, cost/benefit analysis and sensitivity analysis of key parameters of user-side BESS are carried out in detail.
