articleTitle: Renewable energy resources and technologies applicable to Sri Lanka towards a 100% RE future
abstract: The combustion of fossil fuels primarily provides the energy supply in Sri Lanka. The energy generation in Sri Lanka is primarily realized by the combustion of thermal energy such as diesel and coal. The second energy generation source is Hydroelectricity. In 2016, Sri Lanka supplied an average of 67% of the total energy demand using fossil fuels such as thermal oil and thermal coal (100% imported); and 33% with renewable energy (30% hydro and 3% non-conventional, renewable energy), even though there are enough available renewable resources such as solar, wind and biomass, to supply all the energy required. Sri Lanka should begin to utilize the above renewable energy resources more effectively and abundantly as fossil fuel prices increase and deplete; and their effects of global warming worsen. Sri Lanka aims to achieve 100% electricity generation from high-quality renewable energy resources (100RE) by 2050. When meeting this target, the use of solar, biomass, wind, ocean energy and energy recovery from waste technologies are expected to play a significant role. The increasing use of renewable energy technologies will be of help with the solution of energy-related current environmental and socio-economic problems and will assist in sustainable development. This paper reviews the available potential resources, the status of renewable energy technologies and market status in Sri Lanka by considering Sri Lanka's present energy status and the future energy mix towards 100RE.

articleTitle: Factors affecting for consumer attractiveness towards net metered solar PV technology in Sri Lanka
abstract: The objective of this paper is to establish social-economic factors that affect the consumer acceptance of domestic net metered solar PV technology in Colombo district, Sri Lanka. Although, Sri Lankan energy sector admitted net metering in the year 2010, the number of connections has reached only to 5155 with capacity of 32.9 MW by year 2017. However, the authorities expect to achieve a 10% contribution to grid electricity from small non-conventional renewable energy sources and the net-meter facilities by 2020. We develop a conceptual model that describes how consumer's ability to buy and consumer's willingness to pay relate to net-metered solar PV systems. Our model accounts for both socio-economic factors and technological factors. Our results show a positive and a significant contribution of the factors such as investment, technology literacy, tariff structure and consumer demand to the consumer attractiveness towards net-metered solar PV technology in Sri Lanka. However, the regulatory concerns do not show a significant contribution to the consumer attractiveness towards net-metered solar PV technology. There are no moderating effects from consumer education level and their social values to the attractiveness of net-metered solar PV.

articleTitle: Design and application of RTDS & GH Bladed co-simulation research platform for DFIG wind turbine
abstract: With the rapid development of wind power technology, wind power penetration is continually increasing and has reached over 50% in certain areas. Most DFIG wind turbine researches rely on off-line simulation software, it takes longer simulation time than real working condition, they also adopt off-line software controller, which is impossible to completely replace hardware controller and cannot meet the testing requirements for equipment and control strategies. This paper designs a co-simulation real-time research platform for DFIG wind turbine. All electrical parts are built in Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) while all aerodynamic parts are built in GH Bladed, real-time communication among GH Bladed, RTDS and master controller PLC are applied through communication PLC to mirror system real working condition, distributed DSP control system and master controller PLC are both used as DFIG hardware controller. Experiment results demonstrate that the co-simulation platform is capable of mirroring actual wind turbine system working condition.

articleTitle: Research on parameter testing method of centralized reactive power compensation device for photovoltaic power station
abstract: The centralized reactive power compensation devices used in photovoltaic power plants have high voltage level and far exceed the capacity of test devices, laboratory/field test conditions can not meet all typical working conditions, and can not obtain model parameters through test data. Therefore, this paper presents a parameter test method for centralized reactive power compensation device based on Hardware-in-the-loop simulation. Firstly, a detailed topological model and a test device model of the centralized reactive power compensation device are established, connecting model with controller of centralized reactive power compensation device through optical and electrical physical interface, the hardware-in-the-loop simulation test platform of centralized reactive power compensation device is established. Then, for all typical operating conditions, a centralized reactive power compensation device model parameter testing method is proposed. Finally, based on the hardware-in-the-loop simulation test platform, the parameters of a certain type of SVG are tested. The test results show that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: The influence of power loss on asynchronous grid and calculation of assemble power
abstract: The large power grid is divided into several small power grids which are only connected by DC transmission and operate asynchronously. It can effectively reduce short-circuit current and relieve the operating pressure of power grid. However, asynchronous interconnection will reduce the scale of power grid and weaken its ability to withstand power loss. When power loss occurs in a province, available transfer capability (ATC) can be used to calculate the support power from other non-accident system. Under synchronous and asynchronous interconnection, when DC block faults with different capacities occur, the frequency variation of GD grid is given. Based on ATC, a calculation model of maximum callable capacity was constructed. According to the maximum callable capacity of power grid and amount of power loss, the hierarchical division method of power loss and the principle of integrated adjustment of multi-level planning at different levels were proposed.

articleTitle: Application of Bayesian regression method in performance assessment of PV modules
abstract: Threshold-based methods are widely applied for performance assessment of photovoltaic (PV) modules because of their unique advantages. Traditional threshold-based methods apply deterministic estimation models to calculate the residuals between the estimated and the measured PV power, and then compare the residuals to the predefined normal thresholds. When a residual exceeds the thresholds, the corresponding point is identified as an outlier. These methods have a limitation, i.e., they do not take the uncertainties in the model parameters into consideration. In this paper, a new PV performance assessment method is proposed to improve the traditional methods by using the Bayesian Regression (BR) method. The method consists of: (i) developing the BR model of PV efficiency, (ii) constructing confidence intervals based on the developed model, and (iii) using the constructed confidence intervals as the normal thresholds for performance assessment of PV modules. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed methodology, the methods based on the deterministic estimation models are implemented for comparison. Results show that the proposed method is greatly superior to the traditional methods when used to detect power losses of 10%.

articleTitle: A test method for UHVDC protection based on wide area information synchronization
abstract: In order to truly reflect the performance of DC protection in the event of UHVDC system fault, an UHVDC protection test method of centralized control and wide-area synchronous input/output, which can be called "one master and multiple slaves" method is proposed in this paper. The test can meet the needs of the same function UHVDC protection synchronous test in the whole station range. Each test slave's hardware interface is designed according to the requirements of the tested protection's input and output interface. It can achieve the seamless transition of the tested protection's operation state and test state, and the full presentation of the tested protection action results, which is convenient for the operation personnel to effectively judge the tested protection performance. In the test method, 2.4G wireless data interaction technology is used for data interaction, and GPS is used to synchronize with each test slave. The field test of commutation failure protection in converter protection is displayed in this paper to illustrate the implementation steps. The test result shows that the proposed method can truly reflect the action process of the tested protection under actual fault conditions, and the performance check is authentic and reliable.

articleTitle: A health diagnosis method for photovoltaic module based on neural network
abstract: A new health diagnosis method for photovoltaic(PV) modules is proposed in view of the fact that most of the PV modules are installed outdoors and are prone to malfunction due to extreme weather. The meteorological factors affecting PV power generation are analyzed. Training samples are selected based on the weather forecast updated once every 3 hours, and the back propagation(BP) neural network approach is utilized to establish an output prediction model of PV modules in normal state. The fault state of PV module is simulated by experiment. Take the fault data as the input of the well-trained PV output prediction model, and output values of the prediction model are compared with that of the PV module in normal state. The experimental results show that the proposed diagnosis method can detect the faults of PV modules.

articleTitle: Investigate the influence of renewable energy penetration on the electricity market equilibrium
abstract: China is performing the electricity market reform. With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, it is important to understand how the renewables influence the market performance. Renewables are different from the traditional generators in two aspects: 1) the marginal costs of renewable are small; 2) renewables cause fluctuations and increase the requirement of auxiliary service. In this paper, we analyse the influence of renewables on the market equilibrium. A multi-period Supply Function Equilibrium (SFE) model is formulated, where the upper level model maximizes individual profits of market participants, and the lower level model minimizes the market operational costs. To avoid the infeasibility of the equilibrium model, the relaxation of the complementary slackness condition is utilized. This paper exhibits how the increase of renewable penetrations affects the optimal bidding and profits of other market participants, including the traditional generators, hydro generator, and storage. The influence of renewables on the market equilibrium is exhibited as well.

articleTitle: Topology and parameter design of power quality control device for medium voltage distribution network
abstract: Power quality control device for medium voltage distribution network with source-load isolation is presented in this paper. It can solve many power quality problems, such as frequency fluctuation, voltage fluctuation, voltage flicker, voltage sag, short-term voltage, three-phase unbalance, harmonics, intermittent wave, temporary overvoltage and so on. It does not need to detect power quality events, and can realize seamless switching between grid side power supply and energy storage power supply when voltage sag and voltage short interruption, ensuring uninterrupted high quality power supply on the load side. A parameter design method considering redundancy of cascaded H-bridge is proposed, and a set of 1MVA power quality control device for medium voltage distribution network is developed. Experiments verify the effectiveness of the device parameter design method and the power quality management performance. An effective method for comprehensive improvement of power quality in distribution network is proposed.

articleTitle: Research on information interaction mechanism of plug-and-play of battery energy storage system
abstract: With the large-scale application of distributed generators, how to realize self-description and interoperability is a difficult point of plug-and-play information interaction technology. Taking BESS as the research object, a plug-and-play information interaction mechanism is established according to IEC61850 communication model and protocol mapping. The mechanism is based on information modeling and self-description of the terminal-layer device. The mapping relationship between IEC61850 meta-model and IEC60870-5-104 protocol is formed by extending IEC61850 meta-model. The heterogeneous model mapping and data conversion module is designed for interactive data conversion between IEC61850 information and IEC61968 message. In this way, the information interaction path between the master station layer and the terminal layer is formed. On that basis, a plug-and-play information interaction architecture is established. The architecture consists of three parts: the monitoring master station layer, the distributed terminal layer and the communication network. Taking a typical feeder segment from distribution network as a case, the consistency test is conducted to verify the validity of the self-describing information and the information interaction mechanism.

articleTitle: Research on overcurrent suppression strategy of true bipolar MMC-HVDC single pole blocking bridge arm
abstract: Due to the characteristics of Vf control in the islanding flexible dc power grid, when the single-pole latching fault occurs at the sending end of the dc power grid, the converter station connected to the new energy island system cannot control the ac voltage and the incoming new energy power at the same time. A healthy pole converter is forced to transfer the active power of the faulty pole converter, which results in the over-current blocking of the healthy pole converter. In this paper, by describing the dynamic process of the bridge arm current when the single-pole locking fault occurs, the mechanism of the over-current is studied, and a new type of additional control is proposed to suppress the magnitude of the over-current of the bridge arm by controlling the dc voltage. Finally, PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and control strategy.

articleTitle: Evaluation of EV battery degradation under different charging strategies and V2G schemes
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are key to cut down transport CO2 emissions, but the bottleneck lies in costly batteries. Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) can bring benefits to both the power grid and EV owners, but its implementation faces challenges due to the concern of battery degradation. In this paper, EV battery degradation under various charging strategies and V2G operational schemes is evaluated. Based on an empirical capacity fade model and real-world operational data, the capacity losses in lithium-ion batteries under each scenario are quantified. Delayed charging is found to be beneficial to reduce the ageing caused capacity loss of EV batteries. Analytical results also show that providing V2G services does not necessarily accelerate the battery degradation; in some cases, it even mitigates the ageing process. A case study undertaken shows that, compared to non-V2G scenario (no battery discharging to the grid), battery capacity loss under V2G is reduced by 13.51%. This work highlights the practices of implementing proper charging strategy and V2G scheme to reduce the negative impact on the batteries lifespan.

articleTitle: Analysis on the contribution of factors affecting the total city energy consumption
abstract: The control of total city energy consumption is one of the important tasks of the city energy transition. By considering the comparability and availability of the data, and using the numerical method to construct the contribution of each influencing factor to the change of the total energy consumption, different factors affecting the total energy consumption was decomposed and analyzed. The degree model, in turn, obtains the relative contribution of various influencing factors to the change of total city energy consumption. The validity of the model was verified by taking Beijing as a sample. Analysis results from the model can provide support for the selection of key areas and key methods for total city energy consumption control.

articleTitle: Research on SSO suppression method based on reduced order model and variable structure control
abstract: Subsynchronous oscillation(SSO) shows the characteristics of nonlinear oscillation due to the nonlinearity of power system. But most of the existing SSO controllers are designed by linear method, and the effect is imperfect. The order of the system model is too large because SSO has multiple oscillation modes, which makes it difficult to use the nonlinear method to design the controller. So it is necessary to reduce the order of the system model before using the nonlinear control method. In this paper, the nonlinear sliding mode variable structure control method, which has strong robustness, is applied to the design of SSO damping controller. Firstly, the modal perturbation order reduction method is used to reduce the order of the SSO system model, which preserves the key state variables. Then the parameters of SVC damping controller are tuned by pole assignment which is carried out using variable structure control. Finally compared with the traditional phase compensation method, simulation results are given to verify this proposed method can effectively suppress multiple SSO modes at the same time.

articleTitle: Clean energy on wheels: Model, optimisation and P2P energy trading for active distribution networks in smart cities
abstract: To manage the growing penetration of renewables and electric vehicles (EVs), a concept of clean energy on wheels (CEW) is presented for active distribution networks in smart cities. The CEW is an EV fully equipped with battery energy storage systems and EV chargers to improve the performance of modern distribution systems, especially in peak load hours. A multi-area power flow calculation method is employed to predict energy surplus and deficit feeders and locations at the same time. A bi-level optimisation framework is developed to determine the integration buses and capacities of PV systems and CEW vehicles in multiple distribution systems in smart cities. A Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading scheme is adopted to obtain optimal scheduling and power dispatch of CEW in different areas of the city. An improved version of the genetic algorithm is adopted to determine optimisation variables of both the levels. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, eight low-voltage feeders of different areas are selected from the city. Moreover, multiple scenarios are proposed and investigated. The simulation results obtained are found to be promising to accommodate a high penetration of EVs and renewables while increasing the operational flexibility of associated distribution systems.

articleTitle: A high frequency hybrid active filter based on SiC MOSFET
abstract: The extensive use of pulse width modulation control technology in smart grid will lead to prominent enlargement of high-frequency harmonics. In this paper, a hybrid filter structure that uses an active filter in series with an LC filter has been proposed tested in this paper, where a high frequency harmonic compensation scheme utilizing SiC MOSFE is studied. The proposed filter can be applied in high frequency applications because of the high frequency switching characteristics of SiC MOSFET. And the rate voltage on the active filter can be reduced due to the use of capacitors, meanwhile a second-order bandpass filter added in control system to modify the phase shift caused by LC filter. Case studies show that it has a good performance in suppressing the harmonic current amplification caused by the resonance of the transmission line, which is verified by simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Modeling and application of harmonic transfer and amplification analysis of HVDC transmission
abstract: With the wide use of power electronic equipment in power systems, harmonic problems have become one of the more prominent ones in the power grid. In recent years, there are many HVDC 50Hz protection mal-operation events in the field caused by converter transformer unloaded energizing. The phenomena of harmonic transfer and amplification in HVDC has an undeniable impact on overall power system operation. Currently, the study about this has relied mainly on detailed electromagnetic transient simulations. However, simulations normally have large computational burdens and lower efficiency due to the complexity of their models and small simulation time-steps used. So an efficient analysis model of harmonics with HVDC various operating modes is suggested in the paper. This model considers DC smoothing reactors and filters in different operating modes, and the modelling of converters and transmission lines are highlighted. Compared with detailed electromagnetic simulation results confirm the validity and accuracy of the model. Moreover, it also can be easily applied to the HVDC systems for harmonic amplification evaluation. All the results show that the proposed model not only has lower computational requirements but also can represent HVDC harmonic transfer and amplification during different operating modes.

articleTitle: Minimisation of distribution feeder loss using ant colony optimisation applied to network reconfiguration and distributed generations placement
abstract: Reduction in active power loss can help distribution network operators (DNOs) save costs and increase profits. Most research projects have focused only on the optimisation of either the DNR or the DG allocation problem. This study describes an Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO) algorithm to assess the distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) and distributed generation (DG) placement problems simultaneously in terms of distribution feeder loss minimisation. The results carried out on two standard IEEE 33-node and 69-node systems are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The effect of DG capacities on DNR for feeder loss reduction is also discussed.

articleTitle: An improved negative selection algorithm based identification model for distribution network operating state with small samples
abstract: The distribution network is in normal operation for most of the time. How to identify the fault state by using a small amount of fault samples has been drawn a widely concern. In addition, it is difficult to identify the earth fault with high resistance in distribution network. In this paper, an improved negative selection algorithm based identification model for distribution network operating state with small samples is proposed. By using wavelet packet energy analysis, the sum of node energy of the last layer in high frequency is taken as the extracted characteristic of high resistance faults. Using a few fault samples to optimize and cluster the detector set generated by normal samples, an improved negative selection method is proposed to generate enough detector sets with higher coverage of non-self set area. This method improves the detection rate and realizes the classification of abnormal states. Based on a 10 kV distribution network, the performance of the proposed identification model is evaluated. Compared with NSA and the neural network algorithm, the proposed algorithm can effectively identify the operating state in distribution network with small samples.

articleTitle: Research on control strategy of PQ mode virtual synchronous generator with autonomous voltage regulation function
abstract: The virtual synchronous generator reactive voltage regulation strategy running in PQ mode usually adopts droop control, and its outer loop control directly accepts the reactive power command of AVC in the station to realize the voltage tracking control of the station, but is limited by the automatic voltage control (AVC) period control characteristics in the station. When the voltage fluctuates abnormally, it is unable to respond to voltage fluctuations quickly and increase the risk of wind turbine disconnection failure. This paper proposes a VSG control strategy for automatic reactive power compensation with abnormal voltage fluctuations. The principle analysis of the control method and the specific parameter setting principle are given, so that it can follow the stable operation of the AVC reactive command in the station in steady state, and respond to the voltage change autonomously in the transient state. Finally, a wind farm simulation model is built to verify the correctness and feasibility of this control strategy.

articleTitle: A smooth LVRT switching control method for doubly-fed self-synchronous generator
abstract: With the further increase in the proportion of wind power access, self-synchronous control method can achieve better grid connection stability than the traditional phase-locked synchronous control method, however, the current impact problem is hard to solve during LVRT process. In order to make self-synchronous control have LVRT capability, an intuitive idea is to combine the self-synchronous control with the traditional LVRT control method, in other words using phase-locked synchronous control in the voltage traversing process, and switch back to self-synchronous after voltage recovery, however, how to ensure the smoothing of the switching process is still a subject worth studying. Existing research is mostly directed to full-power grid-connected systems, therefore, this paper designs a no-error current trajectory method for self-synchronous regulator during LVRT for doubly-fed generator, which keep the control signal always tracking the current reference to avoid current impact during fault recovery. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Data-driven combining forecasting method for the net demand of power retailers in distribution network
abstract: With the rapid development of China's electricity market and the commercial system for the sale, the net demand forecasting for power retailers in distribution network have attracted great concern. This paper proposes a data-driven technology, i.e., the adaptive combining algorithm, to improve the accuracy of predictive models. Using the technology of big data analysis, this paper proposes an anomaly-state recognition method based on fuzzy algorithm. Moreover, fuzzy clustering and hierarchical clustering method are used to search the optimal similar day. After that, the "Relief-Correlation Test" is executed to adaptively select input features for each sampling point. Finally, a novel variable-weight combining forecasting algorithm is proposed to predict the net demand of power retailers in distribution network. The proposed method is verified by a real distribution-network power retailer in China. Results show that the data-driven combining forecasting model proposed in this paper is more reliable and effective than other individual predictive models for the net demand forecasting of power retailers.

articleTitle: Analysis on fault characteristic of metallic return in true bipolar VSC-HVDC transmission system
abstract: Overhead transmission lines of VSC-based Direct-current(DC) grid is an important application direction of VSC-HVDC charactered by high-voltage and large-capacity in the future. In the research on fault characteristics of flexible DC transmission system, up to now the research result related to the metallic return is seldom reported Asymmetric operating state would change the potential of neutral bus in metallic return network, which may endanger the safe operation state of the the VSC-HVDC transmission system. In this paper, the fault characteristics of metallic return in bipolar VSC-HVDC transmission are analyzed. The mathematical model of metallic return network under grounding and breakage faults are established in different operating conditions. The mechanism of DC voltage rise or decrease and the development progress of fault are also described. The results show that the voltage exceed the steady-state operation requirements in asymmetric state when the metallic return fault is not cleared. The simulation results of PSCAD/EMTDC verify the correctness of the analysis result.

articleTitle: Coordinated scheduling and optimal control of all-electric ship energy system based on mixed logical dynamic method
abstract: An all-electric ship (AES) can be regarded as a mobile microgrid comprised of distributed generators (DGs), multi-energy storage systems (ESSs) and flexible heating, cooling and dynamic loads. Conventionally, coordination of these controllable units and multi-energy coupling is not taken into consideration during AES's voyage, which limits the operation efficiency. Moreover, little research has been conducted on the optimal control process during AES' voyage when uncertain waves and weather factors matters. This paper aims to coordinate energy consumption economically and eco-friendly, and to find out the optimal control decision to follow when AES encounters unpredictable uncertainties. Firstly, a long-term coordinative optimization model is proposed to schedule energy consumption during the period. Obtained optimal schedule is then set as the reference value tracked by the short-term stochastic predictive control model, which is established based on mixed logical dynamic (MLD) method. The short-term optimization will be updated according to actual value of uncertain factors and be continuously solved in a rolling way before next long-term optimization is executed. In this way, an optimal closed-loop control is derived. Simulation results demonstrate AES's better performance through our methodology in reducing energy consumption and dealing with uncertainties during the voyage compared with that of conventional ones.

articleTitle: Study on H-bridge cascaded multi level dynamic voltage restorer with cross-feed and multi energy supply
abstract: Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) has an effective function for power supply. For a further reliability, cross feed structure is always designed. In this paper, photovoltaic and energy storage are introduced in the cell DC supply for a H-Bridge Cascaded Multi Level DVR, which could overcome the shortage of the Diode uncontrolled rectifier circuit. DC/DC converter and the control is designed for the power and voltage regulation. To validate it, a simulation model is established in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The results are satisfactory.

articleTitle: Virtual synchronous generator control in solid-state transformer with DC voltage compensation
abstract: This paper investigates virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy in solid-state transformer (SST). Firstly, this paper introduces the topology and control strategy of SST, including VSG control strategy and single phase shift control strategy. By analysing the DC voltage fluctuation caused by power change and grid connection, a VSG control strategy with DC voltage compensation is proposed. This control method maintains the stability of DC voltage and reduce power fluctuations. Secondly, in order to realize SST seamless connection to the grid, a voltage pre-synchronization control method is proposed. This control method realizes the output voltage of SST tracks the grid voltage to keep the amplitude and phase synchronized. Finally, the simulation is carried out in PSCAD / EMTDC to verify the feasibility of the proposed control strategy and solid-state transformer topology.

articleTitle: Control strategy of cascaded H-bridge grid-connected photovoltaic system without PLL in the static coordinate
abstract: The unbalanced output power among solar cells of the cascaded H-bridge (CHB) grid-connected photovoltaic inverter makes the cells with normal output power over-modulation, which results in grid-connected current distortion. Due to the grid voltage fluctuation, the detection accuracy of PLL (phase-locked loop) decreases, resulting in poor system control performance. Especially in the case of power imbalance, it will lead to system instability. For this reason, a control strategy applied to the CHB grid-connected photovoltaic system without PLL is proposed. Based on the power imbalance control strategy using reactive power compensation, this control strategy uses a reference sine and cosine signals algorithm. When the grid voltage is distorted, the algorithm can provide the unit sine and cosine signals synchronized with the grid voltage fundamental to calculate the grid-connected current reference signal, which can satisfy the control requirements of the system under power balance and power imbalance.

Author Keywords: REFERENCE SINE AND COSINE SIGNALS ALGORITHM

articleTitle: Dynamic Var planning in large hybrid AC/DC receiving-end grid under large scale renewables accessing conditions
abstract: The development of HVDC transmission technique brings the possibility for the consumption of large scale renewables in long distances over areas. However, the uncertainty of large scale renewables and strong-DC-weak-AC property are creating challenges to the operation safety and voltage stability of large hybrid AC/DC receiving-end grid. This paper proposes a locating method for dynamic Var compensation devices in a large hybrid AC/DC receiving-end grid under large scale renewables accessing conditions. By reasonably planning the installation location of dynamic Var compensation devices, it will improve the system's voltage stability as much as possible with limited equipment. Firstly, this paper partitions the grid into regions by means of the hub nodes. Considering the uncertainty of large scale renewable energy, and based on the impedance modulus margin together with load weight of the nodes, the weakness degree index is proposed to evaluate the static voltage stability of each region and determine the weak region. Then based on the weak-region-determine result, this paper proposes an improved trajectory sensitivity index considering specific faults related to the renewables. The pilot node is the optimized installation location which can be obtained through calculating the index with dynamic simulation. Finally, through case study in east China power grid, the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: Harmonic state space impedance model of MMC considering internal impedance of AC and DC Grid
abstract: Impedance modeling of modular multilevel converters (MMC) has attracted extensive research in recent years. Many modeling methods have been proposed to model MMC. To simplify the analysis, these methods ignore the internal impedance of AC and DC grid connected to MMC. However, ignoring these impedances will seriously affect the impedance characteristics of MMC, resulting in an inaccurate model. In this paper, a modified model based on harmonic state space (HSS) method is proposed, which can reflect the influence of arbitrary AC and DC grid impedance on MMC. This method improves the accuracy of the model and provides theoretical basis for impedance analysis when MMC connected to any other equipment. Finally, simulation results validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Study on Krogstad wind tunnel experiment by actuator line model considering nacelle effect
abstract: Wake effect reduces the power output and increases the fatigue damage on wind turbines. As a result, wake models attract attentions from researchers in this realm. Among wake models, Actuator line model is the most promising one, because it can balance well between accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, the Krogstad wind tunnel experiment was studied by using actuator line model. It was found that the nacelle effect that is neglected in the conventional actuator line model is significant in the Krogstad wind tunnel experiment. To overcome this problem, a point-source nacelle model is proposed, which works well not only for RANS model but also for LES model.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of operation boundary for cascaded H-bridge energy storage system with inner phase rapid state of charge balancing
abstract: Battery energy storage system (BESS) offers various kinds of power system applications with high flexibility and reliability. Cascaded H-bridge (CHB) topology is one of the most promising topologies for large scale BESS. Due to its vital role in energy management, the state of charge (SOC) of BESS is given high importance. This paper focuses on the study of the influence of SOC on the operating boundary of battery energy storage systems. The SOC, boundary of input/output active power, and boundary of reactive power are coupled together. Based on the real 2MW∗0.5h/10kV BESS in Baoqing battery energy storage station, Shenzhen, China, the mathematical model of typical single-stage cascaded H-bridge (CHB) BESS is established. Through the aggregation algorithm, a model of the relationship between the potential of the BESS and the SOC is proposed. Considering the BESS potential, current slew and voltage drop across the grid-connection inductors, which determines the input/output currents, the boundaries of input/output active power and reactive power of BESS are analyzed according to SOC range. Finally, the conclusions about the design and operation of the battery energy storage system are presented.

articleTitle: A dynamic defense-attack game scheme with incomplete information for vulnerability analysis in a cyber-physical power infrastructure
abstract: The modern power system is experiencing rapid development towards a smarter cyber-physical power grid. How to comprehensively and effectively identify the vulnerable components under various cyber attacks has attracted widespread interest and attention around the world. In this paper, a game-theoretical scheme is developed to analyze the vulnerabilities of transmission lines and cyber elements under locally coordinated cyber-physical attacks in a cyber-physical power infrastructure. A two-step scenario including resources allocation made by system defender in advance and subsequent coordinated cyber-physical attacks are designed elaborately. The designed scenario is modeled as a game of incomplete information, which is then converted into a bi-level mathematical programming problem. In the lower level model, the attacker aims at maximizing system losses by attacking some transmission lines. While in the higher level model, the defender allocates defensive resources, trying to maximally reduce the losses considering the possible attacks. The payoffs of the game are calculated by leveraging a strategy of searching accident chains caused by cascading failure analyzed in this paper. A particle swarm optimization algorithm is applied to solve the proposed nonlinear bi-level programming model, and the case studies on a 34-bus system are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: An application of Marshall-Edgeworth spot price index in wind-thermal generation swap option pricing
abstract: With the fast development of electricity markets, financial derivatives such as options have been led in to hedge against the volatility of spot prices and other uncertainties, which help generators to realize the risk management. As is known, the spot market price is the important reference of risk control. So equitable and reasonable derivatives require an index which could precisely measure the practical level of spot market prices over a period of time. Firstly, this paper presents the most widely used indices (arithmetic average and weight average) and analyses the major flaws of them. On the basis of predecessors, we introduce an improved index with lower bias based on the Marshall-Edgeworth index system as the underlying price of average rate options. Finally, a simulation example shows that the method will bring less revenue volatility for renewable energy generators.

articleTitle: A transient stability enhancement control method for inverter interfaced distribution generators
abstract: With the development of the renewable energies, the transient stability problem of the distributed generators (DGs) are more and more paid attention to. This paper proposes a droop factors adaptive control method to enhance transient stability for inverter interfaced distributed generators (IIDGs). The method changes droop factors according to the current status of the IIDG. An activation mechanism is designed to judge the IIDG's status. The control method is proved to be efficient to enhance the transient stability of IIDGs through simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of new DC power grids for large-scale clean energy integration and transmission
abstract: The impact of new energy fluctuation on the grid can be reduced and the reliability can be improved by the network structure of new DC transmission technology, compared with point-to-point structure of the traditional DC transmission technology. Focusing on this background, the main research efforts are listed as follows. Firstly, the planning schemes of new DC transmission system in industrialized and underdeveloped countries around the world are summarized, it is concluded that the HVDC technology with network structure will be the main choice of the future power grid instead of point-to-point structure. Secondly, the recent typical HVDC projects are illustrated and the manufacturer's improvements of converter technology are summarized, it is concluded that the DC voltage level will be raised and transmission capacity will be enlarged with the development of the technology. Thirdly, the principle, structure, advantages and challenges of VSC-HVDC technology are introduced, it is concluded that the future research will focus on the new modular topology of the converter and the coordination of protection strategy. Finally, the performance of point-to-point and network-to-network transmission structures is compared and simulated from the steady-state characteristics, transient characteristics and economical three aspects, the results show that more clean energy can be integrated and transmitted with network-to-network structure based on VSC-HVDC technology.

articleTitle: Analysis on stability of DC distributed power system
abstract: Distributed power system is widely used in new energy, communication, aerospace and other fields due to its high reliability, high power density and high flexibility. When the subsystem is designed separately, it can meet the requirements of stability and dynamic performance, but when several subsystems are cascaded into a distributed power system, it may lead to the instability of the whole system. This paper introduces the stability criterion, impedance ratio monitoring and impedance optimization methods of distributed power system in detail, and the hot and difficult problems are analyzed in the future.

articleTitle: Coupling analysis of multi-heterogeneous energy systems considering wind-photovoltaic power
abstract: In this paper, wind-photovoltaic power generations are taken as research objects. Based on the factor analysis method, the outputs of wind-photovoltaic power generations are characterized by dimensionality reduction. The composite score is used as the description index of the daily output power characteristics of each power generation system. By using the capacity coupling concept and the capacity coupling coefficient model in physics, the coupling degree model of multi-energy system is constructed for the analysis of the coupling of multi-heterogeneous energy systems.

articleTitle: A multi-pattern coordinative scheduling for large capacity energy storage system
abstract: With the development of energy storage technology and the reduction of construction costs, the battery energy storage power stations are changing from small capacity and joint scheduling of wind and light storage to large capacity and independent scheduling and operation. To this end, a multi-pattern coordinated scheduling method for the large-capacity vanadium redox energy storage power station is proposed; the operational characteristics of battery energy storage are analyzed. On this basis, the scheduling strategy of battery energy storage participating in power grid peak regulation, frequency modulation and the provision of standby is proposed; the wind power prediction error is fuzzified. Based on the credibility theory, a multi-pattern optimized scheduling model for vanadium redox battery energy storage based on fuzzy chance constraints is established. The model is solved through the mixed integer programming method. The model mentioned above is applied to practical examples. The simulation results show that the energy storage power station participating in multi-pattern applications can further improve the economy and safety of the power grid.

articleTitle: Application and comparison of two heat-electricity ratio regulation modes in regional integrated energy systems
abstract: Determining power generation capacity by heat load is no good for absorbing new energy and cutting down expenses in the operation of regional integrated energy system. Two methods are put forward to solve this problem, one of which is installing heat storage, the other one is adding supplementary combustion device. Both methods could make the heat-electricity ratio more flexible, the system operation cost would decline at the same time, while no article has ever compared the pros and cons of the two modes. In this article, two optimization operation models of regional integrated energy system (RIES) are built to study the application and comparison of the two heat-power ratio regulation modes. An energy flow description method based on sub-hubs is proposed. The models could be converted to 0–1 mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problems and solved by MATLAB along with the mathematical model solver CPLEX. An example was established to verify the algorithm and analyse the results. The comparison between the two modes is made from four aspects including economic benefits, energy efficiency, flexibility of heat-power ratio and environmental benefits. The results show that adding supplementary combustion device is better when comes to economic benefits and energy efficiency, while installing heat storage is more practical when taking environmental benefits, flexibility of heat-electricity ratio into consideration. This article provides reliable reference for integrated energy operators when they have to choose one from the two heat-electricity ratio regulation modes.

articleTitle: Winding loss calculation revisited for medium-frequency transformer in applications of DC generation of new energy
abstract: This paper presents a survey on the winding loss models for foil, round and litz conductors used in design of medium-frequency (MF) transformers in applications of dc generation of new energy, where always one-dimensional (1-D) models are employed. Until now, quite a few 1-D models have been reported, such as the Dowell model, the Ferreira model, the Tourkhani model, the Sullivan model and so on, which makes selection of the models quite confused. To address this issue, the exact 1-D winding loss models are derived first based on a proposed more comprehensible explanation of the orthogonality between skin effect and proximity effect. Different approximations of the exact 1-D models are then investigated, together with an analysis of the reported 1-D models. It is observed that all the 1-D models can be derived from the orthogonality, the Dowell model and the Ferreira model are the exact 1-D solutions, the Tourkhani model and the Sullivan model for litz wires are the high number of strand layers approximation and the low frequency high number of bundle layers approximation, respectively. Based on the observation and other reported observations, proper models are able to be selected in design of MF transformers.

articleTitle: An improved adaptive nonlinear droop control method in DC microgrid
abstract: It is well know that the load sharing among several paralleled distributed sources can be achieved by the conventional droop control in the DC microgrid. However, there is a design tradeoff in the conventional droop control method with respect to load sharing and voltage regulation. To improve both two performances, this paper proposes an improved adaptive nonlinear droop control by the means of dividing the load condition into two categories: the heavy load and the light load. At the light loading range, a good voltage regulation is prioritized due to no overload phenomenon. At the heavy loads, the load sharing is prioritized since a small load sharing error may cause the risk of overload. Moreover, the good load sharing performance also improves the voltage regulation at the heavy loads, which avoids the additional compensation circuits. This paper also gives the design method to define the boundary between light load and high load. Then a curve fitting method is used to permit an automatic track during different load ranges. Finally, two paralleled DC converters are built and the experimental results verify the theoretical analysis well.

articleTitle: A frequency division control for hybrid energy storage system considering the unbalanced current rate of change in DC micro-grid
abstract: In this paper, considering the unbalanced current rate of change in an islanding DC micro-grid, a frequency division control for hybrid energy storage system (HESS) is proposed. In the proposed control, the unbalanced current on the DC bus is decomposed into two components of high and low current rate of change using a rate limiter controller firstly. Secondly, the component of low current rate of change is divided into an average current demand and a transient current demand through a lowpass filter. In the HESS, batteries support the average current demand while supercapacitors support the component of low current rate of change and the transient current demand. Thus, compared with the conventional one-order frequency division control, the proposed control can smoothen the charge/discharge current of batteries, improve the DC bus voltage recovery speed, and reduce the voltage overshoot. Meanwhile, it only needs DC bus voltage without other power calculation modules, which is convenient for system expansion and ease to reduce latency. A model of a DC micro-gird with HESS is built in the MATLAB/Simulink which validates the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy with the short-term and long-term studies.

articleTitle: Users' electricity consumption behaviour analysis in distribution network based on high dimensional random matrix
abstract: To deal with the abnormal behaviours of the users and the abnormal/broken smart meters on the user side of the power distribution network, a user-side fault diagnosis and analysis method for low-voltage distribution network is proposed. Based on the random matrix theory, the data analysis and modeling of the smart meters on the user side of the low-voltage distribution network are carried out. Besides, the high-dimensional data statistical index is used to characterize the user-side electricity consumption data. Based on this, a user-side fault diagnosis and analysis method for low-voltage distribution network is proposed. By analysing the mean spectral radius of random matrix, this paper also presents the specific steps for locating the abnormal nodes by electricity consumption data. Meanwhile, it is also possible to realize the feature discovery of abnormal time points. Finally, the history and real-time measurement data of a smart meter in a certain area is taken as an example to analyse the proposed method. The proposed method set the different abnormal types such as user stealing and meter damage, and the results verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: Confidence interval based distributionally robust real-time dispatch considering wind power uncertainty
abstract: A confidence interval based distributionally robust real-time dispatch (CI-DRTD) approach considering wind power uncertainty is proposed, which can strike a balance between the operational costs and risk even when the wind power probability distribution cannot be precisely estimated. Based on the imprecise probability theory, the confidence interval based ambiguity set of wind power uncertainty can be constructed. By the identification of the worst distribution, the original distributionally robust optimization problem can be reformulated as a robust economic dispatch problem. By using the algorithm developed in our previous work, the robust economic dispatch model can be reformulated as a mixed integer linear programming problem, for which off-the-shelf solvers are available. Case studies verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Leakage current suppression and common-mode resonance active damping for LCCL-filtered transformerless three-phase PV inverter
abstract: Leakage current suppression is currently a serious challenge for transformerless grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) inverters. A LCCL-filtered structure can be adopted to mitigate the leakage current, whose filter capacitors are split into two groups, and the neutral point of one group is connected to the negative DC-link. The LCCL filter can provide a low-impedance CM path to keep most leakage current trapped within the inverter rather than circulating over the ground. However, the LCCL filter still faces the CM resonance problems, which may result in overcurrent and significant losses. In this paper, the leakage-current-suppression mechanism of the LCCL-filtered inverter is explicitly revealed through the established CM equivalent circuit and the leakage-current transfer function. Then, an active damping method with a CM current closed-loop control is further proposed to damp the CM resonance, where the design of controller and the matched 3D-SVPWM scheme are fully discussed. Finally, the suppression of the leakage current and the effectiveness of the proposed active damping method are experimentally verified through a 10kW three-phase T-type three-level PV inverter.

articleTitle: Impact of the DC voltage control of grid-connected PMSG on electromechanical oscillation stability of power systems
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing capacity of grid-connected wind farms, the interaction between wind power generation systems and power systems has received more and more attention. In this paper, the influence of DC voltage control of the PMSG (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> control) on the electromechanical oscillation stability of 4-machine 2-area power system is studied from the perspective of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> control parameter stability region. Firstly, the linearized closed-loop interconnected model of the power system is established. Based on the established model, the modal analysis method is applied to calculate the DC voltage control parameter stability region of the PMSG. The results show that strong interaction between the PMSG and the system can be induced by the modal resonance which results in a large reduction of the area of the parameter stability region. Moreover, the correctness of the theoretical analysis is verified by nonlinear simulation.

articleTitle: On damping coupling of SSO/SupSO modes and oscillation suppression strategy for large scale renewable source generation connected power grids
abstract: Sub/Super-synchronous Oscillations (SSO/SupSO) are observed in power grids sometimes and their characteristics are complex. This paper launches a research on the mechanism, characteristics and suppression strategy on the SSO/SupSO in depth for a power grid integrated with a direct-drive Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (D-PMSG) via voltage source converter based HVDC (VSC-HVDC) transmission system. In detail, the characteristics of the SSO/SupSO modes are investigated, and the damping coupling phenomenon among the SSO/SupSO modes is observed and analyzed according to the eigen-value and participation factors of state matrix. It is concluded that damping coupling derives from the mismatch of controller parameters. For dealing with the SSO/SupSO caused by the mismatch of controller parameters, this paper transforms the oscillation suppression strategy into the parameter optimization issue among controllers. In consequence, a controller parameter optimization model is established in this paper, in which the maximization of the damping ratios of the SSO/SupSO modes is the objective function. In particular, the variant threshold of damping ratio is developed in the optimization process. Finally, the effectiveness of the coupling analysis and superiority of the damping control strategy are verified via both eigen-value analysis in the frequency domain and PSCAD/EMTDC simulations in the time domain.

articleTitle: An algorithm for analysing influencing factors of annual electricity consumption
abstract: Based on the sensitivity analysis method of BP artificial neural network, an algorithm is designed to analyse the influencing factors of annual electricity consumption in different periods and regions. Firstly, an artificial neural network is trained year by year through the data set of socio­economic indicators and annual electricity consumption in a region. The sensitivity of each socio-economic indicator for each neural network is calculated. The influence of each index on annual electricity consumption under different economic forms is obtained by analysing the variation of sensitivity with time. The indicators with high sensitivity are screened out and the data set is reconstructed to train a new network, by this way the simplified electricity consumption forecasting model with high accuracy can be obtained. Taking Jiangsu province as an example, it is concluded that the main factors affecting the growth of annual electricity consumption in recent years are the secondary and tertiary industry output value, the fixed assets investment, GDP and the gross industrial output value. The relative error between model calculation results and actual electricity consumption can be controlled within 5%.

articleTitle: A fault-tolerant method of the second-use batteries at an energy storage power station
abstract: Energy storage power station provides a new way to deal with the decommissioned batteries for electric vehicles. In this paper, the mathematical models of the battery pack and the grid-connected converter are built and the performance characteristics in working conditions such as the battery charging at valley electricity price, the battery discharging at peak electricity price, and the power quality improvement are researched. When abnormal voltage or impedance of the battery is detected, a fault-tolerant method is employed to bypass the defective battery and put the spare battery into use, avoiding the outage of the whole equipment. The theoretical analyses above are finally verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Coordinated start-up strategy of the converters in multi-stage DC PV power collection system with unidirectional power flow characteristic
abstract: Based on the unidirectional power flow characteristic of DC power collection system in practical engineering applications, the related issues of coordinated start-up and operation mode switching for the converters in different stages are investigated in this paper. With the assistance of start-up resistors on LVDC side, the asynchronous start-up for front-end MPPT converters are proposed along with the corresponding inter-stage coordinating strategy in order to meet the requirements of different application scenarios. Based on the proposed strategy, the coordinated start-up and operation mode switching of converters in different stages could be realized without relying on the real-time communication. The principles, logical flow and features of the proposed coordinated start-up strategy are introduced in detail. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed coordinated start-up strategy have been fully verified by the system simulation. The results of this paper could be used as a theoretical guidance in the practical application of DC PV power collection system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of μPMU based intelligent distribution network by AHP and ANP-improved entropy weight methods
abstract: To improve the comprehensiveness and reasonability of μPMU based Intelligent distribution networks' performance evaluation, this paper presents a novel evaluation method based on the analytic hierarchy process and the improved entropy weight method. Firstly, the evaluation index system is established and refined by the Spearman rank correlation method to remove the strong correlation among indices. On this basis, an evaluation system of weak vertical correlation is built by the analytic hierarchy process. For the evaluation system, an optimal weighting combination analysis is carried out, jointly by the network analysis method and the improved entropy weight method to overcome each other's drawbacks. The proposed performance evaluation strategy in this study can well reflect the vertical and horizontal correlations among indices, and achieve an effective balance between the subjective and objective weighting. The proposed evaluation strategy is finally tested on an μPMU based Intelligent distribution network.

articleTitle: Sub-synchronous torsional interaction with LCC-HVDC in DC current control timescale
abstract: High voltage direct current (HVDC) systems based on line commutated converter (LCC) is an effective technique for power transmission of integrating large-scale renewable generations. With the increasing applications of LCC-HVDC, sub-synchronous torsional interactions (SSTI) between LCC-HVDC and thermal power unit causes widespread concern. This paper presents a small-signal model of LCC-HVDC power-sending terminal based on the motion equation concept. Moreover, the interactions between LCC-HVDC and the adjacent thermal power unit shafting are analyzed based on the concept of self-stabilizing/en-stabilizing to explore the mechanism of sub-synchronous oscillations. The results show different effect of different operation points and different controller parameters of LCC-HVDC systems. Time domain simulations in the PSCAD/EMTDC verify the analytical results.

articleTitle: DC fault blocking methods in DC transmission system for remote wind farms
abstract: Wind power technology has become one of the most promising renewable power generation technology. Due to the development of wind farms in remote and offshore areas, long distance power transmission is indispensable. Modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a promising ingredient to build a high voltage direct current system or for grid interconnection. However, before the converter system is constructed, the dc side fault blocking capability must be considered. This paper first introduces three categories of methods to achieve dc side fault isolation. Then, several existing topologies with dc side fault blocking capability are evaluated in this paper. The number of semiconductor devices and the conduction voltage drop are compared in this paper. After the comparison, the topology with the lowest cost and loss is chosen to verify the dc side fault blocking capability. The simulation result validates the dc side fault blocking capability of the converter system.

articleTitle: Synchronizing signal detection for grid voltage based on sliding-mode observer
abstract: In renewable energy integration filed, the grid voltage synchronization signal should be fed back to the gird-tied converter for reliable operation. The frequency and phase information of the grid voltage, and the positive and negative sequence are also needed for the converter control. A sliding-mode grid voltage observer is proposed and verified in this paper under an unbalanced network. The fundamental positive sequence component and fundamental negative sequence component are inherently separated in the observer without employing any additional separated filters. Due to embedded filtering effect, high frequency chattering and harmonic ripples can be well suppressed. The proposed observer is simulated in the environment of MATLAB and simulation results show that the proposed observer is correct and effective.

articleTitle: Arm current balancing control strategy for modular multilevel converters under grid fault conditions
abstract: Symmetrical ac current control is generally employed in grid-connected modular multilevel converters (MMCs) under grid fault conditions. However, it can result in unbalanced arm currents and consequently asymmetrical electrical stress and thermal distributions for semiconductor devices as well as unbalanced state of charge (SOC), heating, aging and even overcharge for batteries in MMC based energy storage systems. This paper analyses the reason of the unbalanced arm currents and proposes an effective method to solve this issue. Firstly, the mathematical expressions of the arm currents are derived under different fault severities and operation conditions to show the "side-effect" of the symmetrical ac current control. Then, a zero-sequence voltage injection method is proposed. The injected voltage is directly obtained from the negative sequence ac current controller and ac current without extra controllers. The effect of the injected voltage on the modulation index of MMC is quantitative analysed. The effectiveness and performance of the proposed analysis and control method are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Short-term wind power prediction based on singular value decomposition and multi-position NWP
abstract: In order to improve the prediction accuracy of short-term wind power, a forecasting method based on multi-position NWP data is proposed. The multi-position NWP data has two problems, which are high dimension and multiple information features, so the singular value decomposition(SVD) technique is proposed to reduce dimension and filter the features at first. Then, a BP neural network model is established based on the data of SVD dimensional reduction. By predicting the power of a wind farm in China, the NMAE of the proposed model is 5.60% and the NRMSE is 7.26%. Compared with the prediction model without SVD, the NMAE decreased by 5.66% and the NRMSE decreased by 6.42%. And compared with the prediction model based on NWP of single position, the NMAE decreased by 1.70% and the NRMSE decreased by 2.29%.

articleTitle: Fuzzy modelling of power system economic dispatch incorporating load and wind generation uncertainties
abstract: It is known that the intrinsic uncertainty of load widely exists in power systems. In particular, the rapid development of renewable energy resources like wind and solar units introduce more uncertainty into the existing power grid, which further impose additional risk in optimal economic operation of power systems. In this paper, an analytical expression for fuzzy modelling of power system economic dispatch incorporating load and wind generation uncertainties is proposed. Based on the classic economic dispatch model, the possibility distributions of wind generation and load are introduced to the equality constraint. Among them, the possibility distribution of wind generation output can be derived by Dubois possibility and probability consistency principle(DPPCP), and the possibility distribution of load is described with triangular fuzzy number. By applying the Lagrange function based on extreme value theorem and the fuzzy second extension theorem, the linear or piece-wise linear functional relations between generation outputs and load can be deduced elaborately, in which the possibility distribution of the must-run and dispatchable generating units can be obtained analytically. Finally, the proposed model and method are tested on the IEEE 30-bus standard system. Some interesting and meaningful conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Design of an energy management scheme for residential demand response in a microgrid system
abstract: The fluctuating prices of fossil fuels coupled with other technical and economic limitations have compelled the utilities to use renewable energy technologies (RETs) for power generation. In view of this, the physical accessibility of solar and wind resources has encouraged the application of RETs in the microgrid (MG) systems. The feasibility assessment of a MG system is investigated in this work with the aim of promoting the photovoltaic (PV), wind turbine (WT) and battery storage system (BSS) for power generation application in a standalone MG system. The optimal configuration of a MG system is achieved with the application of an fmincon optimization function. The research work is carried out by using a typical load profile of low-medium sized residential buildings in Cape Town, South Africa. This study is designed to evaluate the technical and financial viability of a MG system. This leads to the minimization of the net present cost (NPC) and cost of energy (COE) as well as the maximization of cost of net energy purchased, benefit and benefit-cost ratio (BCR). It can be established from the outcomes of the study that green technologies are the cost-effective means of accomplishing sustainable energy goal.

articleTitle: Design of demonstration platform for PV DC-DC converter in DC distribution network
abstract: Due to less transformation links, stronger transmission capacity and less line loss, DC transmission is an important way for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) sources accommodation in distributed network. Meanwhile there are a high ratio of power electronic devices with bulk capacitor, which is prone to loses stability due to the rapid rise of current and the fast protection of equipment when the fault occurs. The power quality, power control capability and transient response of PV DC-DC Converter are not clear. Therefore, in order to truly reflect the long-term performance of DC converters, it is urgent to establish an DC network demonstration platform. In this paper, the structure for multi-scenario DC distribution network, DC circuit breaker and various power grid faults and working conditions are introduced. Meanwhile, the design of a multi-point synchronize measure and data acquisition system is given, which can record the dynamic processes of network under complex parallel operation of PV DC-DC converters.

articleTitle: An energy trading strategy considering the priority of renewable energy and electric vehicles
abstract: The large number of uncertain renewable energy (RE) and electric vehicles (EV) participate into day-ahead electricity market which makes the day-ahead energy trading difficult. Therefore, in this paper, a new energy trading optimization for multi-mode energy supply scenarios with centralized management and unified dispatch is proposed to improve the fairness, credibility, economy of energy trading. In this model, wind energy, energy storage and EV are involved as independent participator, and the total profit of system are selected as objective of model. Meanwhile, due to the clean characteristics of RE, the priority of clean energy is considered to ensure the RE can be traded specifically. Finally, the proposed model is expressed as a mixed-integer stochastic linear program and solved by CPLEX. In a case, the influence of clean energy trading priority under different scenarios is analyzed, and the effectiveness of proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Optimal coordinated generation and demand scheduling for ship hybrid energy system
abstract: For the economic and environmental consideration, improving the energy efficiency of ships is essential and worth further investigation. Most researches focused on the energy efficiency optimisation of shipboard power systems with conventional generators. However, the demand in ships is in different forms, including electric, thermal and mechanical power. Additionally, integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation is a trend. In this paper, we model the ship hybrid energy system with PV generation, electric, thermal and mechanical power demands. For a better energy utilization, we formulate a coordinated generation and demand scheduling problem with the voyage planning, which is a mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP) problem. To make the problem tractable, the non-convex and non-linear terms of the problem are transformed by exact relaxation and linearization, respectively. Thus, a mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) problem is obtained, which can be solved efficiently. At last, simulations are given to verify the proposed solution. The results are demonstrated that our solution has a further improvement of ship' energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of DFIG-based wind turbine's fault current on distance relay during symmetrical faults
abstract: Doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind turbine (WT), as a highly penetrated power source in modern power systems, has different fault current contribution from traditional power sources. It has significant impacts on distance relay's performances and may result in maloperation. In this paper, the impacts of DFIG-based WT's fault current on the performances of distance protection are studied in terms of apparent impedance trajectories and fault current expressions, for the symmetrical faults. Based on the apparent impedance trajectories and EMTP simulations, a new kind of maloperation is discovered that the zone-1 distance relay of the lines connecting to DFIG-based wind farms will overreach. And the following analysis indicates that the transient components of DFIG-based WT's fault current are the underlying reasons. With those understanding, suggestions are provided to help prevent the overreach by optimizing the setting of zone-1 distance relay.

articleTitle: Research on zero-sequence control strategy of flexible multi-state switch based on transformerless VSC-MVDC
abstract: Flexible multi-state switch (FMS) can realize the equipment compactness without the connection transformer, but it has some problems that the zero-sequence component transfers between different supply areas, which enlarges the fault influence range. By means of classical circuit analysis and sequence component decomposition calculation, this paper reveals the essential characteristics and intrinsic mechanism of zero-sequence component transferring between ac and dc systems. Based on theoretical analysis and formula deduction, two zero-sequence suppression control strategies for the voltage source converter (VSC) with and without faults are proposed. A back-to-back transformerless FMS simulation model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the two zero-sequence suppression control strategies.

articleTitle: State estimation in distribution system considering RES uncertainties with correlations
abstract: The increasing penetration of RES (renewable energy resource) and DGs (distributed generations) in the distribution grid brings more uncertainties, and aggravates the shortage of measurements for the state estimation problem. Researches have been done to incorporate pseudo-measurements of DGs to increase computational redundancy. Little consideration has been taken for the uncertainty and power correlation among DGs to increase the accuracy of the pseudo-measurements. Therefore, this paper presents a method of DG pseudo-measurement considering Pair-copula wind power correlation model and GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model) equivalent uncertainty model, which can take into account the complex correlation and uncertainty of DG power outputs, and improve the accuracy of distribution network state estimation. Results obtained based on a modified IEEE 14-bus network would be presented and analysed, to validate the capability of GMM for pseudo-measurements to consider the RES uncertainty considering power correlations in state estimation problems.

articleTitle: A multi-resolution interface model of combined shifted frequency phasor and electromagnetic transient simulations for STATCOMs and large-scale AC/DC grids
abstract: It is desirable to propose a simulation method, which can provide instantaneous and wide frequency band phasor values simultaneously, especially for STATCOMs and large-scale AC/DC grids. To doing so, the DC and the AC grids, especially STATCOMs, are decoupled for the whole system. Then, an interface model between SFP and EMT subsystems is proposed to reflect the AC and DC connections between different subsystems. Simulation results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and the multi-resolution interface model.

articleTitle: Sub-parts control parameter fitting method of VSC based on RTDS
abstract: Based on hardware-in-loop simulation and digital simulation, the paper presents a new method of parameter fitting applied to characterize physical voltage source controller(VSC). Take typical VSC grid-connected model for a instance, firstly proposing a self-adaptive observational coordinate system which drawing lessons from phase-lock-loop(PLL) and make it true that comparing the step response of two different simulation system. Then separately introduce the fitting method of PLL, current inner loop and DC voltage outer loop in VSC control system. self-adaptive observational coordinate system is used in the process of current inner loop parameter fitting. Finally, the efficiency of the method is verified by the comparative analysis of simulations.

articleTitle: A novel two-stage model predictive control for wind power smoothing based on HESS
abstract: The increasing penetration of large-scale wind power causes frequency fluctuation and voltage instability in power systems. To rise to the challenge of the security and stability operation of power grid, the hybrid energy storage system (HESS) containing batteries and super capacitors is used for smoothing wind farm output fluctuations, enabling friendly access of wind generation. This paper presents a novel two-stage Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy for HESS to co-ordinately optimize the charge and discharge power of these two kinds of storage components. It controls the HESS at two time scales. The lower frequency wind fluctuations can be smoothed in the first stage, while the higher frequency fluctuations can be smoothed at the second stage on smaller time scales.
