The proposed approach is implemented on a modified IEEE 24-bus test system and the results justify the efficiency of the proposed RO-based co-planning model.

articleTitle: Study on safe operating area of series VSC-LCC hybrid rectifier connected with weak grid
abstract: Series VSC-LCC hybrid rectifier (SVLHR) is a more promising scheme for long-distance transmission of large-scale renewable power comparing with pure LCC and VSC rectifier schemes, due to its operational flexibility and economic efficiency. Meanwhile, SVLHR synthesizes both the supporting grid voltage ability of VSC rectifier and the DC fault blocking ability of LCC rectifier, which is meaningful for high renewable power penetration sending grid. In this paper, SVLHR connecting with weak grid scenario is studied, and the control strategy of SVLHR is also proposed. Further, SVLHR operational characteristics are analysed for determining the safe power output area. Simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC with detailed switching model verified the effectiveness of proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Identification method of the high-resistance single-phase disconnection fault in distribution network based on distributed measurement
abstract: The single-phase disconnection fault is highly dangerous and severely harmful to the operation of the distribution network, so it is much significant to identify the single-phase disconnection fault accurately. On the basis of distributed measurement, the identification method of the single-phase fault of the distribution network has been studied. Firstly, we analyzed and calculated the load-side equivalent circuit of the single disconnection fault and single grounding fault, educed the voltage features of these two faults at the load side and further put forward the single-phase disconnection fault identification method based on the voltage amplitude of load-side fault phase. The results of PSCAD/EMTDC simulation show that this method can accurately identify the high-resistance single-phase disconnection fault in the distribution network and is expected to resolve the difficult identification of single­phase disconnection fault of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Exploring demand side flexibility via smart energy hub in two-stage electricity markets
abstract: Demand response (DR) is a critical and effective measure to stimulate demand side flexibility to interact with power grids. However, the conventional scope of DR with only electricity carrier cannot fully explore the interaction capability due to users' must-run loads. By integrating various forms of energy, smart energy hubs (SEHs) make it possible for more users to flexibly participate in DR programs. In this paper, we explore the flexibility of this novel vision, termed as integrated demand response (IDR). An SEH model is formulated comprised of various kinds of distributed energy resources (DERs) including plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), photovoltaic systems and gas-fired micro-turbines. With the help of the internet of things technology, an SEH can manage these DERs to bid in electricity markets without violating electric load. In the SEH, a number of vehicle-to-grid (V2G)-enabled PEVs are aggregated to act as a controllable battery storage, thereby further improving the responsive capability of IDR. A two-stage stochastic market bidding model is developed to schedule the operation of the SEH against the uncertainties in PEVs, solar power and market prices. Case studies based on real-world datasets illustrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed market bidding framework.

articleTitle: Research on index system and comprehensive evaluation method of China's electricity spot market
abstract: With the further deepening of China's electricity reform, the construction of spot market has become the key target of the main body of regional market construction. Establishing an index system that conforms to the operating rules of the spot market can effectively evaluate the operating mode and environment of the spot market, thus improving the operating efficiency of the spot market. Based on the basic principles and methods of constructing the evaluation index system, this paper first establishes a multi-dimensional evaluation index system of spot market, covering the economic and safety aspects of market operation. Secondly, in view of the proposed multi-dimensional index of spot market, the comprehensive evaluation index of spot market is obtained by comprehensive evaluation method. Finally, an example of PJM spot market in the United States is given to illustrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed multi-dimensional index system and comprehensive evaluation method can provide effective reference for guiding and improving the operation of power market.

articleTitle: Evaluation method of power system flexibility for renewable energy accommodation
abstract: High penetration of renewable energy is an important feature and trend of power system development, which brings unprecedented challenges to the operation and control of power system. This paper focuses on the optimal operation of power system, and a quantitative evaluation method of do-not-exceed (DNE) limit considering wind spillage and load curtailment is proposed. Based on day-ahead and real-time dispatching frameworks, a two-stage robust optimization model with multi-period coupling constraints is established. In the day-ahead dispatching stage, a security constrained unit commitment model is established based on wind and load forecasting data. In the real-time dispatching, the wind absorption envelope is calculated and can be described as the DNE limit problem of wind power. For any wind power output curve in the envelope, the wind spillage and load curtailment in the real-time dispatching stage can be acceptable by adjusting the day-ahead scheduling. Based on the solution framework of benders algorithm, and applying duality theory and big-M method, the intractable min-max-min model is reformulated into mixed integer linear programming (MILP). Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an example of the IEEE RTS-30 bus system.

articleTitle: A new coupled intelligent model of working fluid parameters in collector field of DSG parabolic trough
abstract: Accurate and real-time simulation for parameters of working fluid is essential for dispatching and operation in DSG Parabolic Trough. In this work, a new coupled intelligent model of working fluid parameters is proposed for DSG parabolic troughs, which has three characteristics as follows. (1) The proposed model is coupled with a mechanism model and an artificial intelligence model, which overcomes the problems of expensive computing cost in pure dynamic mechanism models, the low accuracy in pure steady-state mechanism models and the large data requirements in pure data driven models. (2) A heat-transfer and hydrodynamic coupling steady-state mechanism model is established to as a prior model, which not only obtains the prior values of the parameters including the mechanism factors, but also ensures the rapidity of calculation. (3) A four-layer neural network is proposed to improve simulation accuracy. The calculation results show that the mean absolute percentage error of the inlet pressure and the outlet temperature is 0.4784% and 2.1725%, respectively, which are better than that of pressure in the other two reference models. In future work, the structure of two neural networks will be used to improve the temperature.

articleTitle: A novel linear battery energy storage system (BESS) life loss calculation model for BESS-integrated wind farm in scheduled power tracking
abstract: Recently, rapid development of battery technology makes it feasible to integrate renewable generations with battery energy storage system (BESS). The consideration of BESS life loss for different BESS application scenarios is economic imperative. In this paper, a novel linear BESS life loss calculation model for BESS-integrated wind farm in scheduled power tracking is proposed. Firstly, based on the life cycle times-depth of discharge (DOD) relation-curve, the BESS life loss coefficient for unit throughput energy with different state of charge (SOC) can be determined from the life cycle times-DOD relation-curve fitting function directly. Secondly, as unidirectional variation of SOC in a single time step, the BESS life loss can be calculated through integration of the life loss coefficient-SOC relation function. A linear BESS life loss calculation model is established through self-optimal piecewise linearization of the primitive function of the life loss coefficient-SOC relation function. Thirdly, the proposed life loss calculation model is incorporated in the BESS-integrated wind farm scheduled power tracking optimization. Case studies demonstrate that with the proposed method, the BESS life loss item can be incorporated in the optimization model effectively, and the scheduled power tracking cost of the BESS-integrated wind farm can be determined and optimized more comprehensively.

articleTitle: A low-cost power-taking scheme for self-starting of unidirectional diode-rectified DC wind turbines with medium-voltage direct current transmission
abstract: For small-scale offshore wind farms, the medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) transmission scheme with unidirectional diode-rectified based DC wind turbines possesses better economy and reliability. However, the diode-rectified based DC wind turbine lacks self-starting ability. To solve this problem, a high-voltage DC power-taking scheme is proposed in this paper. In this method, a certain medium-frequency AC voltage, which is generated by the grid-side MMC converter control, will be injected into the DC transmission line. At the wind farm side, the medium-frequency AC voltage is captured by using RLC passive circuit, then through a transformer and a small-capacity power converter, the captured medium-frequency AC voltage can thus be supplied to the DC wind turbines to realize its start-up. The precise mathematic model of the proposed passive power-taking circuit is derived. An optimal design method for main circuit parameters is proposed to minimize the amplitude of the injected medium-frequency AC voltage. The boundary conditions of the availability of the optimal design method are then determined by sensitivity analysis. Finally, a simulation model is built in MATLAB/Simulink, and the simulation results verify the feasibility of the proposed power-taking scheme and parameter design method.

articleTitle: An intelligent implementation of improved nonlinear droop control scheme in MTDC networks using fuzzy search
abstract: Multi-terminal direct current (MTDC) networks typically operate under active power and DC voltage (P-U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>) droop control. Such control arrangement facilitates active power dispatch, and its design is greatly influenced by DC network characteristics. Therefore, the first part of this paper analyzes P-U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> droop characteristics when implemented on Grid-Side Voltage Source Converters (GSVSCs) of a MTDC network, in which the variations of DC cables' resistances with temperature are taken into account. The analysis establishes that the actual droop characteristics of GSVSCs are nonlinearity, which are contrary to the widely assumption of linear relationships. These findings of presented analysis is fundamental for the design of accurate power dispatch for the GSVSCs. Therefore, an improved droop control scheme using fuzzy search (VDCFS) for MTDC networks is proposed. The proposed improved droop control performs real-time search to capture the droop curves of the GSVSCs over full range of permissible DC voltages and active powers. The proposed droop control is implementation without the assumption of prior knowledge of the DC network parameters which are subject to variations and uncertainty, and instead the droop curves are periodically obtained and updated. The technical viability of the proposed improved droop control has been tested on a four-terminal HVDC network simulation model established in MATLAB/Simulink. Simulation results confirm the accuracy and superiority of the proposed VDCFS scheme over the traditional linear droop scheme in general, and particularly, under the scenario of DC cable resistance changes and power flow variations.

Author Keywords: IMPROVED DROOP CONTROL SCHEME UNSING FUZZY SEARCH

articleTitle: Analysis of hierarchical total supply capability for distribution network based on spark parallel computing
abstract: With the development of smart grid and data acquisition and monitoring technology, the massive data accumulated by the power company provides the data base for load forecasting. A dynamic Bayesian network is established as a load forecasting model of transformer areas in this paper, which includes the causal relationship between temperature, humidity, day type and other factors with load and Markov characteristics of load time series. In order to solve the problem of model parameter calculation based on massive data and the parallelization of lots of transformers' load forecasting, a dynamic Bayesian network with large sample data is built by using parallel computing component of Spark GraphX. Then combining Vertex cut and parallel path search to extracting probabilistic information fast. The Pregel computing model used to parallelized forward backward algorithm to realize the distributed cluster computing of the prediction method and ensure the parallelization of global prediction tasks. The experimental results show that load forecasting technology of transformer district based on distributed graph computing has high prediction accuracy and fast calculation speed and is an efficient and feasible technique for large data analysis. ce-based and the proposed admittance-based criterion.

articleTitle: A coordination strategy to smooth fluctuation of distributed renewable energy in combined heat and power community microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes a coordination strategy to smooth the tieline power fluctuation of the combined heating and power community microgrid (CHPCM) by using the controllable devices and the virtual energy storage system. The structure and energy coupling mode of the CHPCM are analyzed. The controllable devices in CHPCM include micro-gas turbines, heat pumps, batteries and super capacitors. Based on the ideal of demand response, virtual energy storage system is a thermal model utilizing the heat storage characteristics of building. Considering the controllable devices and the virtual energy storage system state index, this paper uses weighted moving average filtering algorithm to optimize the tie-line reference power. The coordination strategy designs state map table to regulate the filter time constant based on the operation state of the controllable devices. The output of controllable devices is adjusted by the correction factor calculated by the state map table. The proposed strategy is validated by the field data from Green Energy University Laboratory in China. The simulation shows the strategy realizes the coupling and coordination between power and heat, ensures the power fluctuation smoothing effect and enhance the microgrid control flexibility. Besides, the customers temperature of the CHPCM is maintained in a comfort level. The coordination strategy is able to enhance the penetration and consummation of distribution renewable energies and prolong the controllable devices' life

Author Keywords: MICROGRID COMBINED HEATING AND POWER COMMUNITY MICROGRID HEAT PUMP

articleTitle: Decentralized generation-storage-load coordination control for DC microgrid
abstract: For an islanded DC microgrid, battery storage system is usually regarded as a main power source to regulate the DC bus voltage and manage the power. However, SOC out-of-limit and overpower should be avoided during operation. In this paper, a decentralized control method is proposed to maintain the stability of the DC microgrid which contains photovoltaic (PV), battery, and controllable load. The DC bus voltage is utilized to deliver the signal of battery. And then the PV system deals with the over-charging and overpower problems by sampling the DC bus voltage. Besides, the controllable load will also help deal with the over-discharging problem of battery storage system. Furthermore, the efficiency of proposed method has been verified by simulation tests.

articleTitle: Analysis of generation rights transaction mechanism based on inter-provincial renewable energy consumption
abstract: This paper investigates the domestic and international development of the inter-provincial power generation trading market, studies the current situation of inter-provincial power generation trading in promoting clean energy consumption, and analyzes the existence of inter-provincial power generation trading mechanism in promoting clean energy consumption. The problem and propose an actionable solution to the optimization problem; finally, based on the existing inter-provincial power generation trading mechanism, give optimization suggestions.

articleTitle: A mechanism of regional reserve market for promoting large-scale renewable energy consumption
abstract: With the continuous expansion of large-scale renewable energy such as wind power in power system, cross-regional transmission and balance has become an important form of renewable energy consumption. Towards the cross-regional balance and consumption of renewable energy, a transaction mechanism and clearing model of regional reserve market are proposed, and also the market structure and clearing process are elaborated in this paper. Taking the scenario of cross-regional balance of wind power as an example, the regional reserve market proposed in this paper has been proved to realize the mutual utilization of reserve resources in each region, helping to alleviate the regulation pressure of whole regional system and improve the overall operation economy, which will ultimately promote the consumption of large-scale renewable energy.

articleTitle: An improved benchmark level evaluation method for power quality
abstract: Power quality benchmark level evaluation is the basis of power quality benchmarking management. The existing power quality benchmark level evaluation methods can not accurately and comprehensively reflect the regional power quality level. An improved power quality benchmark level evaluation method is proposed in this paper. The method uses K-means based stratified random sampling method to select sample points, aggregates the monitoring data of sample monitoring points from the monitoring point level to the system level, and evaluates the power quality level for the regional power grid represented by sample points from two aspects of steady-state index and transient index. The power quality level is evaluated to learn the power quality benchmark level of regional power grid, and then the evaluation and comparison of power quality benchmark level between different regional power grids are realized.

articleTitle: Control function research and performance test of WuJiang STATCOM project
abstract: In order to solve the problem of reactive power and voltage in southern Suzhou power grid, the Wujiang STATCOM project which is the largest capacity STATCOM has been put into operation. Based on the application of Wujiang STATCOM project and the analysis of power flow regulation demand, this paper sorts out control function requirements and the key control performance indexes of STATCOM system. Finally, through system commissioning, the control functions and performances of the STATCOM are tested, it mainly includes STATCOM basic control performance indexes such as steady-state control precision and dynamic response, voltage regulation function by comprehensive means of accessing AVC, near-zone fault blocking function, fast and strong output in transient conditions function, which are used to test control ability and operation effect of Wujiang STATCOM project, it accumulates important practice experience and data for the construction of the follow-up engineering.

articleTitle: Study on deep-peak regulation of coal-gas-hydro power system in Portugal when considering high wind penetration
abstract: In the field of renewable energy generation, Portugal is in the leading position in the world. The electricity production of wind farms accounting for one third of the total electricity demand in Portugal. At the same time, the high penetration of wind power in the country's power system brings more uncertainty to net demand, which can bring grave challenges to peak load regulation. Considering the high penetration rate of wind power in Portugal power gird, a model on configuration of peak load regulation resources and a strategy of peak load regulation are established. The model aims to minimize the prime cost of peak load regulation. It is based on the mathematical model of each kind of resource. It also reckons the difference of hydro plants' peak shaving ability in different seasons. Finally, it proves its rationality and practicability through applications on specific examples of Portugal power system. The results show that the study on this model has great importance to peak load regulation in a power system with high penetration rate of new energy resources.

articleTitle: Optimal contract electricity of wind-thermal hybrid power plant in forward market
abstract: Power producers are no longer limited to only use fossils as their primary energy. For wind-thermal hybrid power plants, their bidding strategies are very important for providing decision-making reference for power market participants. Based on the wind-thermal hybrid power plant to participate in the forward market, this paper firstly introduces the development situation of the wind-thermal hybrid power plants and its market mode in the forward market. Then, the factors that the wind-thermal hybrid power plant needs to consider when formulating the bidding strategy are analysed. According to the power generation cost of the hybrid power plant, electricity bidding strategy model is established to analyse the impact of different contract electricity quantity and different bundling ratios on the benefits of wind-thermal bundling systems. Simulation results of the monthly market show that the contract electricity bidding strategy proposed in this paper can effectively improve the efficiency of wind-thermal hybrid power plant, which would be very valuable for the hybrid power plant bidding in the forward market.

articleTitle: A convex model for shipboard grid fault reconfiguration
abstract: The network reconstruction of ship power system is one of the pivotal ways to recover from system faults. Existing fault reconfiguration strategies are usually based on the DC power flow model without considering voltage and power transmission constraints. However, some important loads on ships can only work normally within a certain voltage range. Therefore, it is necessary to research fault reconfiguration strategy considering voltage security constraints. This paper proposes a shipboard grid fault reconfiguration strategy based on the distflow model. And a second order conic programming (SOCP) method is proposed to convert the fault reconfiguration model to convex optimization model in order to obtain the global optimal solution. Based on an improved IEEE 33-bus distribution network model, simulation results show that the proposed fault reconfiguration strategy can minimize the power loss and improve the voltage quality of important loads after recovery. And the SOCP method shows good performance on global optimal solution.

articleTitle: Angle of current waveform based protection for DC distribution system
abstract: DC line protection is one of the key problems in the development of multi-terminal flexible DC distribution system. This paper proposes a pilot protection method based on included angle cosine of fault current waveform to solve the existing problems of the pilot current differential protection. The included angle cosine is calculated by using the fault current waveform at both terminals of the line to identify internal and external faults. When internal faults occur the directions of fault current waveform are opposite and the included angle cosine is negative. When external faults occur the directions of fault current waveform are same and the included angle cosine is positive. The simulation results show that the proposed protection principle can identify internal and external faults reliably. In addition, the proposed method is able to respond to faults with high resistance and is in dependent of distributed capacitive current.

articleTitle: Modified sequence domain impedance modelling of the modular multilevel converter
abstract: The accurate sequence impedance model of the modular multilevel converter (MMC) is essential for the precise stability analysis of various MMC-based interconnected systems. This paper presents a modified sequence impedance model for MMC considering off-diagonal coupling effects. Instead of simplifying the MMC as the single-phase model, the three-phase harmonic state-space model of the MMC is established based on harmonic state space theory. Then, the linear symmetric transformation is applied to transform the MMC's three-phase model into the modified sequence impedance model. The accuracy of the proposed model is validated by comparing with corresponding frequency scanning results in Matlab/Simulink. The research shows that there exist strong couplings between the positive and negative sequence of the MMC which cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: A method for multi-VSC interaction analysis based on current excitation and voltage response in current control timescale
abstract: High frequency oscillations caused by the voltage source converters (VSCs) have been increasingly emerged in the VSC-dominated power systems. However, most studies concentrate on the single VSC scenarios and lack enough cognitions of the interactions among multi-VSC. Hence, this paper will propose a method to study the interactions among multi-VSC. First, VSC will be uniformly modeled as the current excitation and the voltage response. Then, the interactions of the other VSCs on the studied VSC can be depicted and summarized as the current variations of the studied VSC induced by the voltage perturbations of the other VSCs. By converting the interactions of the other VSCs into the studied VSC, the multi-VSC system can be equivalent into the single VSC system. Hence, by studying the self-effect paths and the interacting-effect paths in the equivalent single VSC system, it is possible to study the interactions of the other VSCs on the stability of the studied VSC. Eventually, this method is illustrated in a two-VSC system and time domain simulations validate the correctness of the analyses.

articleTitle: General model and parameter tuning of doubly-fed wind turbines under asymmetric fault of power grid
abstract: In order to meet the needs of wind power grid-connected stability calculation, it is indispensable to establish an accurate electromechanical transient simulation model of wind turbines. At present, the mainstream simulation software considers positive sequence control in the electromechanical transient modeling of wind turbines, and it can well simulate the positive sequence components of active and reactive power of wind turbines under symmetrical fault. Nevertheless, under asymmetric faults, in order to achieve asymmetric fault ride throngh capability, wind turbines usually give priority to negative sequence control. If the negative sequence control is not considered in the model, the simulation of the transient response characteristics of wind turbines under asymmetric faults will be inaccurate. For doubly fed wind turbines, a general simulation model of wind turbines under positive sequence control is established, and the adaptability of the model under asymmetric fault of power grid is analyzed in the paper. Secondly, on the basis of positive sequence control model, an additional model considering the influence of negative sequence control is established. Finally, according to the actual FRT test data, the model parameters are adjusted to verify the effectiveness of the model and parameters under asymmetric faults.

articleTitle: An adjustable robust optimal dispatching method for microgrids considering uncertainty distribution of wind power
abstract: For the uncertainty caused by wind power in microgrids, this paper proposes an adjustable robust optimal dispatching method considering the wind power uncertainty distribution. The objective function of dispatching strategy is the economy of system operation. Since robust optimization has the contradiction between reliability and optimization objective, this paper proposes an uncertainty budget and penalty cost calculation method based on uncertain set robust degree. Through the combined solution of the two kinds of costs, this method realizes the coordinated optimization of robustness and economy. Based on the distribution characteristics of wind power fluctuation, this paper proposes a new wind power output uncertain set construction method. Compared with the traditional robust optimization method, the construction method can surmount the problems of wind power output discretization or excessively uncertain set construction cost in ultra-short-term dispatch. The simulation results demonstrate the economy and effectiveness of the proposed optimal dispatching method.

articleTitle: Circulating current control scheme under capacitor aging in modular multilevel converter
abstract: The capacitor is one of the weakest components in modular multilevel converter (MMC). The capacitance drops with the aging of capacitor, consequently, the capacitor should be replaced when its capacitance reaches the lapsed criteria. Before the replacement, the capacitance decline in the submodule (SM) and the capacitance difference between SMs would affect the MMC performance. Presently, the effect and protection scheme under capacitor aging has not been focused. Accordingly, this paper studies the changes of the upper and lower arm voltages, currents and the circulating current under capacitor aging based on the MMC equivalent circuit. It is found that a fundamental component in the circulating current would be caused, which increases with the rise of the difference between the upper and the lower arm equivalent capacitances. To suppress the fundamental component in the circulating current, a scheme based on three-phase vector control is proposed. A simulation conducted in PSCAD/EMTDC verifies its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Feasibility study on energy storage replacing external power supply based on sequential operating simulation method
abstract: In recent years, China's energy storage industry has shown a good development trend, especially the electrochemical energy storage performance continues to improve, and the cost continues to decline. According to the analysis and prediction of authoritative organizations, the cost of electrochemical energy storage will continue to decline rapidly in the future, and the cycle life of batteries will gradually increase. It is possible to commercialize large-scale electrochemical energy storage. Considering the constraints of energy resources and transportation conditions in Jiangsu Province, as well as the constraints of environmental capacity on the development of local power supply, regional external electricity has become an important power supply in Jiangsu Province. This paper considers the development of large-scale energy storage and substitutes for a DC transmission system and analyses its operation. Some research directions and preliminary theoretical calculation references for the possible application of large capacity energy storage in power system in the future are proposed. It provides the necessary basis for provincial power grid to promote energy production and consumption revolution in the future, and explores the feasibility of further supporting the development and application of energy storage industry.

articleTitle: General modelling method for impedance of voltage source converter
abstract: Voltage source converters (VSC) have been widely used in renewable energy generation, flexible ac/dc transmission and energy transfer devices, which result in a lot of system transient stability problems, but essential cause and the physical significance are not yet systematically analysed. Firstly the paper researches the working principle and stable mode of typical voltage source converters, when considering control strategy, circuit parameters and other influencing factors, and then, the general mathematical model of AC side and DC side impedance of voltage source converters is established with internal dynamic process based on the stationary reference frame. On this basis, all of states are studied on the influence of output impedance amplitude of VSC for the operation characteristics, the influence domain characteristics of impedance for the operation stability of converter, and the key components or parameters that affect the output impedance amplitude. In the meanwhile, the frequency-domain analysis is developed to verify the correctness of above results.

articleTitle: Reduced-order model of VSC-HVDC applied to passive network based on optimal reduction algorithm
abstract: The detailed switch-level converters are computationally expensive for the simulation of large-signal transients and hard to linearize for small-signal frequency-domain characterization. This paper proposes a novel simplified converter model in voltage source converter-based (VSC) high voltage dc (HVDC) applied to passive network by remaining its function and controlled characteristics and neglecting detailed topology of converter. It includes the main physical devices and is controlled by PI controllers. Model order reduction based on optimal reduction algorithm in s domain is adopted to the simplified model over a desired steady state point of converter. The frequency domain characteristic of the simplified model coincides with that of detailed model, then the analytical expression of state variables can be obtained. Simplified model and detailed model are built in electromagnetic transient simulation program (PSCAD\EMTDC) to show accurate matching during steady state and transient operation. A significant reduction of CPU time consumption is also achieved with the simplified model.

articleTitle: An IES comprehensive profit model based on improved PSO algorithm
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of energy utilization, optimize the allocation of energy, the integrated energy system has become the first choice This paper designs an integrated energy system(IES) based on energy hubs, considering the coupling between heat, electricity and natural gas and we establish a comprehensive profit model involving multi-agent participation including distributed energy. We consider an improved particle swarm optimization (MPSO) algorithm, adding variation and dynamically correcting particle inertia weights. Simultaneously, the compression factor method is used to ensure the convergence of the algorithm. Through the MPSO algorithm, we can get the distribution coefficient of each conversion device in the energy hub under the known load level. So that achieve the best use of energy.

articleTitle: Resilent active power and virtual inertia coordinated control for multiple distributed energy storage units
abstract: Energy storage units is widely used in renewable power systems. For multiple distributed energy storage units, active power and frequency response characteristics can be effectively improved when virtual synchronous control is adopted; However, if the virtual inertia is unevenly distributed, it is not easy to achieve good performance for the dynamic adjustment of active power and system frequency. To solve this problem, resilent active power and virtual inertia coordinated control is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the total virtual inertia for the system can be calculated and analyzed quantitatively through the resilent active power of distributed energy storages. Secondly, the virtual inertia is assigned to each distributed energy storage unit according to the predefined active power ratio, respectively. The proposed resilent active power and virtual inertia coordinated control can improve the dynamic response of the system frequency, effectively reduce the oscillation of the active power, and realize active power sharing for the distributed energy storage units. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy are verified by Matlab/Simulink simulation results under different scenarios.

articleTitle: Dynamic assessment method for reactive power of DFIG
abstract: Most wind farms do not make full use of the reactive power capability of DFIGs, and accurately evaluating the real-time reactive power capacity of DFIG is of great practical value for fully utilizing the reactive power of DFIG and optimizing the reactive power control strategy. A dynamic assessment method of DFIG's reactive power is proposed to forecast and evaluate the reactive power capacity in the near future. This method is based on the reactive power characteristics of DFIG, and introduces the active power prediction data of wind turbines. A wind farm in East China is taken as an example to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of this method. The result shows that the reactive power capacity in the future time state can be evaluated by the proposed method and the prediction error is acceptable.

articleTitle: Joint generation and energy storage systems expansion planning in interconnected power systems with high penetration of wind power
abstract: Wide use of renewable energy is one of the important development directions of power systems in the future. To avoid the renewable energy curtailment and improve the system's ability to consume renewable energy, this study establishes a joint planning model of generation and energy storage systems. By combining short-term operation problems with long-term planning issues, the fluctuation and intermittence of wind power are simulated effectively to improve the practicability of planning schemes using scenario-based stochastic optimization method. Multiple sub-regions are interconnected to achieve wind power accommodation in a wide range through tie lines. To avoid the low utilization rate of tie lines, a detailed model of a tie line operation procedure is created. The load rate, climb/downhill rate, and change in power flow direction of tie lines are considered in the model. By introducing artificial variables, the abovementioned model is transformed into a mixed integer linear programming formulation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the modified IEEE RTS system.

articleTitle: Voltage fluctuation suppression method for DC 1500V traction system based on flywheel energy storage system
abstract: With the metros in frequent starting and braking operation, obvious voltage fluctuation appears in DC 1500V traction grid. In order to suppress the voltage fluctuation of DC 1500V traction grid, flywheel energy storage system (FESS) is applied. Firstly, voltage fluctuation under different operating conditions is built in MATLAB/Simulink. Finally, FESS is used to suppress the voltage fluctuation of traction grid in view of the operation state of one metro. The simulation results show that FESS can suppress the voltage fluctuation of traction grid.

articleTitle: An improved BOOST dual-loop control for improving the MPPT efficiency in photovoltaic systems
abstract: BOOST circuit is usually used in the front-end of a two-stage transformerless grid-connected photovoltaic inverter. The control performance of the BOOST circuit will significantly affect the MPPT efficiency because its settling time and anti-disturbance performance limit the sampling interval and perturbation amplitude of the MPPT. Aiming to improve the control performance of the BOOST, an optimized dual-loop control is proposed. Firstly, according to the established average BOOST model that considers the nonlinearity of photovoltaic array, the disturbance mechanism of the voltage fluctuation in the inverter dc bus is obtained, with the output change characteristics of the photovoltaic array to the control system discussed in detail. Secondly, compared with the following performance and anti-interference performance of the existing dual-loop control, the improved dual-loop control method with active damping and differential calculation of the capacitor current is presented, which can achieve satisfactory control performance while not introduce the hardware cost. Thirdly, the influence of control delay is considered. And an improved regulator parameter design method is put forward. Finally, simulation and experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed dual-loop control and regulator design method.

articleTitle: MMC-HVDC transmission line protection based on Bergeron model and state estimation
abstract: This paper presents a novel protection scheme for MMC-HVDC transmission lines. The physical laws that the MMC-HVDC transmission line should obey is firstly described using the Bergeron model, to fully consider distributed shunt capacitance of the line. Afterwards, the proposed protection method checks the consistency between the instantaneous measurements and the model of the MMC-HVDC line under protection and trips the transmission line if any inconsistency is detected. State estimation algorithm is utilized to make full use of the redundancy of available measurements as well as minimize the influence of measurement errors. Simulation results prove that the protection algorithm can quickly and dependably trip internal faults as well as securely ignore external faults, independent of fault type, location and impedances. In addition, the protection algorithm also demonstrates robustness towards measurement errors.

articleTitle: Optimal bidding strategy for wind farms in electric spot market
abstract: In a deregulated electric power market, renewable energy such as wind power needs to compete with traditional energy such as thermal power. The uncertainty of renewable energy greatly increases the difficulty of gaming in the market. Considering the uncertainty and forecast error of wind power, this paper focuses on the benefit gaming problem between wind farms and thermal units in the spot market. Based on the two-stage spot market model, the analytical relationship between the optimal bidding strategy and the forecast error of wind farms is deduced under different gaming combinations of wind farms and thermal units. Finally, with the optimal bidding strategy for wind farms, the effectiveness of the optimal bidding strategy for wind farms is verified using actual data. The optimal bidding strategy proposed in this paper can provide a reference for wind farms to deal with the risk of benefit uncertainty caused by forecast errors in multi-party competitive market.

articleTitle: Active distribution network state estimation algorithm based on decision tree of self-identification
abstract: Under the background of active distribution network, this paper proposes a state estimation algorithm of managing analysis data to solve the problem of big data, data missing and complex analysis. This paper proposes an active distribution network state estimation algorithm based on decision tree self-identification. Setting appropriate quality weight of big data based on the check rules different from traditional single-phase currents. Data in the input state estimation model is better compatible by estimating the pre-processed data, classifying and correcting the data including voltage and current. Moreover, on the premise of lacking of distributed energy measurement devices, this paper establishes a state estimation model for distributed power, which is used to correct the default data of distributed energy and improve the quality of input data in wind power and photovoltaic. The method can be verified in the actual example. Compared with the traditional state estimation, the active distribution network state estimation algorithm based on decision tree self-identification has better estimation effect and faster iteration speed. Therefore, the proposed algorithm can be effectively applied to the current state estimation of large-scale distributed energy access.

articleTitle: Stator inter-turn fault diagnosis of induction motor based on wavelet packet decomposition and random forest
abstract: The inter-turn short-circuit fault of the stator winding is one of the most common faults in induction motor, and its early detection is of great significance for reliable operation of motor-driven systems. The inter-turn short-circuit fault of the stator winding leads to the imbalance of the three-phase load current and generate a large negative-sequence component. When a turn-to-turn short circuit fault occurs, a specific frequency component is generated in load current and the energy distribution in different frequency bands of the signal is changed. Therefore, this paper proposes to extract the ratio of negative-sequence voltage and negative-sequence current, called negative-sequence impedance, as a feature for fault diagnosis. In addition, the load current was decomposed into different frequency bands using wavelet packet decomposition techniques and the energy in different frequency bands of the signal was considered as features reflecting winding condition. A method for comprehensively utilizing these features and using the random forest classifier for fault classification is proposed. Experiments show that the proposed method can achieve higher fault diagnosis accuracy compared with the support vector machine.

articleTitle: Tie-line power transmission control for micro-grid with multi-parallel connected inverters based on Lyapunov function
abstract: A novel control strategy including two control loops based on lyapunov function is proposed, which can effectively control and precisely regulate the tie-line power between the micro-grid with multi-parallel inverters connected and the main grid. With this method, voltage and frequency at common ac bus can be accurately regulated by multi-inverter, also, precise power sharing among different inverters can be achieved even under unbalanced LC filter parameters and unknown line impedance. In addition, no internal communication among inverters are required, which increases the redundancy and saves the costs. Benefited with this method of direct control of the voltage and phase at common ac bus, the reliability and robustness of the control system can be improved. And Excellent transient performance can be achieved. Real-time simulations have been implemented to verify the feasibility and advantages of the presented control scheme in the case that the micro-grid with multi-parallel inverter is interconnected with the main grid through tie-lines.

articleTitle: Voltage segment control of wind/PV hybrid islanded DC microgrid with multiple energy storages
abstract: For power shortage and no electricity areas, building wind/pv hybrid islanded DC microgrid with multiple energy storages can reduce the power supply insufficient or imbalance caused by single energy. It can improve system performance and power supply reliability, and is advantageous to the complementary advantages and coordination control between various micro-sources. Ring topology is adopted with more flexibility and higher reliability. Then three different operation modes are proposed, that is energy storage voltage regulation mode, wind/pv power reduction mode, and load shedding mode. According to the regulation of DC voltage operating range, the voltage segment control strategy is proposed, to ensure energy storage units, power generation unit and loads are all involved in the coordinated control. They can adjust the DC voltage automatically according to their priorities. For multiple energy storage units, droop coefficient of droop control is adjusted dynamically based on load power share. In addition, control methods of converters in each voltage segment are analyzed to meet different operation requirements, such as changes of wind speed, intensity of light and loads, or energy storage reaching limit value. The control strategy can be extended to other distributed power-based DC microgrids. Finally, the proposed control is validated by simulations using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A frequency-separated strategy for the integration of different types of electric vehicles into grid frequency regulation
abstract: Electric vehicles with different types of energy sources would have different performance when participating in grid frequency regulation. Batteries and supercapacitors are two booming concepts for electric vehicle energy sources. Supercapacitors are able to provide temporary power surge and charge or discharge frequently with less cost of lifetime compared to batteries. This paper first develops the mathematic model of electric vehicle battery and supercapacitor energy sources to differentiate these two types of electric vehicles. Then, the performance of different types of electric vehicles during the frequency regulation process is studied. According to different working characteristics, a frequency-separated strategy for grid frequency regulation is proposed, where supercapacitors deal with the high-frequency signals while batteries deal with the medium-frequency signals. By applying this strategy, the advantages of these two types of electric vehicles are taken and the cost of lifetime loss becomes less.

articleTitle: Equilibrium strategy of regional integrated energy system based on Stackelberg game theory
abstract: Regional integrated energy system (RIES) gradually changed from a theoretical concept to an effective means of energy integration. Multi-energy complement can be achieved by making use of the coupling mechanism of multiple energy sources, which can significantly enhance the economic efficiency and energy utilization of plant. Firstly, overall framework of RIES is presented, and the method of energy trading between integrated energy service provider (IESP) and energy user (EU) is analysed. Secondly, game model of IESP and EU is proposed based on Stackelberg game theory. IESP decide the energy price through price competition, and EU decide the energy demand according to the energy quotation. The equilibrium strategy solution of the model is obtained by bi-level evolutionary algorithm based on quadratic approximations. Finally, with practical example, feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Study for mitigating scour around the monopile foundations of offshore wind turbines
abstract: Scour occurring around the monopile foundations of offshore wind turbines has been widely reported in recent years. It threatens the safety and reliability of those offshore wind turbines supported by monopile foundations. Currently, tons of rock/stone are poured down around the foundations as a measure for mitigating scour. However, such a method is costly and inconvenient to implement at offshore site. Moreover, the rock and stone will spread on the seabed over time. It will be very difficult to recycle them in the future. Therefore, it has become a pressing task to address this issue particularly in the light of fact that the offshore wind industry is booming across the world today and more and more wind turbines will be installed offshore and supported by monopile foundations. Motivated by this urgent requirement, the feasibility study of a new scour reduction technique, namely fishnet, is conducted in this paper by the approach of numerical analysis. From the numerical research, it is found that in contrast to existing scour mitigation method, fishnet is not only effective in reducing scour around the wind turbine monopile foundations, but is also more cost-effective and easier to deploy at site.

articleTitle: The comprehensive voltage regulation strategy considering the severity index of voltage sag with energy storage
abstract: A basic energy storage regulation strategy is proposed to enable energy storage to respond quickly to voltage abrupt changes and eliminate static voltage deviations while avoiding frequent movements of the energy storage system. Based on the real-time perception of the grid state and the proposed voltage sag severity index, an energy storage comprehensive voltage regulation strategy considering the severity index of voltage sag is proposed. It can respond quickly when the voltage fluctuation is large or the voltage sag occurs to achieve adaptive dynamic reactive power support. The simulations of slight continuous load disturbance and voltage sag under high disturbance condition are carried out on MATLAB/Simulink platform. The simulation results show that under slight continuous disturbance, the base voltage regulation strategy with energy storage can keep the voltage fluctuation within ±5%. It can reduce the number of times of the transformer variable ratio tap and reduce the capacity requirement of the reactive power compensation equipment. When the voltage fluctuation is large or the voltage sag occurs, the proposed comprehensive voltage regulation strategy can quickly respond to the voltage sag and achieve adaptive dynamic reactive power support. The above simulation results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Transient stability assessment for inverter-interfaced distributed generators by using energy function
abstract: The inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDG) are widely applied in the distribution networks. The lack of inertia brings about the transient stability problem in the distribution network. This paper establishes the equivalent control system of IIDG and the connected distribution network model for transient analysis. The power-angle curves of the IIDG are derived by the transient model. Then an energy function including potential energy and equalized kinetic energy is formulated on the basis of power-angle curves. The energy function is utilized to evaluate the transient stability of IIDGs under three phase grounding faults. A transient stability criterion is derived by the energy function. A transient stability assessment is further proposed based on the criterion. Study cases are built in PSCAD/EMTDC and the results verify the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed transient stability assessment. The transient stability assessment will promote the reliable operation of the gird-connected IIDGs.

articleTitle: Whole stability margin of phase lead filter design in repetitive control for voltage harmonic mitigation of current source inverter
abstract: The repetitive controller (RC) is proved to be effective for periodic disturbances rejection, and is applied in many industrial applications. This paper proposes an improved repetitive controller for harmonic mitigation of current source inverters (CSI). In order to prevent control performance deterioration and system instability caused by the entire system delay, this paper elaborately designed the phase lead filter must be. Based on a novel stability analysis method, the general law of the system stability with parameters is revealed. Furthermore, the whole system stability margin for can be calculated by a novel design method. Through quantificational analysis and elaborate design of the phase lead filter, the necessary and sufficient conditions can be found, and the novel method improve excellent dynamic performance and steady state of the system. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Parameters identification of synchronous condenser based on trajectory sensitivity analysis of parameters and particle swarm algorithm
abstract: UHVDC Transmission is an effective method to promote new energy consumption and resource allocation, and accurate synchronous condenser parameters are the basis for analysis, operation and control of AC/DC hybrid power systems. This paper proposes a step-by-step parameters identification strategy for the synchronous condenser, which is based on the analysis of the trajectory sensitivity of the parameters. Firstly, a six-order practical synchronous motor model considering saturation characteristic is adopted, whose d-axis and q-axis parameters are decoupled. Then, according to the trajectory sensitivity characteristics of different parameters in different disturbances, the steady parameters and transient/sub-transient parameters are identified iteratively with the particle Swarm algorithm(PSO). Finally, the proposed parameters identification strategy is applied to the ikezhao-yinan UHVDC project. The research shows that the measured data and the calculated results fit well, and the proposed identification strategy is superior to the traditional single disturbance parameters identification method.

articleTitle: Bi-level multi time-scale voltage/var optimization and control in a hybrid distribution network
abstract: The penetration of distributed generators (DGs) and microgrids (MGs) constitutes a hybrid distribution network (DN). The task of voltage/var control (VVC) in this system is challenging considering the different controlling functions of existing voltage regulators such as on-load tap changer (OLTC) and newly emerged electronically interfaced DGs and MGs. In this paper, a mix of centralised and decentralised control schemes is proposed to enable DGs and MGs to participate in the HDN's voltage regulation by coordinating MGs, DGs, OLTC and SCs in the system. The scheme includes a centralised bi-level multi time-scale voltage/var optimization (VVO) model to dispatch all the voltage/var regulators in the HDN, as well as the local control systems to face the dynamic voltage variation and to execute the setpoints calculated by the VVO model. Under the proposed VVC scheme, the system-wide voltage quality is well-secured, and the grid-tied MG ad DGs becomes not only the self-regulated systems but also the active voltage regulators. The proposed VVC scheme is validated on a modified benchmark 11 nodes distribution system.

articleTitle: Average model of MMC with full-bridge sub-modules for blocking situation
abstract: This paper proposes a fast electromagnetic simulation model based on sub-module average modelling. The model can effectively reflect the behaviour of sub-modules and ensure high precision in time domain simulation, and greatly improve the simulation speed. By changing the corresponding control strategy, the characteristics of the submodule under the blocking situation can be simulated. This provides a simulation method for further study of MMC under fault condition. The correctness and feasibility of the model are verified on the PLECS simulation platform.

articleTitle: Study on primary frequency regulation strategy of energy storage in photovoltaic power station
abstract: Large-scale integration of photovoltaic power generation will put a great deal of pressure on frequency regulation since PV do not have such inertia response features as synchronous generators do and their outputs are volatile and randomness. In order to improve photovoltaic power generation to participate in power grid frequency regulation capacity, it is necessary to introduce new supplementary means of frequency regulation and battery energy storage system (BESS) has an advantage here because of its rapid response feature. This paper firstly presents the technical requirements of energy storage participating in primary frequency regulation in China, and then puts forwards a frequency regulation technology scheme considering the state of charge of energy storage. Finally, two parallel operation models of energy storage converters are built in RTLAB real-time simulation platform to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis of low harmonic windings for high-speed permanent magnet machines
abstract: When the high-speed permanent magnet machine is operating, the power supply frequency and the core frequency can reach thousands of Hertz. The rotor loss caused by high speed and high frequency, especially the temperature rise, which poses a severe challenge to the reliable operation of high-speed machine systems. Therefore, it is necessary to weaken the interaction between the MMF harmonics and the rotor magnetic field. To this end, this paper uses multi-layer winding to optimize the MMF of the Stator to minimize the negative effects caused by the MMF harmonics. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the appropriate number of winding layers can significantly weaken the harmonics of the other orders except for the fundamental wave, reduce the torque ripple and minimize the rotor loss (especially eddy-current loss) to improve the performance of high-speed permanent magnet machine.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of cascading failure in power grid based on brittleness theory of complex system and entropy theory under geomagnetic storm conditions
abstract: Geomagnetic disturbances will induce GIC (Geomagnetically Induced Currents) in high voltage power grid. GIC can cause cascading failure in the power system, resulting in power system collapse or blackouts. Research on risk assessment of cascading failures in power grid under geomagnetic storms can provide important reference for preventing accidents caused by geomagnetic storms. In this paper, the mechanism of cascading failure in power grid under geomagnetic storms is analysed. Using the brittleness theory of complex system to analyze the propagating process of cascading failure in power grid under geomagnetic storms. A comprehensive assessment index based on entropy theory and power system load shedding is proposed to evaluate the cascading failure in power grid under geomagnetic storm conditions. Finally, the assessment process and the assessment index are validated by using the IEEE-RTS79 system. The verification results show the validity and practicability of the proposed assessment process and index. The results of risk assessment can provide reference for quantifying and preventing the risk of power grid under geomagnetic storms.

articleTitle: State-vareying inertia and time-decaying damping emulation control scheme for VSC-HVDC transmission system
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy in modern electric power systems, the lack of system inertia has become a particular concern of the transmission system operators. To solve the problem, this paper proposes a state-varying inertia H and time-decaying damping emulation (SHTD) control scheme for VSC-HVDC transmission system which aims to support system frequency stability and oscillation damping. The proposed SHTD will operate the VSC to mimic the synchronous generator based on the swing equation, and its virtual inertia constant and damping factor are determined by the system states and the duration of the disturbances. As an improvement of traditional VSC-HVDC control schemes, the proposed SHTD scheme employs the energy coming from the DC capacitors and does not affect the AC system on the other connected side. The effective of the proposed SHTD control scheme has been demonstrated through a power system model simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment, and its performance is evaluated for grid disturbances of faults and load changes.

articleTitle: Circuit theory-based method for power loss estimation in distribution systems with distributed generator
abstract: With the rapid developing of renewable energy, it has become a trend that a large number of distributed generations (DGs) integrate into distribution network. Existing distribution energy loss calculation method cannot quickly evaluate the effect of DGs on the distribution loss. To explore new method, the application of circuit theory-based loss calculation method is discussed in distribution network with DGs. Considering that DG has the ability of voltage regulation, namely it can play an important role in distribution voltage support, the grid connection nodes of DGs are equivalent to voltage source nodes, while the other load nodes are equivalent to current source nodes. Then the distribution loss are calculated in three parts: the loss caused by the voltage source alone, the loss caused by the single action of the current source, and the loss related to the both sources and network structure parameters. Loss calculation and discussion are done the 33-bus test distribution system with DGs. The applicability of the method in quickly evaluating the power loss of DG integrated distribution system is analysed and some valuable observation is also presented.

articleTitle: A novel power forecasting method for distributed PV system based on finite data
abstract: The installed capacity of distributed PV power system has been increasing rapidly in recent years. Therefore, it is urgent for power grid dispatching departments to apply distributed PV power prediction system to assist power grid operation and dispatching. Compared with centralized PV station, distributed PV station lacks operational data and weather forecast services are not purchased in general. Therefore, existing PV prediction methods are not applicable. To solve the problem of distributed PV power prediction, a distributed PV regional equivalent model based on coarsegrained data is proposed in this paper. By cluster analysis of distributed PV data in the selected region, distributed PV system is equivalent to a number of centralized PV stations. With the help of meteorological forecast data from nearby centralized PV station or weather station, a power prediction method suitable for distributed PV in the region is proposed. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified by power forecasting result and practical distributed PV power data in a certain region.

articleTitle: Comparison analysis of local stability criteria for the DC distribution power system based on impedance and admittance
abstract: DC distribution power system (DPS) develops rapidly making the stability issue more and more complicated and prominent. This paper revisits the major impedance-based criteria for DC DPS that have been developed so far. Recently, the harmonic stability problem in the multi-paralleled grid-connected inverters system is analysed based on global admittance (GM). Then, the modified Nyquist criterion is introduced to GM and the stability requirement of the system is obtained. As well know, admittance is the reciprocal of impedance so that the aforementioned impedance-based criteria could also be expressed in the form of admittance. Consequently, an admittance-based criterion for the stability assessment of DC DPS is proposed. Besides, comparison analysis is executed to identify their advantages and disadvantages. Finally, some meaningful simulation cases are presented to illustrate the main characteristics of the reviewed impedance-based and the proposed admittance-based criterion.

articleTitle: Research on the scheme of the sample synchronization scheme for optical differential protection scheme in merge unit
abstract: This paper describes the system structure of the sampled value transmit by network in smart substation. The key techniques of sampling timing of electronic transformers based on network transmission mode and sampling synchronization in stations are analyzed. Based on this, a synchronization scheme of longitudinal fiber differential protection based on network transmission sampling values is proposed. This scheme realizes the optical differential sample synchronization in the merging unit. The opposite side sampling data is re-sampled based on the calculated two-side sampling time deviation and the re-sample time stamp of this side. Finally, sample synchronization is completed in the merge unit, then the synchronous sampled value is sent to the network by IEC61850-9-2. Through theoretical analysis and simulation verification, the sampling synchronization scheme does not depend on the synchronous clock source, which has high synchronization precision, small computational complexity, easy implementation. It also has the advantages of flexible engineering application and strong compatibility, and has a wide range of practical significance.

articleTitle: Improved power flow calculation of active power distribution network with distributed generation
abstract: Power flow calculation is the basis of the research of active distribution network. Firstly, this paper establishes different type of power flow calculation model for Distributed Generation. Secondly, an improved power flow algorithm with distributed generation is proposed, and the process of the improved power flow algorithm is deduced in detail. Thirdly, combined with the implementation of the algorithm, an improved power flow calculation procedure with Distributed Generation is presented. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed algorithm is validated by the comparison of the IEEE33 node example.

articleTitle: Quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter based on switched inductor-capacitor unit and passivity based controller
abstract: A new quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter is proposed based on switched inductor-capacitor unit. The converter uses switched inductor-capacitor technology to provide a relatively high voltage gain and reduce the input current ripple. There is only one switch in the converter, which belongs to the single switch circuit. The operating principle and the operating mode of the proposed quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter are analyzed and the EL model of the proposed quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter is set up. Based on passivity based control theory, a passivity based controller of the proposed quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter is designed by damping injection method. The passivity-based controller can give the quasi-Z-source DC/DC converter good dynamic and static performance and good robustness to the change load. The simulation results show that the converter and its passivity based controller are feasible.

articleTitle: Research on control strategy of LCC-MMC hybrid HVDC system
abstract: A new hybrid HVDC system is investigated to synthetically utilize the advantages of line commutated converter based HVDC (LCC-HVDC) and modular multilevel converter based HVDC (MMC-HVDC). The rectifier of the system adopts LCC, the inverter is composed by LCC in series with the MMC unit, and the MMC unit is composed of multiple MMCs in parallel. The mathematical model of the hybrid HVDC system is deduced and the coordinated control strategy between the rectifier and the inverter is designed. In PSCAD/EMTDC simulation environment, typical transient conditions such as start-up, AC system fault, DC overhead line fault and converter fault of the hybrid HVDC system are analyzed. The simulation results show that the system has good dynamic performance under various conditions.

articleTitle: Equilibrium model of electricity market considering green certificate transaction under renewable portfolio standard
abstract: Renewable portfolio standard (RPS) plays an important role in promoting the consumption of renewable energy and tradable green certificate (TGC) which is its supporting mechanism has a great influence on the electricity market. Firstly, this study clarifies the power and TGC supply and demand relationship among subjects like renewable energy generators and grid enterprises. On this basis, an evolutionary game model is established. Then the impact of key parameters' setting, such as quota ratio, penalty amount on subjects' strategies is analysed and the change of different types of grid enterprises' strategies' over time is studied by using this model. Finally, the trends of strategies' changes are simulated by case studies to examine the effectiveness of the proposed model, so as to provide references for entities to participate in the electricity market and the TGC market.

articleTitle: Mitigation of subsynchronous oscillation in the large-scale wind energy transmission system with HVDC link based on the local gain-varying control
abstract: The interaction between large-scale wind farms and HVDC transmission system may cause the risk of subsynchronous oscillation (SSO). Studies have shown that the SSO tends to arise from small signal amplitude oscillation at the early stage. Meanwhile, the dominant SSO mode of the wind energy transmission system with HVDC link is strongly correlated to HVDC control parameters and the risk of SSO can be reduced by decreasing the gain of HVDC control. Based on the above analysis, the local gain-varying controller (LGVC) is proposed to suppress SSO, which is added in the current control loop of HVDC rectifier. LGVC's gain depends on the input representing the SSO amplitude of the system. When the input amplitude is below the threshold value, the gain is adjusted according to the input. Otherwise, it is kept unchanged to maintain original control performance. Obviously, LGVC is nonlinear, so the describing function (DF) method is used to representing its characteristics. Then, the influence of LGVC on the system stability can be determined by Nyquist stability criterion. The simulation results show that LGVC can suppress SSO with no change in the system original control performance.

articleTitle: Island partitioning method for active distribution network considering adjustable load
abstract: In order to take full advantage of the power generation capability of distributed generation (DG) to improve grid power supply reliability under fault conditions, this paper proposes an island partitioning strategy for active distribution networks. Firstly, considering the load importance, DG running characteristics and island standby, Using the priority search algorithm to search the network, aiming at maximizing the recovery of the important load power supply capability, and obtaining the initial island range. In addition, A controllable load model is established, and uses the improved bat algorithm to find the optimal value of the controllable load, further expand the island range, and increase the ability to supply power to important loads outside the island. Finally, the method proposed in this paper is verified by IEEE33 system with DG, as a result, the proposed method can effectively utilize the controllable load to expand the island range, and effectively control the operation cost of the island.

articleTitle: Regional coordination control of active distribution network based on model predictive control
abstract: The introduction of renewable energy such as photovoltaic and wind power will lead to uncertain fluctuation of feeder switching power in active distribution network (ADN). In order to solve the above problems, this paper builds ADN model based on mixed logic dynamic model (MLD), and designs a coordinated control strategy for distributed power generation, energy storage and other equipment in the region combined with model predictive control (MPC) method. This strategy ensures that the exchange power at the feeder outlet and the exchange power in each sub-area tend to the optimal target value. Then, the coupling problem among control objectives in regional coordinated control is further studied, and a distributed MPC structure with correlative variables is proposed. At the same time, the dynamic switching logic of regional control mode is introduced into the optimization objective function to simulate and verify the inter-regional cooperative control of ADN. The simulation results show that compared with traditional PI control, MPC method has more flexible and stable control effect for regional coordinated control of ADN.

articleTitle: Research on different topologies of over-voltage-ride-through testing device for PV power generation
abstract: This article provides three different topologies of over-voltage-ride-through (OVRT) testing device for testing the OVRT performance of photovoltaic (PV) inverters or PV power plants. It analyzes the components of different test devices and the principle of how to simulate the over voltage faults, does research on the advantages and shortcomings of different test equipment. This article gives recommendations plans of laboratory test and plant-on-site test.

articleTitle: Distributed equilibrium interactive strategy of integrated energy system based on demand response using dual decomposition method
abstract: Integrated energy system (IES) is an important direction of energy consumption in the future. The optimization of IES operation can improve the economic and environmental benefits. To this end, an energy transaction model composed of multiple distributed energy stations (DES) and energy users (EU) is established, and IES interactive strategy based on demand response is proposed. DES aim to maximize their benefits respectively, while EU aim to maximize their utility respectively. Firstly, the initial problem is decomposed into demand response problems of multiple subsystems by dual decomposition, and then the demand response optimization problems of each subsystem are solved in a distributed way. The main advantage of this method is that both sides of the energy transaction do not need a central controller or any third party, and their privacy is guaranteed. The effectiveness of the proposed model and interaction strategy is verified by an example.

articleTitle: Evaluating and optimizing the evenness of power system load distribution
abstract: The orderly growth of the load in distribution networks is critical to the efficient operation of the power grid. Firstly, this paper establishes the evaluation model of the maximum transmission capacity of the distribution network, which can accurately calculate the maximum load allowed by each node. Secondly, a method and index for evaluating the load balance of each node in the power grid are proposed. Then, with the objective of optimizing the load equilibrium indicators at each node, the load growth is the control variable, and a load balancing optimization model is established. The primal dual interior point method is used to solve the optimal increment of load at each node. Finally, through the IEEE-30 node test system, the rationality of the model and method is verified, which provides a theoretical basis for the load growth in the distribution network.

articleTitle: Hierarchical decomposition based distributed energy management of distribution networks
abstract: With the proliferation of distributed generators (DGs), electric vehicles (EVs) and distributed energy storage systems (DESs), the distribution system operator (DSO) is facing a great challenge in energy management. This paper proposes a layered and distributed control framework to address the optimal operation problem of distribution networks.
