We first introduce a ‘DSO-aggregator-end users’ architecture and formulate the corresponding optimization problem, where DSO communicates with aggregators and each aggregator interacts with its distributed end users, e.g., EVs and residential loads. Then, a layered and distributed algorithm based on dual decomposition is proposed, which divides the original problem into subproblems to be solved by agents in different layers. In this way, the computation and communication burden is relieved, and users' privacy is preserved. Finally, the IEEE 33-bus distribution system is utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization of capacitor bank considering the parasitic parameters of capacitors
abstract: For the applications where a single capacitor is incapable to meet the needs, different types, behaviors and specifications of capacitors can be packaged as a capacitor bank to fulfill the requirements of the systems. Even though some commercial capacitor bank products have already existed in the market, most of them are the experienced based design which uses same capacitors connected in parallel or series to fulfill the capacitance and voltage rating requirements, so that the volume, cost, reliability and other performance factors are not optimized. To the best knowledge, no quantitative design for capacitor banks is available by considering all the design phases. This paper proposes a design method for capacitor banks with multiple design constraints. Considering the multi-physics aspects, the performance factors (e.g., lifetime, efficiency, cost and volume) of the capacitors are modeled. By optimizing the capacitor bank configurations (e.g. hybrid capacitance ratio of types, and the capacitance and numbers for individual capacitor), the solutions which fulfill the requirements of applications are identified. To verify the accuracy of the proposed method, a capacitor bank for the DC link of a 5.5 kW PV inverter is optimized and demonstrated.

articleTitle: Double integral sliding surface based intelligent proportional integral control for standalone wind energy conversion system
abstract: In this paper a Double Integral Sliding Surface based Intelligent Proportional Integral controller (iPI-DISMC) is proposed for controlling the voltage & frequency (VF) of variable speed standalone Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS). Fluctuation in the wind velocity introduces variations in terminal voltage and frequency. To address the above issue iPI-DISMC is proposed and this strategy mainly includes the double integral of voltage tracking error term which leads to the elimination of steady state error and robustness against input variations. Lyapunov candidate function is used for analysing the stability of the proposed controller. Dual Second Order Generalized Integral (DSOGI) phase locked loop (PLL) is utilized for the tracking of the frequency. The effectiveness of the proposed iPI-DISMC has been validated using simulation for different wind profiles. Finally the proposed iPI-DISMC is compared with conventional PI controller to illustrate the robustness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Robust decentralized coordinated controller design considering uncertainties of wind power
abstract: The present study proposes a coordinated design methodology of multiple decentralized FACTS damping controllers, which is robust to the uncertainties of wind power. Different from most of the existing robust control approach, the design method fundamentally based on a multiple polytopic model, which could deal with multiple system uncertain operating conditions simultaneously. The coordination control is then realized by designing the FACTS controllers via controller decentralization such that system is capable to remain robust to different operating conditions. Moreover, strong damping is guaranteed based on the LMI pole placement. Numerical simulation of the test system with the proposed controller design is carried out. Effectiveness and applicability of the coordination strategy have been demonstrated through numerical simulations on a two-area four-generator test system at the end of this study.

articleTitle: Robust load frequency control and integration of electric vehicles and renewable energy in the grid
abstract: The balancing of generation and demand, known as Load Frequency Control (LFC) is a key challenge as always, and currently it requires further attention due to the intermittent Renewable Energies (RE) and new form of Loads, Electric Vehicles (EV) in the grid. An effort is put forward by proposing a model where these worrisome generation' sources and loads can be integrated in the grid, while exploring their strengths. Beside the Conventional Sources (CS), in this model EVs take part in the LFC and RE provides inertial response. The multi objective LFC problem, is synthesised as a robust mixed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> based on static output feedback control problem addressed by iterative linear matrix inequality technique. As a test case, a three-area system having EVs, REs and CSs, is simulated in Matlab/Simulink. The EVs, which pose a challenge as an extra load, would be managed to avoid the need of too much new installation of CS and would help the integration of REs like wind and solar energy in the grid

articleTitle: Distributed generations interconnection based on the clustering algorithm and graphy theory
abstract: Because the renewable energy generation has obvious characteristics of spatiotemporal distribution and intermittence, the interconnection of various distributed generations and loads becomes an effective solution to achieve the reliable energy supply. Considering the type and distance of distributed generations, a weight-based clustering algorithm is proposed in this paper to divide the large-scale distributed generation into sub-areas and to further form structured microgrids. Between microgrids, the topology structure is achieved and optimized using the minimum spanning tree algorithm on the basis of clustering centers. In this way, the layout optimization of large-scale distributed energy can be solved. Finally, the effectiveness of the above optimization scheme is verified by simulations, which can provide a novel idea for building an economical and reliable distributed energy interconnection network.

articleTitle: The method of grid disturbance test for very large capacity photovoltaic inverter based on hardware-in-loop simulation platform
abstract: With the increase of photovoltaic inverter's single machine capacity, the current power grid disturbance test platform has been unable to meet the detection requirements of very large capacity products. In this paper, a method of grid disturbance test for very large capacity photovoltaic inverter based on hardware-in-loop simulation platform is proposed. At present, very large capacity photovoltaic inverters are designed in parallel with multiple units. Firstly, the grid disturbance test data of a single unit is obtained through the grid disturbance test platform. Secondly, the control system of a single unit is connected with the HIL platform, and the unit model and test device model are established in the simulation platform according to the detailed topology structure and device parameters of a single unit. Thirdly, the model parameters in the simulation platform are adjusted to make the test data and type test data in the model consistent. Finally, in the simulation platform, the full power model of the product is established according to the actual parallel structure of the product, and various tests are carried out. The results show that the test method can accurately reflect the grid-connection performance of the product under the condition of grid disturbance.

articleTitle: Spatial-temporal characteristics analysis of frequency oscillation in renewable integrated power grids
abstract: Frequency dynamic can be a macro manifestation of power system active power imbalance. Thus, the study of frequency dynamic behavior in renewable integrated power systems is of great significance. There is inseparable correlation between space and time for the characteristics of frequency dynamic oscillation. However, existing analysis methods are typically restricted by time. Complex empirical orthogonal function (CEOF) is a modal decomposition algorithm that describes high-dimensional dynamic data using coupled spatial-temporal modes. In this paper, CEOF is adopted to analysis the frequency dataset obtained from disturbed power grids. The frequency datasets are decomposed into the forms of time and space functions. The propagation direction and speed can be described by phase of space and time functions, respectively. The distribution of disturbance energy is shown by the amplitude of both functions. These indexes are reasonable to reflect the spatial-temporal characteristics of frequency dynamic oscillation. Two test systems are used to verify the validity of CEOF. The spatial-temporal characteristics are exacted by the proposed method. Resulting analysis indicate that CEOF is generally applicable as a useful method in the analysing and understanding of frequency dynamic behavior in power grids with high proportion of renewables.

articleTitle: Stability measurement of DC distributed power system
abstract: The application of distributed grid impedance stability analysis in engineering practice is to use small disturbance and wide band signal injection to measure the amplitude frequency characteristics and phase frequency characteristics of small disturbance response of the system, and judge the stability margin of the system according to Nyquist stability theory, the device that can be used for disturbance injection and impedance stability measurement can only be applied to a small power distributed power grid below 10kW. The impedance measurement device for large power systems has not yet been reported. This paper studies an impedance measurement suitable for high power systems. Broadband disturbance injection and uses power electronic switching devices to overcome them. The problems of harmonic distortion and high frequency output are analysed, and the system working principle, topology structure and control algorithm are simulated. The simulation results prove the feasibility of the device theory.

articleTitle: Power grid frequency regulation participated by photovoltaic generation to adapt to different control modes of grid-side AGC
abstract: Large-scale grid-connection of photovoltaic (PV) generation causes the power system to face the problem of insufficient inertia and insufficient frequency modulation capability. One of the important means to solve this problem is to take part in grid frequency regulation actively. On the basis of spare certain active power, this paper puts forward the active power-frequency droop control strategy. By modifying the original control structure of the inverter, PV generation actively takes part in the grid frequency primary regulation. In order to achieve non-error adjustment of frequency, this paper further proposes a secondary frequency regulation control strategy that adapts to different grid-side AGC control modes (constant frequency control mode, constant tie line power control mode and tie line power frequency deviation control mode). The effectiveness and feasibility of the control strategies are verified based on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform.

articleTitle: Analysis of influence on branching factor of AC grid based on characteristics of grid-side inverter
abstract: With the advantage of saving resources and high utilization, DC transmission becomes the vital part of the sustainable development. However, due to the control strategies of grid-side inverter, the characteristics of branching factor will change dramatically, different from the constant value in traditional AC grid. As an essential role in setting and coordination of relay protections, the branching factor enormously influences the reliability of distance protection and other relative protections. The fault characteristics of grid-side inverter was firstly proposed and new characteristics of the branching factor based on grid-side inverter was analysed in this paper. By theoretical deduction, the results reveal that the magnitude and phase of branching factor change according to the different current inserted by the inverter with different locations of the fault. Operating characteristics of distance protection under single-phase fault and phase-to-phase fault was also analysed in this paper. Distance protection will be immovable when neglected the new characteristics of branching factor. The new characteristics of branching factor and operating characteristics of distance protection were verified by simulation in PSCAD model.

articleTitle: A real-time spinning reserve allocation method considering forecast errors and contingencies
abstract: A distributionally robust chance-constrained (DRCC) optimization model for spinning reserve allocation in real-time market is proposed in this paper. In this model, two types of uncertainties are considered 1) the forecast error of loads and renewable power generation 2) the probability of line and generator outage contingency. The objective of the model is to minimize the total cost of system operation, including the cost of procuring power generation, the cost of procuring spinning reserve, the curtailment penalties of renewable energy resources and the expected interruption cost (EIC). Under the normal scenario and contingency scenarios, generators implement an affine control policy to balance the forecast errors. Security constraints of generators and transmission lines are modelled as chance-constraints and a tractable data-driven distributionally robust second-order cone reformulation is applied to the model. The effectiveness of the proposed model is demonstrated in a PJM 5-bus system and a modified IEEE 30-bus system. The proposed spinning reserve allocation method can improve the security of the system and is more economical than deterministic methods under some conditions.

articleTitle: Research on price mechanism of electrical energy storage power station for power grid
abstract: Electrochemical energy storage has the characteristics of fast response, four-quadrant adjustment, short construction period, and it can help to improve the safety, economy and flexibility of the power system. Price mechanism is the decisive factor to promote large-scale application of energy storage power stations. The paper describes the basic application scenarios and application values of energy storage power stations in power systems, and analyzes the price design schemes of energy storage power stations, including the two-part electricity price mechanism under controlled conditions and the market-based electricity price mechanism under the market model. According to different energy storage application scenarios and roles, the paper proposes an electrochemical energy storage price mechanism that adapts to the development of China's power system. The case results show that the economic mechanism of energy storage facilities can be effectively improved by establishing a price mechanism that objectively reflects the value of energy storage.

articleTitle: Decentralized self-balancing control strategy for the optimal operation of energy storage systems in network
abstract: With the development of energy storage system (ESS) in multi-capacity levels and the popularization of electric vehicles, the economical, stable and efficient operation of distribution network has become a hotspot of research. In this paper, a decentralized self-balancing control strategy has been proposed for the optimal operation of ESS in distribution network. The control strategy of ESS is self-adapted to the condition of network in a proposed self-balancing mechanism. The corresponding models of network and ESS have been built together with the objective function with multi-optimization target including economy and efficiency. The safety and stability of system has been set as constraint condition. Modified Quasi-Newton Methods have been used to find the iterative solution of the optimal operation scheme according to the self-balancing mechanism. An example has been given in the end to verify that the proposed methods in this paper can be approved effective and has a great value to the operation of distribution network with integrated ESS, EV, renewable energy, etc.

articleTitle: Research on network topology and coordination control of multi-terminal low frequency transmission system adapted to the characteristics of new energy convergence scenes
abstract: The multi-terminal low frequency transmission system is a new type of transmission system that can be applied to new energy convergence scenarios such as offshore wind power integration. In this scenario, considering the transmission capacity, transmission distance, economy and other requirements, we studied the network topology, the voltage level and the frequency optimization methods of multi-terminal low frequency transmission systems. Then, we proposed multi-terminal low frequency transmission networking mode under the new energy convergence scene. Next, based on the characteristics of the new energy convergence scenario, we study the coordinated control strategy of the multi-terminal low-frequency transmission system, and propose the master-slave control strategy of the multi-terminal low-frequency transmission system. Finally, the simulation model was built in the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation environment, and the simulation verification was carried out to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Voltage-frequency coupled transient instability analysis of the weak grid-connected DFIG-based wind plant during LVRT
abstract: With the rapid increase of the wind plant (WP) injection, the interaction between the WP's output current and the transmission line's impedance will affect the terminal voltage as well as the phase-locked loop (PLL) output value at the same time. The new shapes of the transient instability issues of the large-scale doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind plant during low voltage ride through (LVRT) must be noted. In this paper, the transient equivalent model of WP based on grid code is established firstly. On this basis, the voltage-frequency coupled transient instability phenomenon of the DFIG-based wind turbines (WTs) during LVRT is investigated. Moreover, the major influencing factors which resulting in the instability risk were identified, including voltage dips degree, operating conditions, and the transmission distance. Finally, the simulation for the DFIG-based WT system is carried out using Matlab/Simulink, and the simulation results are presented to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Start-up strategy for modular multilevel converters with modified nearest level modulation method
abstract: A specific issue associated with modular multilevel converters (MMCs) is that the sub-module (SM) capacitors need to be pre-charged to their rated voltages. Otherwise, voltage mismatches could cause large in-rush currents at the ac- and dc-sides of an MMC. This shortcoming should be avoided for both the start-up and post-fault restart processes. However, it normally takes a long time to pre-charge the capacitors using open loop methods. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a start-up strategy for MMCs. To speed up the start-up process and eliminate in-rush currents, a modified nearest-level modulation method is presented. The presented strategy does not require extra measurements and is feasible for both half-bridge and full-bridge based MMC topologies. For completeness, the effectiveness of strategies is verified by simulations conducted in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Resilience-oriented operation scheme for AC/DC distribution network integrated with distributed energy storage system
abstract: In order to enhance the resilience of AC/DC distribution system in the case of resisting extreme events, this paper proposed a resilience operation strategy of AC/DC distribution system with coordinating distributed energy storage systems (DESS) and voltage source converter (VSC). In this strategy, DESS is used as a backup power source for the outage area to provide emergency load restoration. When a major outage occurs on AC/DC distribution system, the power flow can be transferred by proposed greedy search algorithm and coordinating DESS and VSC, The load restoration results are evaluated based on the established resilience evaluation system. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated by modified IEEE33-node test feeder, the results indicate that the proposed restoration strategy can enhance the resilience of AC/DC system in most cases.

articleTitle: Comparison of market-incentive mechanisms based on peak regulation economy of thermal power units
abstract: In order to effectively promote large-scale wind power integration, the economy of thermal power units which participate in cross-regional peak regulation market is compared under different market-incentive mechanisms. There are three different market-incentive mechanisms fixed compensation model, one-stage clearing market model and two-stage clearing market model. These three incentive mechanisms are described as different objective functions and constraint conditions. And one example of cross-regional peak regulation ancillary service market which consists of six thermal power units and one wind turbine is simulated. The results show that: the proportion of wind power connection in area with inadequate peak regulation resources can be improved by opening cross-regional peak regulation market. If combing cross-regional peak regulation market with multi-stage clearing market model, the enthusiasm of thermal power units to participate in peak regulation market will be higher.

articleTitle: Method of emergency degree evaluation of power grid frequency response
abstract: Nowadays, the problem of power system frequency stability is of great significance under large disturbances, especially in the background of the gradual formation of UHV AC and DC hybrid power grid and the large-scale access of new energy. The frequency stability situation is extremely severe. Due to the short duration of frequency decline after disturbance, if it can improve the speed of frequency response during this period, it may greatly change the transient process of frequency fluctuation, thus better ensure the stability of the system frequency and maintain the safety of the system. Because the frequency response emergency degree evaluation of power grid is based on the transient minimum frequency under the disturbance of power grid, it is necessary to obtain the transient minimum frequency quickly after the system is disturbed. In this paper, the mathematical relationship between transient minimum frequency and quasi-steady frequency in frequency response process is derived and verified. On this basis, the method of dividing emergency degree of frequency response is put forward. Finally, taking New England 39-bus system as an example, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: Optimization of active power control strategy for wind farm
abstract: The active power control performance of some wind farms can't fulfil the requirements of grid code completely, such as response time, control accuracy, control mode switching, etc. For that reason, an integrated optimal control strategy for active power of wind farm based on the dynamic grouping and priority control of wind turbines was proposed. Wind turbines in wind farm were divided into 16 subgroups based on the generator speed and the operation status of wind turbine, and the differential control strategy was adopted for different dynamic subgroups, the response time and control precision of the active power control of wind farm was significantly improved. In addition, the flexible switching of four active power control modes of wind farm was realized, including limited mode, free generation mode, frequency modulation mode and emergency control mode. Finally, the active power control strategy of a wind farm was optimized and improved, and the effectiveness of the control strategy was verified by comparative analysis of field test results.

articleTitle: High impedance fault analysis and location of single-phase-to-ground fault in feeder with multiple DGS connections
abstract: Since the single-terminal fault location in the collection line of wind farm is seriously affected by the complex wind turbine branch, the traditional fault location methods are not applicable to the wind farm anymore. According to the traditional single-terminal impedance fault location method, the zero-fault sequence network of wind farm is studied. Generally, the box transformer is delta-connected to the wind turbine, so when a single-phase-to-ground fault occurs, there is no zero-sequence fault current flowing in the wind turbine branch. Then an improved fault location algorithm for the collection line of wind farm is proposed. In this method, with the wind turbine branch current considered, the collection line of wind farm is divided into several sections, and the fault location is searched step by step after the fault. This method can effectively reduce the influence of wind turbine branch on fault location and the fault distance and the fault resistance can be calculated accurately. Based on PSCAD simulation, the proposed fault location algorithm is validated.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of grid-connected VSC based on impedance modelling
abstract: Recently, real field incidents have shown that permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind farm are prone to sub synchronous oscillation (SSO) issues when integrated into weak AC systems. The mechanism behind this subsynchronous interaction (SSI) is still unclear, and great concern has been aroused to the stability of grid-connected voltage-sourced converters (VSC) both in academia and industry. The main approaches to analysing the SSO issues include the frequency scan method, eigenvalue analysis method, time domain simulation and impedance modelling method. Depending on the domain that impedance model derived from, existing literature of impedance modelling can be classified into three categories, namely sequence domain impedance, dq domain impedance, and polar coordinates impedance. This paper focuses on the emerging impedance modelling and aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of different modelling method. Detailed derivation of these three impedance methods is presented. Through the stability analysis of VSC, the pros and cons of different methods are compared. Finally, A detailed VSC model is built in the RTDS to validate the results.

articleTitle: Multilevel comprehensive operation risk assessment of active distribution network based on PMU
abstract: With the universal penetration of distributed generations in distribution network, the safe and stable operation of power system is facing new risks. Operation risk assessment of active distribution network is an effective way to control risk. This paper proposes a multilevel comprehensive method of operation risk assessment of active distribution network. First, the threshold value for indicating the sensitivity of the risk is determined, and according to the voltage and current phasor measured by the PMU technology, the quasi-voltage overlimit node set and the quasi-overload line set under the fault event are screened. Second, calculate the risk probability, risk severity and risk value of the busbar and branch in the set separately, and use the analytic hierarchy process to form the weight. Finally, the total risk value under the fault event is obtained. The total risk value is graded and clarified on a further macroscopic level, and the risk level of each expected fault is clarified. In view of the better stability, accuracy and rapidity of PMU data sampling, this paper takes PMU as the measuring tool of active distribution network. Through case analysis, the applicability of the method. It announces a new scheme for multilevel comprehensive operation risk assessment of active distribution network, lays a new foundation for the application of PMU in active distribution network and provides a reference for grid dispatching work.

articleTitle: An on-line monitoring method of UHF partial discharge
abstract: On-line monitoring of UHF partial discharge has an effective mean for Gas insulated switchgear(GIS). However, false positives and non-response problem are seriously existed in UHF partial monitor device. Therefore, The anti-interference performance is very important. A set of intelligent monitoring and fault diagnosis system of UHF partial discharge is designed in this paper. Sensor of partial discharge should be calibrated to insure the accuracy of the system. Then the electric field wave radiated by partial discharge is obtained by the sensor, and the results can be transformed to expert system in real time by Ethernet network. By intelligently identifying the possible partial discharge in GIS, the types of partial discharge of GIS can be found timely and major accidents can be avoided effectively.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of wind turbine pitch systems based on multi-dimensional indicators
abstract: The inevitable performance degradation of components will reduce the reliability and the availability of wind turbines. Therefore, performing the performance assessment of components can optimize the operation and maintenance strategy of wind turbines and improve the management of wind farms. Pitch systems play a key role in wind turbines to collect wind energy. The blade angle is regulated by the pitch system not only to maintain the efficiency of wind energy conversion, but also to protect wind turbines from high wind speeds and emergency situations. This paper proposes a framework of performance assessment of pitch systems based on multi-dimensional indicators. First, the structure and function of pitch systems are analysed in details. Second, four performance assessment indicators: the functional performance indicator, power loss indicator, heat dissipation indicator and reliability indicator are presented to assess the degradation trend of pitch systems. Third, the proposed methodology is validated on a dataset collected from a real wind farm in China. The results show that the proposed method is effective in implementing the performance assessment of pitch systems.

articleTitle: An improved hybrid modulation strategy for cascaded H-bridge photovoltaic inverters
abstract: As a new pollution-free energy generation form, photo voltaic(PV) power generation has been vigorously promoted to decrease the pollution caused by thermal power. The traditional centralized and cluster PV system cannot achieve maximum power point tracking and status monitoring in each solar panel, while the cascade H-bridge(CHB) one can tackle the problem. However, traditional modulation strategies require high-speed fiber-optic communication between the master controller and each H-bridge module to ensure dynamic response of the system. Since the H-bridge modules are far away from each other due to the large size and wide distribution area of photovoltaic panels, the costs caused by fiber-optic communication may be considerable. In this paper, an improved hybrid modulation strategy is proposed to balance the dynamic response of the system with low costs. Only a few high-frequency(HF) modules are reserved to ensure the dynamic response of the system. Remaining low-frequency(LF) ones can use ordinary cables for communication to reduce switching losses and communication costs. The validity of the proposed method is confirmed by simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Correlation analysis between load and output of renewable energy generation based on time-varying Copula theory
abstract: Typical renewable energy sources such as wind and solar energy have significant time-varying and spatial correlations. Large number of wind power and photovoltaic power grid-connecting will bring challenges to the safe operation of the distribution network. In order to describe this correlation more accurately, we need to establish a model for the correlation between load and output of renewable energy generation. This paper uses kernel density estimation to model the source charge, using kernel density theory and Copula theory to analyze the static correlation between source output and load. And then add in time variables by using time-varying Copula functions to characterize the timespace correlation, and test the model to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: Wind turbine mechanical load estimation based on adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system
abstract: Estimating accumulated mechanical load of operating wind turbines (WT) is important to the operation security and lowering operation and maintenance (O&M) costs. This paper aims to estimate the mechanical load of a WT using data from its Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. Firstly, input parameters are determined by calculating the correlation coefficients between SCADA data and mechanical loads of the WT. Moreover, the Adaptive Network-based Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) is applied to establish the relationship between input parameters and mechanical loads. In order to prove the validity of proposed method, SCADA data and load measurements on seven crucial locations of a 2.5MW WT are collected to compare estimated and measured loads. Results show that the estimated loads are in good agreement with measurements. The coefficients of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) on different locations of the WT is between 88% and 97%. Using the proposed method, the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> increases nearly 2%. This method can be used to optimise and lower the cost of operation & maintenance (O&M), for example by prioritising inspections and replacements.

articleTitle: Optimized eight vector space based converter fault tolerance control for PMSG wind turbine
abstract: Power converter is the critical assembly of a direct-drive wind power generation system. The faults of converter switches will cause unscheduled downtime of WTs. In this paper, an eight vector space based fault tolerance control method for faulty WT converters is investigated, base on which an optimized control method is proposed. The simulation shows that this method effectively achieves fault-tolerant compensation for the open-circuit fault of the converters. Finally, the experimental result verified the effectiveness of the method. The realization of fault tolerance control for WT converter is useful for optimizing large scale offshore wind turbines O&M strategy.

articleTitle: The operating environment substitution-based field test technology of UHVDC protection system: Part 1 test scheme and hardware environmrnt substitution
abstract: At present, there is no effective test technology or device can be used to test the functions and performance of the UHVDC protection system on site. In order to fill this gap, the operating environment substitution-based field test scheme is proposed in the paper. For the proposed field test scheme, the field test device of the UHVDC protection system has various hardware ports, such as AC analogy sampling value output ports, switching value output/input ports, digital sampling value output ports, control bus signal output/input ports and DC voltage output ports, to equivalently replace the external interface devices of the UHVDC protection system. Besides, the realization of synchronous output of multi-source data and output of multi-protocol digital signals are introduced, which can make those hardware ports of the field test device behave like the external interface devices of the UHVDC protection system, i.e. lively substitute the hardware environment of the tested UHVDC protection system.

articleTitle: Study on fault process division of wind turbine electrical model validation
abstract: Accurate electrical models of wind turbines are the basis of fault characteristic simulation of wind farm. Model validation is used to ensure the accuracy of wind turbine model, and fault process division is the key point to model validation. Based on the study of domestic and abroad model validation standards, the measurement data of wind turbine fault ride through was analysed firstly, then the principle of division of transient and steady state in the whole fault ride through process of wind turbine was proposed. Finally, a model validation software was developed and the consistency of fault ride through characteristics between the model and the actual wind turbine was verified. The research results provide a technical method for wind turbine model validation and parameters identification of simulation model.

articleTitle: Amplitude-phase admittance modelling and analysis for a grid-connected converter system
abstract: This paper proposes an amplitude-phase admittance models of grid-connected converters system in polar frame. The proposed admittance matrix in admittance model have a special symmetrical structure — namely, off-diagonal elements are the opposite of each other. By matrix transformation, a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) closed-loop system of grid-connected VSC system can be equivalent to a single-input single-output (SISO) system model. The stability of the grid-connected converters system and influence of phase-locked loop (PLL) parameters are analyzed by employing the Nyquist criterion and gain margin. Moreover, the gain margin of the SISO system model represents the output current limit of the VSC for stable operation. The model and analysis are validated against simulations.

articleTitle: A novel frequency regulation control strategy based on the external characteristics of PV generation
abstract: Large-scale grid-connected PV generation results in the power system facing with the problem of reduced inertia and inadequate frequency regulation capability, which is urgent for PV generation to take participate in frequency regulation. In this paper, the research object is the double-stage PV generation, a novel frequency regulation control strategy based on the external characteristics of PV generation is proposed. f-U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</inf> compensation is introduced into DC low-voltage control loop, which makes the DC low-voltage vary with the grid frequency, thus controlling the output power of PV generation. The influence mechanism of the control strategy on the frequency dynamic process of power system is also analysed based on the frequency response model (SFR). The results show that: the larger the ΔU<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</inf> generated by the f-U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PV</inf> compensation unit, the more power of PV generation can be generated; the control strategy essentially affects the damping coefficient of the system, which not only affects the transient process of the system frequency, but also the steady-state frequency deviation.

articleTitle: Application of improved SVM algorithm and variational mode decomposition in power quality disturbances recognition
abstract: As the penetration rate of distributed generation (DG) to the power grid increases, the impact of DGs on the power quality problems of modern power systems cannot be ignored. In order to accurately recognize the power quality (PQ) problems induced by DGs and other disturbance sources, a novel power quality disturbances recognition method is proposed, based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) and support vector machine optimized by simulated annealing (SA-SVM). The VMD is adopted to extract the features from the power quality disturbance signals that are decomposed into different modes, which can better assist in differentiating useful information from various raw signals. The SA-SVM classifier is then utilized to recognize the single or composite power quality disturbances. Numerical results indicate that the proposed method can effectively recognize all the 10 typical power quality disturbances, including both single and mixed disturbances, and has satisfying recognition accuracy under both noiseless and noisy circumstances compared with the conventional algorithms such as pure SVM and decision tree. The proposed method can provide helpful assistance for the potential power quality improvement measures of the power system with a large number of DGs in the future.

articleTitle: Coordinated reactive-load compensation method for distributed network
abstract: With the increasing demands for environmental protection and rapid development of power electronic, inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDG) have gradually been built and put into use. However, due to the uncertainty and limited capacity of IIDG, only depending on IIDG cannot satisfy the requirement of reactive-load compensation and external equipment should be installed. As commonly used reactive-load compensation devices, thyristor switched capacitor (TSC) and static var generator (SVG) are overwhelmingly applied to achieve dynamic reactive-load compensation. It is essential to study the coordination between IIDG and reactive-load compensation devices. Therefore, a three-layer coordinated control strategy of reactive-load compensation based on SVG-TSC combination is proposed in this paper, constituting coordination layer, control layer and execution layer. By analyzing the grid parameters, the amount of reactive-load compensation is calculated and separately allocated to SVG, TSC and IIDG when a grid fault occurs. Meanwhile, the sequence of reactive-load compensation devices is also determined by the control strategy. The control strategy is simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC. The results reveals that the proposed control strategy can provide sufficient reactive-load compensation, increase the voltage of PCC and strengthen the low voltage ride though (LVRT) capability of the system.

articleTitle: Research on control scheme of single phase high efficiency bridgeless PFC based on GaN
abstract: The topology of single phase bridgeless Power Factor Correction (PFC) Based on GaN can effectively improve the circuit efficiency, which is a good prospect for the development of PFC power conversion circuit. Taking advantage of the circuit working in the continuous mode, the paper proposes the instantaneous current inner loop control strategy based on synchronous rotation transformation, and designs the single phase locked loop (PPL) to realize the track of voltage real phase. Both of the two technologies are inseparable from the acquisition of orthogonal signals, so the generalized second-order integral is used. In the paper, the system performances are verified by the computer simulations. According to the experimental results, the applications of the GaN device and the current control strategy based on synchronous rotation transformation not only realize the high power factor, but also reduce the harmonic interference to the power grid and reduce the circuit loss.

articleTitle: A method for mitigating subsynchronous oscillation risk based on a novel control strategy of VSC
abstract: The penetration of the grid-connected voltage source converter (GCVSC) based renewable power generation in power system is increasing, and the sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) caused by it is also increasing. This new oscillation phenomenon caused by the power electronic equipment is seriously threatening the safe and stable operation of power system. Due to the huge numbers of power electronic equipment, in order to suppress this kind of oscillation, changing the control strategy of the STATCOM which is stalled in renewable power generation plants is an effective method to restrain the SSO. This paper firstly describes the fundamental reason of the SSO is that the terminal voltage of the GCVSC is greatly affected by the converter voltage. Based on it, a damping control strategy based on STATCOM is proposed to weaken the influence of the converter voltage on the terminal voltage. This method has simple control structure and is not limited to specific oscillation frequency. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is verified by time domain simulation.

articleTitle: Agent-based simulation for electric vehicle aggregators' bidding and pricing strategy considering reserve provision
abstract: The emergence of electric vehicle aggregators (EVAs) could significantly improve the interaction between power grid and massive electric vehicles. In this paper, the market behaviour of EVA is studied, and an agent-based simulation model is proposed for EVAs' bidding and pricing strategy considering reserve provision. The EVA optimizes its bidding prices, charging prices and incentive prices with the objective to maximize total profits gained from charging service and reserve service. The EV agents will adjust their charging schedules in response to the time-of-use charging prices in order to decrease their charging cost. Based on the energy-reserve combined market clearing model, the interaction between EVA and EV owners are modelled as a Stackelberg game and simulated using agent-based approach. The numerical analysis proves the feasibility and effectiveness of model proposed.

articleTitle: Research of droop control based on nonlinear disturbance observer for energy storage
abstract: DC microgrid with energy storage and power electronic transformer (PET) facilitates the integration of large-scale renewable energy resources. In this paper, an improved control method is proposed for energy storage to achieve a switching from PET connected operation to islanding operation with a sudden disconnection of the PET. By introducing the nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) to droop control for energy storage, no additional current sensors are required to measure the disturbance current when a disturbance occurs in the system. Moreover, a feedforward control is embedded in the droop control for the energy storage unit, which uses the disturbance current estimated by the NDO and enables the energy storage unit to track the disturbance quickly. By using the proposed control method, the transient fluctuations of dc-bus voltage are suppressed and the voltage recovery time is reduced. A DC microgrid model including a PET, a photovoltaic array, an energy storage unit, and DC loads is established. The simulation results have verified the performance of the proposed control method during various operations.

articleTitle: Multi-objective planning of distributed generations based on time-sequence characteristics
abstract: With global energy depletion, a large number of distributed generations (DGs) are connected to the distribution grid. In order to ensure efficient, stable and safe operation of the distribution network, it is necessary to carry out scientific and rational planning of DGs. Based on the time-sequence characteristics of DGs and loads, we propose a multi-objective planning model of DGs with economic, technical and security into consideration. We choose the number of photovoltaic cells (PVs) and wind turbines generators (WGs) connected to each node as two random variables, and use the multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) and fuzzy membership function to solve the model. Finally, an example with IEEE-33 node is used to verify the feasibility and validity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Wind turbine failure detection based on SCADA data and data mining method
abstract: WTFD (Wind Turbine Failure Detection) system is important for improving wind turbine reliability and reducing operation & maintenance cost. A WTFD method using only SCADA data and data mining algorithm is proposed. Firstly, select representative variables from a wide variety of SCADA variables using ARD (Automatic Relevance Determination) method. Then, the denoising autoencoders (DAE) model using the selected variables with sliding window is developed to capture nonlinear correlations among multiple variables and autocorrelation of each variable. Finally, using the Mahalanobs distance (MD) of reconstruction error to make the WTFD. Real world dataset is used to validate the efficiency of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can provide advanced failure alarm for wind turbines many hours before failure happens. The results of our proposed WTFD method can reduce operation & maintenance cost and improve wind turbine reliability.

articleTitle: Current decoupling control under asymmetrical open-circuit faults of dual three-phase PMSG
abstract: Wind power plays an increasingly important role in the field of new energy. Dual three-phase permanent magnetic synchronous generator (PMSG), as a kind of multi-phase wind generator, has great fault-tolerant performance, as well as the large power density and capability of being large-scale. In this paper, a control strategy under one or two-phase open-circuit fault of the dual three-phase PMSG is proposed. To solve the problems caused by asymmetry of the PMSG under faults, an asymmetrical decoupling method is applied, which is able to transfer the time-varying characteristics into stable outputs in the d-q coordinate. To compensate for the negative effect of stator resistance and leakage inductance, the structure of current loops is rebuilt for the more complete decoupling of the system and more flexible control. Besides, subspace for harmonics suppression is also established and acquires apparent improvement. Simulation and experiment results are displayed to verify that, with the fault-tolerant control strategy, the PMSG is able to maintain the safe operation of the PMSG and obtain stable power generation.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of power system with photovoltaic generation based on multilevel cross entropy method
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic (PV) generation, the uncertainty of PV generation brings great challenge to the reliability evaluation of power system. Considering the inaccuracy of PV generation model based on parameter estimation method, non-parametric kernel density estimation (NKE) technique is used to model PV generation and then PV output samples are simulated through selective sampling. Moreover, as to the low efficiency of stochastic simulation of power system including PV generation, the multilevel cross entropy (MCE) method is used to simulate the states of power system including PV generation. Case studies have been researched on IEEE RTS79 system with PV stations and results of case studies verify the accuracy of the modelling method based on NKE technique and high efficiency of MCE method, which provides a reference for the planning and construction of PV stations in future.
